Diagnosed (docs/RESEARCH_QUESTION_OPTIONS.md) as an artifact of the marginal-occupancy construct, not a discovery about football.
claims.unit: separation index at n=6
claims.method: cross-match Wasserstein style distance, style_fingerprint_v1/v2/v3
caveats: The n=6 value rests partly on one inverted (mislabelled) leg, per the 2026-07-23 team-mapping correction; the correlation-decay DIRECTION still stands

claims.statement: Lucey-style entropy-map team-identification is NOT viable on this corpus: 7-class leave-one-out accuracy 0.208 (below the permutation null mean of 0.256); only 1 of 90 declared parameter settings clears p<0.05 (4.5 expected by chance, family-wise p=0.86). No signal to report.
claims.unit: 7-class LOO accuracy
claims.method: leave-one-out 1-NN over entropy maps at 90 declared parameter settings, permutation nulls per test

claims.statement: The entropy-map failure is NOT a camera field-of-view problem (a calibrated broadcast-camera censor costs only 0.005 bits on Metrica full-pitch truth); it IS a frame-level tracking-continuity problem: 47.4% of 1Hz ball samples carry no calibration-trusted player row at that frame at all, collapsing possession-string length from Metrica's 8s median to our 3s median.
claims.unit: pct 1Hz samples with no trusted player row
claims.method: Metrica full-pitch truth run through the identical camera-censored pipeline as our real data (a degradation control)
caveats: Fix has a stated acceptance criterion: median possession string >= 8s, a continuity/calibration engineering target

claims.statement: Under a strict 5-second-continuous window, per-match transition/counterpress metrics FAIL: at N>=5 pressing-team players visible throughout, pooled 71 usable windows over 12 matches, median 5/match (below the 10/match floor); at N>=7, 21 pooled, median 1/match.
claims.method: pre-declared threshold census (>=30/match viable, 10-30 pooled-only, <10 dead) on the shipped possession-state-change detector
caveats: Binding constraint is geometry (only ~11 players tracked, split across two teams), not the ball

claims.statement: Retracted for the correct window: the Bauer & Anzer counterpress construct only needs the ball tracked and pressers visible at 3 discrete instants inside a 2-second window (not 26 continuous slots over 5s). At the corrected 2s window, N>=3 and N>=5 PASS (median 67/match and 34/match respectively, both >=30); only N>=7 stays marginal.
claims.unit: median usable windows/match at N>=3
claims.method: re-census using the literature's actual instant-sampled requirement instead of an invented continuous-window requirement
caveats: The success (regain-within-5s) label is right-censored in 49% of even the N>=3-usable turnovers, and the censoring is INFORMATIVE (a naive rate among decided cases would read ~2.5x the true rate)

claims.statement: Counterpress-success censoring is informative, not random: among the 653 decided turnovers, 88.4% are regains, against the literature's true regain-within-5s rate of 30.2-36.2% -- the event that breaks the ball track is exactly the event that implies no regain, so the decided-cases subset over-represents successes ~2.5x.
claims.unit: pct regains among decided cases
claims.method: comparison against Bauer & Anzer's published 5s regain rate on a labelled 97-match corpus
caveats: The label needs a survival estimator with a stated, non-random censoring mechanism, not a naive rate

claims.statement: Team-level counterpress-rate metrics (%CP, CP+/T, %CP+) need 58-90 matches to separate two teams even with perfect tracking and zero measurement error -- our 12-match corpus is 5-8x too small before broadcast censoring is even considered; this is a sample-size bound, not a broadcast-quality bound.
claims.unit: matches needed (lower bound of range)
evidence: results/MANUTD_IDENTITY_PROFILE.md#What this profile cannot tell you
claims.method: irreducible binomial/Poisson noise floor derived from Bauer & Anzer's own published between-team and season variance tables
caveats: By contrast turnovers-per-match (T/M) is broadcast-bound, not sample-bound: our own corpus shows its between-team component truncated to 0.00 (F<1, p=0.54), consistent with a 30% per-match calibration CV against a 4% between-team CV

claims.statement: RQ-D survives the Choi/Theiner scoop check, narrowed to: under measured (not simulated) broadcast visibility, which PRESSING and TRANSITION metrics retain enough resolution to distinguish one team from another, and does calibrated off-screen imputation move that threshold. The word doing the work is "calibrated"; the metric family doing the work is pressing/transition.
claims.method: adversarial paper read of the two closest incumbent works

claims.statement: The two-week de-risking check for RQ-D (turnover-window census + PPDA numerator check + a one-metric end-to-end dry run) came back PASS/MARGINAL, not FAIL: the transition family reopens under the corrected 2s window, and the study design is answerable with instruments already on disk (no new CV work, no new data needed).
claims.method: W1-A/W1-B/W1B census, pre-committed pass/marginal/fail thresholds
caveats: Counterpress RATE metrics remain sample-size-dead at n=12 (w1-004); the battery must be scoped to instantaneous/local features and structure metrics, not team-level rate comparisons

claims.statement: Claims audit (2026-07-21): 41 prior claims VERIFIED by a single-verifier pass (not panel-confirmed, quota-interrupted); 5 CONTRADICTED claims found and corrected (2 already fixed, 3 confirmed contradicted by this pass), 1 amended.
claims.unit: verified count
claims.method: adversarial re-derivation of headline numbers from raw artifacts, not from the documents that assert them
caveats: A single-verifier VERIFIED should be read as "no defect found by one pass", not "panel-confirmed" -- re-derive before quoting in a review

claims.statement: STATUS.md transcribed the BAS pass-count ratios for southampton_manutd and tottenham_manutd swapped (southampton is 0.996, not 1.047; tottenham is 1.047, not 0.996); results/bas_validation.md was always correct. Fixed in STATUS, annotated.
claims.method: cross-check against outputs/oracle/sofascore
caveats: Aggregate stats (mean |dev| 2.9%, 5/6 within 5%) unaffected

claims.statement: Repo storage audit (pre-fsck): 136.4 GB total, of which video is 82% (111.4 GB) not the ~90 GB-non-video the user believed; every Man Utd match is stored TWICE (51.2 GB root .mp4 duplicated byte-for-byte in matches/<id>/ chunks via lossless stream-copy).

evidence: results/STORAGE_AUDIT_2026-07-24.md#5.1 Every ManU match is stored TWICE
claims.method: read-only Get-ChildItem + git count-objects audit, no deletions performed by the audit itself

evidence: results/DELETION_VERIFICATION_2026-07-24.md#5. matches/fra_sen -- the audit's ... call is WRONG

claims.statement: Scouting-pack demo design: the Brighton pair (opponent manager stable across both legs) is the primary demo; the Southampton pair (opponent changed its OWN manager between legs, has zero identity, and its gate tier sits at ABSTAIN) is deliberately re-cast as the honest stress/negative case, not a second success story.
claims.method: pre-registered plan, dated 2026-07-26
caveats: Promoted back to a full demo only if S2 identity work lands >=6 Southampton players named at >=0.75 confidence AND the gate tier lifts off abstain

claims.statement: Scouting-pack review found the pre-match cut-off protocol was declared but NOT mechanically enforced in code: the identity layer's oracle is the actual match team sheet, and season style factors (FBref PCA coordinates) are full-season 2024-25 aggregates including matches played AFTER the fixture being forecast -- a leak that would be the finding a December examiner lands on hardest.
claims.method: code-path audit of FORECAST_V0's protocol claims against the actual repo
caveats: Fix specified: a mechanical as-of-date filter enforced in code, not a verbal claim, before any pack is generated

claims.statement: The scouting pack excludes absolute defensive line heights in metres (comparative shares only), set pieces (corner counts only exist), any shot/xG claim as ours (no CV shot detector exists; FIFA benchmark finds broadcast save detection at F1 0.00 in every configuration), per-player pass networks, goalscorer identification, and any positional assertion about a named player at a named moment.
evidence: docs/SCOUTING_PACK_PLAN.md#3. WHAT MUST NOT GO IN IT
claims.method: pre-registered exclusion list, cross-referenced against measured coverage ceilings for each family

claims.statement: Bauer & Anzer (2021) define the counterpressing detector's feature window as 2 seconds after the ball loss (BPC + {0,1,2}s), not 5 seconds; the 5s window in their paper appears ONLY in the success LABEL (was the ball regained), and 20s only in the outcome label (shot/goal) -- the detector itself never needs 5s of continuous observation. This directly corrected our own W1 census's mistaken 5s-continuous requirement.
claims.unit: seconds
claims.method: full-text read of Bauer & Anzer, Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery 35:2009-2049, Sect 2.2.2 p.2016

claims.statement: The naive "defender within 5 yards of the ball carrier" (StatsBomb-style radius) counterpressing rule scores AUC 0.602 and precision 0.31 against Bauer & Anzer's human-labelled ground truth -- barely above chance, and it labels 72.41% of ALL turnovers as counterpressing. Any battery implementing a bare radius rule as "counterpressing" is implementing a near-chance detector.
claims.unit: AUC
claims.method: quoted from Bauer & Anzer Table 3, row 5

claims.statement: Corpus design is a repeat-measurement study: 12 Man Utd matches = 6 same-opponent home/away pairs straddling the ten Hag -> Amorim managerial change, forming a balanced 2x2 (venue x manager) at n=3 opponents/cell -- estimable direction-only for the pooled manager and venue main effects, not the interaction or any single pair's decomposition.
claims.method: design analysis of the corpus's venue x manager balance

claims.statement: Results are opponent-determined, not venue- or manager-determined: 4/6 pairs share the exact result across both legs (beat Fulham and Southampton twice, lost to Brighton and Tottenham twice); no pair flips win<->loss.
claims.method: pair-by-pair result comparison, corrected team mapping

claims.statement: Venue has a near-null pooled effect on Man Utd's shape and possession: home block 27.6 m / possession 53.2% vs away 28.9 m / 52.9% -- essentially flat; the opponent, not venue, sets the observed territory pattern.
claims.method: pooled venue main-effect estimate (manager-balanced), corrected team mapping

claims.statement: RETRACTED assumption: that B4 v1's Metrica-calibrated 50%/90% predictive regions (b4-003) generalise to real broadcast footage. This was asserted in prose and printed on every frame of the tactical-clip demo (`tools/tactical_clip.py`) without ever being independently checked against broadcast ground truth.
claims.method: the claim was never a measured result -- it was an unverified extrapolation from the Metrica gate-2 pass (b4-003)
caveats: The Metrica-only calibration claim (b4-003) is NOT retracted and remains true; only its extension to broadcast is wrong

claims.statement: On real broadcast footage the frozen B4 v1 (P2 policy) predictive regions cover 21.2% where they promise 50% and 55.4% where they promise 90%, pooled over 4900 liveness-guarded re-appearances across 4 matches (tottenham_manutd 20.5/55.3 n=1259; manutd_liverpool 21.9/57.8 n=791; manutd_brighton 21.6/56.3 n=2033; liverpool_manutd 20.7/51.4 n=817); 14 of 14 testable buckets fail at both levels.
claims.unit: pct PICP50 (pooled; PICP90 55.4)
claims.method: liveness-guarded within-track re-appearance test (>=4 gated players alive on every gap frame), frozen P2 emit policy, no re-conformalisation, replicated on 4 independent matches
caveats: Spread across matches is tight: 1.4 points at 50%, 6.4 points at 90% -- not a fixture artefact
10-30s bucket carries 5 events across 4 matches, 30s+ carries none (see b4-018)

claims.statement: The pooled observation-noise floor on our own projected broadcast positions (sigma = 0.541 m/axis, 0.765 m radial, n=240611 midpoint triples) is necessary but insufficient to explain the calibration failure: widening the frozen regions in quadrature by it recovers the 50% level (55.0%) but leaves the 90% level 20 points short (70.4%); sigma varies 2.2x across matches (0.278-0.614 m) while coverage does not track it.
claims.unit: m/axis sigma
claims.method: midpoint-triple deviation (cancels constant-velocity motion) on consecutive-sighting triples, pooled across 4 matches
caveats: manutd_liverpool has half the noise of manutd_brighton (0.278 vs 0.614 m) yet near-identical coverage -- noise level does not predict coverage

claims.statement: Selection bias is real (re-appearing players displace 2-3x less than a Metrica occlusion at the same horizon, because ByteTrack only re-associates a track that came back near where it left) but does NOT explain the calibration failure: on the displacement-matched Metrica subset (same short movements) the frozen regions still cover 52-59% / 92-95%, while our comparably-easy broadcast events cover only 17-41% / 51-87%.
claims.method: displacement-matched comparison against the Metrica holdout re-scored on only same-displacement samples, per match
caveats: This also means the RMSE tie with hold-last in the accuracy tables is a property of the biased test sample, not a measured property of the point model

claims.statement: Method limit: ByteTrack's association buffer caps liveness-guarded within-track occlusion gaps at ~10.8 s, so occlusions beyond 10 s are UNTESTABLE on this footage; the 10-30s bucket carries 5 events across 4 matches and 30s+ carries none -- exactly the horizons where B4 v1's entire published Metrica advantage (-5.17 m at 10-30s, -3.92 m at 30s+) lives. This is a structural ceiling of the tracker, not a sampling accident, and does not improve with more matches on this footage.
claims.unit: s (max liveness-guarded gap observed)
claims.method: census of liveness-guarded within-track gap durations across 4 matches
caveats: Four extra matches multiplied 0-3s evidence by four and added nothing at 10-30s/30s+; quadrupling the corpus again would not change that -- only an identity layer would

claims.statement: Re-appearance as free ground truth is a positive methodological contribution: it is the first calibration check of an off-screen player-imputation model on REAL broadcast footage in this literature. DeepMind's Graph Imputer, Choi (arXiv:2607.11548, 2026) and our own frozen B4 v1 gate are all calibrated and evaluated on simulated censoring only.
claims.method: literature comparison of calibration-validation methodology against the two closest incumbent papers
caveats: The method is a genuine contribution even though the finding it produced is a retraction -- it is the instrument, not this particular verdict, that is novel

claims.statement: `tools/tactical_clip.py` asserted the false 'calibrated' claim on every rendered frame; fixed same day: the legend now reads 'model region: NOMINAL 50%/90%' with the measured coverage printed alongside, and a `--self-check` asserts no on-screen string can say 'calibrated' without 'NOT'. A second, root-cause defect shipped alongside it: `imputation_b4_external.load_ours` ghosted a track only after its FINAL sighting, so the uncertainty panel could only ever draw dead re-identification fragments and never a genuinely occluded live player; `full_match_reconstruction.fill_internal_gaps` fixed the assembly layer and took live-track occlusions from 0% to 56% of the ghost population on the flagship passage.
claims.method: code fix + re-render, verified by grep that the demo was the only place the project asserted broadcast calibration
caveats: Re-rendered: results/tactical_clips/tottenham_manutd_h1_0343s.mp4 (+ _sheet.png)

claims.statement: Faces are physically dead for carrier-moment attribution: 0 of 1095 resolvable carrier moments (three labelled matches) clear the ~50 px face-recognition bar. Median face height is 9.9 px against a geometric ceiling of 16.8 px (the tallest carrier in the sample). A real Haar detector finds 17/1093 (1.6%) detections, none at >= 50 px.
claims.unit: fraction of carrier moments clearing 50 px
claims.method: geometric head/face-height derivation from estimate_player_box (head=1/8 standing height, face=1/9) plus OpenCV Haar cascade detection, 3x upscaled crops
caveats: Haar is a weak detector and understates detection, but the geometric ceiling (16.8 px, detector-independent) is what the verdict rests on
Every Haar detection above ~17 px is necessarily a false positive on kit texture or turf

claims.statement: Even on close-up crops (where jersey numbers are read), number-read failures with a usable (>= 50 px) face are only 20 of 3062 (0.65%); the same chunk's jersey reader already produces 508 anchors. Faces would add well under 5% to the anchor supply in exchange for building a face-recognition system and a reference-face database this project does not have. Do not build face recognition.
claims.unit: of 3062 failed close-up reads with a usable face
evidence: results/CROSS_MATCH_GALLERY.md#On close-up crops (where jersey numbers are read)
claims.method: row-aligned join of closeup_reads.csv jersey-read outcomes against Haar face detection on the same 3570 crops (brighton_manutd h1_chunk_000)
caveats: One match/chunk only; multiplied qualitatively, not quantitatively, to the corpus

claims.statement: A cross-match, kit-conditioned pooled gallery lifts REACHABILITY from 0.719 to 0.800 and held-out END-TO-END from 0.400 to 0.522 at unchanged coverage (14.1% of passes) -- but on the 21 held-out moments where both the per-match and pooled galleries assigned a name, the predictions are IDENTICAL (0 discordant pairs, McNemar). The entire gain is 6 moments where the assign/abstain decision flipped, all in the right direction; the dev split shows the opposite sign (0.333 -> 0.312). The gain is wiser abstention, not better identification -- claim no precision gain.
claims.unit: reachability, pooled_kit (fully pooled)
evidence: results/CROSS_MATCH_GALLERY.md#What actually changed, moment by moment
claims.method: leave-one-track-out pooled PRTreID gallery (club, player) keyed across 9 registry matches, scored at the frozen v1 operating point (min_sim 0.88, min_margin 0.01), paired McNemar analysis on shared held-out moments
caveats: Wilson 95% intervals on held-out end-to-end overlap almost completely (0.234-0.593 vs 0.330-0.708)
Dev-only re-tuning of the threshold did not transfer (held-out 0.522 -> 0.438)
Per-player attribution remains not defensible at useful coverage: 0.522 held-out means about half of named passes are wrong

claims.statement: The identity-naming pipeline systematically fails on goalkeepers and centre-backs: Matthijs de Ligt, Andre Onana, Virgil van Dijk and Guglielmo Vicario are named ZERO times across all 1664 named tracks in the entire 9-match corpus, despite being among the highest-volume passers in their matches (26-73 passes each). Goalkeepers are barely tracked at all: 1105 goalkeeper rows against 122732 player rows in one match, because a ball-following broadcast camera rarely frames them. Nine-match cross-match pooling (gallery-001) did not name Onana once -- this is a naming-pipeline defect, not a data-volume defect.
claims.unit: times named (4 highest-volume-passer players)
evidence: results/CROSS_MATCH_GALLERY.md#The passing volume that is still unreachable
claims.method: per-player named-track census across the 9-match pooled gallery corpus, cross-checked against Sofascore totalPass oracle
caveats: The one untried lever is pre-match/warm-up footage with name captions, which the project already owns and has never processed for this purpose

claims.statement: StatsBomb 360 freeze frames carry no ground truth behind their own censoring: freeze-frame points carry only location plus teammate/actor/keeper flags (only 6.05-6.73% of points -- the actor -- carry a recoverable identity), and there is no location, identity, or even a missing-player flag for anyone not visible. It is a second censored sample of the same broadcast-limited process, not a validation set.
evidence: results/STATSBOMB_OPEN_AUDIT.md#2. What a 360 freeze frame actually contains (measured)
results/STATSBOMB_OPEN_AUDIT.md#(c) Is there any ground truth for the players who are not visible?
claims.method: direct measurement of the freeze_frame schema on 2 fully-measured matches (102402 entries) plus 4 more sampled for visible-count statistics
caveats: Both keepers never appear together in any of the 6 measured matches; all 22 players appear together in 1 frame of 18859 measured

claims.statement: StatsBomb 360's visible-area polygons (426 matches, ~1.3M frames) agree with our simulator's along-pitch censoring window (33.5-35.4 m measured vs our tuned 33.8 m half-width) but disagree on the cross-pitch axis: the real, de-rotated polygons taper to 55-59 m of pitch width, against our flat, full-width 68 m rectangle. This disagreement should be resolved before any bias table is computed from the current rectangular censoring operator.
claims.unit: m tapered visible width (range 55-59, vs our flat 68 m)
claims.method: de-rotated visible_area polygon measurement (2 matches deep, x-span at pitch centre and y-extent) compared against synthesizer.imputation.visibility_mask's fitted rectangle
caveats: The along-pitch axis was fitted to hit 11.8 visible players on Metrica and had nothing to do with StatsBomb -- the agreement there is an independent check, not a shared fit

claims.statement: Porting GTA-Link's Connector (agglomerative merging of tracklet-mean PRTreID embeddings, mean recomputed after every merge, under no-overlap / same-team / same-role / 9 m/s gates) onto our SoccerNet-GSR submissions raises GS-HOTA from 22.85 to 24.18 on the 58-sequence valid split, helping 51 of 58 sequences (worst -0.17). At the threshold matched to the shipped single-linkage relink (cosine 0.960) and matched merge precision (80.1% vs 81.0%), it yields 27% more correct merges and +0.68 GS-HOTA / +1.99 GS-AssA, isolating the gain to the connector algorithm rather than the threshold.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA
evidence: results/GTA_LINK_STAGE1.md#4. GS-HOTA on the full SoccerNet-GSR valid split (58 sequences)
claims.method: official trackeval SoccerNetGS evaluator, never reimplemented; GTA arms rewrite only track_id/id (+ propagated jersey) on the same eval_koshkina submissions, so geometry/role/team/confidence are byte-identical to the on-record 22.85 arm; tau frozen on the 3 pilot sequences before touching the other 55
caveats: The frozen tau 0.06 runs at 69.7% GT-audited merge precision, below the 80% bar pre-committed in tools/prtreid_probe.py for graduating relink to per-player facts; per-player facts must use tau 0.04 (80.1% precision, 23.53 GS-HOTA) instead
Required a new GPU pass: 312,830 per-detection PRTreID embeddings at frame stride 2 (the shipped relink cache holds only one median vector per fragment)
GS-DetA stays pinned near 11.7 because most tracks still abstain on jersey; the gain is association, not detection

The association gain does NOT transfer to appearance identification: applying the same connector to the carrier-attribution gallery leaves the naming factor statistically unchanged and makes gallery LOTO top-1 flat-to-worse (see gta-004)

claims.statement: GTA-Link's Tracklet Splitter (DBSCAN over per-detection embeddings) is a NET NEGATIVE on our data and is shipped OFF. It reverses sign between tuning and test: +0.95 GS-HOTA over its own no-split twin on the 3 contaminated pilot sequences (purity 0.7995), but -0.19 GS-HOTA (23.85 vs 24.04) and -3.06 loc GS-AssA on the full 58-sequence split (purity 0.9077), hurting 20 of 58 sequences (worst -5.80) against 7 (worst -0.17) for the connector alone. It removes only 7% of contaminated tracklets at scale (411 -> 381) while nearly doubling fragmentation (87.2 -> 111.4 tracklets/sequence). On real broadcast (fulham_manutd) it makes fragmentation worse (5.043 -> 5.130 tracklets per named-player-half).
claims.unit: GS-HOTA delta vs the identical connector with the splitter disabled
evidence: results/GTA_LINK_STAGE1.md#5. Negative result: the Splitter does not pay on this data
claims.method: split-vs-nosplit ablation with every other variable held fixed, scored by the official trackeval SoccerNetGS evaluator; splitter eps calibrated to the measured PRTreID scale (within-identity cosine distance median 0.044/p90 0.093 vs cross-identity median 0.11-0.15) after eps=0.30 produced zero splits; purity gain checked against a random-cut control at equal cut count (0.9672 vs 0.940-0.945)
caveats: A post-hoc conservative setting (eps 0.08, min_samples 8, min_run 15) reaches 24.24 GS-HOTA, the best single number measured, but it was chosen after seeing full-split scores and is not a clean result; it still loses to no-split on loc GS-AssA (48.11 vs 49.34)

On real matches the splitter is additionally starved: aligned positions are sampled every 5 frames and embedded every 2nd sample, giving a median of 6 embeddings per tracklet (32.8% have >=10), so DBSCAN at min_samples=5 has almost nothing to cluster
The splitter's purity gain is real (0.9077 -> 0.9423, and beats a random-cut control); it simply does not convert into GS-HOTA once the connector also runs

claims.statement: On real broadcast (fulham_manutd), the GTA connector cuts tracklets per named-player-half from 6.739 to 5.043 within chunks (-25.2%) at 82.8% named-merge precision, and to 3.783 (-43.9%) if chunks of a half are connected on one timeline, but cross-chunk merging drops named-merge precision to 71.4% because the 9 m/s motion gate is inert across a chunk boundary and those merges rest on appearance alone.
claims.unit: tracklets per named-player-half (from 6.739; 3.783 cross-chunk)
claims.method: tools/gta_match.py: per-detection PRTreID embeddings from chunk videos via estimate_player_box, connector per chunk (or per half), audited against the 155 OCR-named tracklets over 23 player-halves whose anchor reads are 98.6% verified; a merged group holding two different named players is a proven wrong merge
caveats: The audit covers only the 155 OCR-named tracklets of 8,905, so named-merge precision is a partial view biased toward tracklets clear enough to read a number on
Cross-chunk connection is reported, not recommended, until Stage 2 mutual-exclusion constraints can arbitrate
The naming factor was subsequently measured on the three labelled matches and did not move (gta-004)

claims.statement: Applying the GTA-Link connector to the carrier-attribution gallery does NOT move the naming factor. On the 90 hand labels the factor reads 0.609 (14/23) at baseline and 0.750 (15/20) at tau=0.040, but that is one extra correct answer on a smaller denominator (Fisher p=0.35 vs baseline, p=0.50 vs a zero-merge resample control) bought with a 22.5% coverage loss (40 -> 31 assigned moments), and it is non-monotone in tau (0.750 / 0.700 / 0.652 at tau 0.040/0.050/0.060). On a 2,232-sample paired proxy over identical query crops the merged gallery is flat-to-WORSE: 0.6366 -> 0.6232 at tau=0.040 (McNemar p=0.139), 0.6345 -> 0.6085 at tau=0.050 (p=0.0088) and 0.6503 -> 0.6201 at tau=0.060 (p=0.0028), a monotone decline tracking merge precision (80.1% / 75.0% / 69.7%). The gate-hit factor is identical (0.846) in all five arms, so this stage cannot touch it either.
claims.unit: carrier naming factor (unchanged; best arm 0.750 at p=0.35)
evidence: results/GTA_LINK_STAGE1.md#A2. Factorisation (90 hand labels, 78 judged moments, all 3 matches)
results/GTA_LINK_STAGE1.md#A3. The high-power proxy: gallery leave-one-group-out top-1
claims.method: pure test pass: connector settings frozen from the SoccerNet-GSR split, operating point the v1 frozen threshold (0.88/0.01), config the all-constraints-OFF v1 reproduction whose 0.846/0.719/0.609 was reproduced exactly before any arm ran. Three controls: merged-group leave-one-track-out (else a sibling fragment of the query's own player re-enters its gallery), gallery budget scaled by merge-group size (else merging shrinks the gallery), and a zero-merge resample control isolating the stride-2 frame grid. Proxy pseudo-truth restricted to crops whose source tracklet carried a direct OCR read, so no label invented by the merge is scored.
caveats: With 23 usable moments the label set cannot resolve any intervention smaller than ~0.25; the label-set numbers are a sanity check, not a test
Mechanism for the decline: the gallery scores a player by MAX similarity over his crops, so at 70-80% merge precision every wrongly merged crop becomes a permanent high-similarity distractor
Only the within-chunk connector was used (cross-chunk measured 71.4% named-merge precision, below the 80% bar)
This does not contradict gta-001: association (GS-HOTA, fragmentation) improves; appearance identification does not

claims.statement: Stage 2's Lu-style global identity solve FAILS its pre-declared gate. On 38 held-out SoccerNet-GSR sequences (304,132 auditable rows) per-row identity accuracy (team AND jersey) goes 0.2559 -> 0.2604 (+0.0045) against the appearance-only Stage-1 arm, and the pre-declared paired-per-sequence test cannot separate them (Wilcoxon p = 0.566; 20 helped, 18 hurt, worst -0.229, best +0.193). Gate 2 passes with no regression: GS-HOTA 23.37 -> 24.19 on the same sequences (paired mean +0.709, 24 helped / 14 hurt, p = 0.243). The two arms reach the same accuracy by opposite routes -- the baseline names 15.4% of rows at 88.2% jersey precision, the solver names 85.4% at 26.4% -- and per-row accuracy is blind to that difference, because on a numbered GT player a wrong number scores exactly the same as an abstention.
claims.unit: per-row identity accuracy (team+jersey), GSR held-out 38 sequences
evidence: results/IDENTITY_SOLVER_STAGE2.md#6. Gate 2 - PASS (no regression), and the ablations
claims.method: MILP (scipy.optimize.milp / HiGHS) over x[tracklet, identity|unknown] on the frozen tau=0.040 connector partition; unaries = OCR soft votes with a measured digit-confusion prior, PRTreID mean-of-top-k gallery similarity, team and role gates; constraints = one label per tracklet, no two tracklets sharing a frame share an identity, <=11 named per team per frame. Weights fitted on a declared DEV subset (20 of the 58 sequences, sorted[::3]), written to disk, then TEST (the other 38) scored once. GS-HOTA by the official trackeval SoccerNetGS evaluator on submissions differing only in attributes.jersey of player rows.
caveats: No GSR train or test split exists on this machine -- only the 58-sequence valid split -- so DEV/TEST is a declared partition of it (stated in eval/gsr_identity.py), not the official test split

The input tracklet partition (tau=0.040) was chosen in Stage 1 with all 58 sequences in view, so TEST is clean for the Stage-2 weights only; both arms consume the identical partition, so it cancels in the paired comparison

The pre-declared row-level McNemar secondary is significant (26,468 vs 27,838 discordant rows, p = 4.2e-09) but anticonservative: all rows of a tracklet flip together, so the effective n is tracklets, not rows

The DEV grid optimum sits on a boundary (r_abstain = 0, never reward abstention) and won by 0.005 over a conservative regime in the same grid; the selection metric, not the solver, chose the reckless operating point
POST-HOC and not claimed: one point of the same DEV grid, chosen after seeing TEST and moving two parameters, reaches 0.2742 at p = 0.0029 with 18.3% named-row coverage at 85.3% precision
Ablations on TEST: no OCR 0.1397, no mutual exclusion 0.2317, no appearance 0.2379, no digit-confusion prior 0.2564 (the prior is inert, row McNemar p = 0.52)

claims.statement: Broadcast player naming is capped by OCR reach, not by the inference layer. On the SoccerNet-GSR public split only 8.7% of tracks carry a Koshkina jersey read (425/4,870, precision 328/375 = 0.875), and only 24.1% of prediction rows belong to a player read anywhere in their sequence. Handing each merged tracklet its best possible label gives an oracle of 0.835 identity accuracy, but restricting that oracle to the OCR-anchored identities -- the only ones any method can reach -- gives 0.365, against 0.128 for abstaining on everything. The appearance link that would spread those reads runs at 0.640 tracklet top-1 (0.676 row-weighted) against a mean of 4.55 anchored candidates, and 1,348 of 1,815 queries have no anchored identity to match at all.
claims.unit: evidence ceiling on per-row identity accuracy (team+jersey), GSR 58 sequences
evidence: results/IDENTITY_SOLVER_STAGE2.md#2. What the evidence can possibly support (measured first, all 58 sequences)
claims.method: counted directly from the GT annotations, the Koshkina vote checkpoints and the tau=0.040 merged partition: read rate over all tracks; per-row auditable GT match within the official 5 m tolerance; oracle = dominant GT jersey per merged tracklet; anchored oracle = the same restricted to identities with at least one direct OCR read; appearance top-1 = mean-of-top-k cosine against the anchored galleries with the query's own tracklet excluded.
caveats: GSR-specific numbers; the read rate on our own broadcast matches is different (155 named tracklets over 23 player-halves on fulham_manutd)
The 0.640 appearance top-1 replicates the ~0.62 LOTO top-1 measured on real matches in results/GTA_LINK_STAGE1.md A3, on a completely different corpus
The oracle assumes one label per tracklet; it is bounded above by the 0.894 row purity of the merged partition
SoccerNet-GSR labels no goalkeeper numbers at all (0 of 77 GK tracks numbered), so the GK half of the identity problem is invisible on this benchmark

claims.statement: The never-named-goalkeeper defect is fixed by the Stage-2 role gate plus a lineup roster slot. Across manutd_liverpool, manutd_tottenham and manutd_brighton the Stage-1 arm names ZERO keeper slots (0 of 4 per match) and the few goalkeeper-role tracks it does name it names with an outfielder (0 of 7, 0 of 7, 0 of 3); the solver fills both keeper slots in all three matches with the correct starters (Onana plus Alisson / Vicario / Verbruggen) and names 166/182, 169/186 and 237/280 goalkeeper-role tracks. On manutd_liverpool the name set grows from 18 players to 29, adding Matthijs de Ligt (384 tracks) and Virgil van Dijk (242) -- two more of the four players recorded as never named.
claims.unit: keeper slots filled per match (was 0 of 4)
evidence: results/IDENTITY_SOLVER_STAGE2.md#7. Real matches: the goalkeepers are named (gate 4), and the spot-check (gate 3)
claims.method: tools/identity_match.py: the GSR-frozen solver config applied per half, with roster, shirt, position and substitution windows from outputs/identity/<match>_lineup_assign.parquet, OCR reads from the anchor-named track table and appearance galleries pooled over the whole half. Baseline = the Stage-1 connector plus unanimous OCR-name propagation (tools/gta_carrier.propagate_names).
caveats: Measured at the frozen r_abstain = 0 operating point, which names 87-95% of all tracklets, so 'named' is cheap here; only 35-50% of goalkeeper-role tracks receive a keeper's name
There is no per-track ground truth on these matches: this counts coverage of the keeper slot, not naming accuracy
Implementation ceilings: candidate identities pruned to the best 6 per tracklet and HiGHS given 60 s per chunk, so real-match assignments are incumbents, not proven optima
The same operating point collapses the 78-moment carrier factorisation (assigned moments 40 -> 16, naming 0.609 -> 0.583 on a denominator falling 23 -> 12); nothing is claimed from that label set

claims.statement: The evidence-density law for player-event attribution, measured by simulating identity evidence on FOOTPASS ground truth (97,397 action events, 54 matches) with a simulator calibrated to this project's own measurements. Event-attribution precision 0.85 at coverage >= 0.50 requires an OCR-like read density of d = 0.347 reads per tracklet at read precision 0.86 (d = 0.268 at precision 0.95) -- 4.0x and 3.1x today's measured 0.087. Today's density delivers coverage 0.124 at that precision floor. In actionable units that is 0.74 -> 2.96 reads per minute a player spends on screen. Raising read precision from 0.86 to 0.95 is worth only a 1.3x reduction in the required density: volume, not purity, is the binding constraint. Held-out VAL (3 unseen games) reproduces d* = 0.347 exactly.
claims.unit: x increase in OCR read density needed for attribution precision 0.85 at coverage 0.50
evidence: results/EVIDENCE_DENSITY_LAW.md#3. The OCR-like channel -- the law
claims.method: tools/evidence_sim.py fragments FOOTPASS's dense per-frame truth into tracklets reproducing the measured post-connector fragmentation (4.72 per 30 s on-screen), feeds a synthetic appearance channel calibrated to the measured 0.6366 top-1 at 4.55 candidates and OCR-like reads at swept density/precision, and solves with the UNMODIFIED generator.identity_solve. Graded PCBAS-style on action events: coverage over all events, precision over answered, dial = assigned-identity posterior. 20 TRAIN halves (19,603 events) per condition; VAL held out.
caveats: The simulator hands the solver the acting player's tracklet (oracle gate), so these are NAMING numbers; end-to-end attribution would be ~0.85x them (the measured 0.846 gate-hit factor).

Calibration gate passed on the two numbers that matter (solver 0.2576 vs Stage 2's 0.2604; appearance-only 0.1246 vs 0.136) but the anchored fraction and direct-read coverage run 20-30% low, a row-weighted vs event-weighted denominator effect -- the simulator is if anything pessimistic.
The fragmenter never produces a contaminated tracklet (Stage 1 measured 10.96% of real fragments as contaminated), and under-represents both tails of the tracklet-span distribution.
18.5% of FOOTPASS events are committed by a player off-screen at that instant, so 0.815 is the maximum coverage any from-pixels arm can reach.

claims.statement: The pre-declared Stage-3 commentary operating point (>= 1.5 names/min, name precision >= 0.60, timestamp lag IQR <= 4 s) FAILS its go/no-go gate, and by a wide margin. Simulated on FOOTPASS it delivers coverage 0.000 at precision floor 0.85 AND at floor 0.60, with full-coverage precision 0.142 against a no-evidence control of 0.139 -- indistinguishable from having no evidence at all. Added to today's OCR channel it is actively harmful: coverage at precision 0.85 falls 0.124 -> 0.042 and full-coverage precision 0.361 -> 0.337, dose-dependently. The cause is alignment, not the channel: at a 4 s lag IQR a mention binds to the correct player 13.2% of the time against a 12.5% chance rate, because the ball travels a median 24 m in 4 s. Subtracting the lag's median doubles binding to 0.283 and still clears no floor; only sub-second alignment (IQR <= 0.5 s, binding 0.72) makes the channel reach today's-OCR-grade usefulness. Even with perfect binding, 3 names/min at 0.95 precision reaches coverage 0.295 at precision 0.85, short of 0.50.
claims.unit: coverage at precision 0.85 delivered by 1.5 names/min at precision 0.60, 4 s lag IQR
evidence: results/EVIDENCE_DENSITY_LAW.md#4. The commentary channel -- verdict on the pre-declared go/no-go point
claims.method: tools/evidence_sim.py generates (timestamp, name) mentions at FOOTPASS action events, names the true actor with the arm's precision, timestamps it late with a Gamma(2) lag matched to the arm's IQR, and binds it to the tracklet nearest the ball proxy at the lagged time -- including wrongly. 27 commentary-only conditions (0.5-5.0 names/min x precision 0.60/0.80/0.95 x lag IQR 4/8 s) plus lag-compensated and oracle-bound controls; 19,603 TRAIN events per condition, replicated on held-out VAL.
caveats: The ball position is a proxy (the acting player's position at each event, linearly interpolated between events); FOOTPASS ships no ball track. A real ball track would move the binding numbers somewhat but not the ordering, since the chance rate is set by the 8.0 tracklets alive at an instant.
The gate as written never specified a timestamp-alignment precision, which this experiment shows is the only variable that matters -- the failure is partly a defect in the gate.
Simulated mentions are drawn uniformly from annotated action events; real commentary is biased towards salient events, which would raise volume on shots/goals and lower it elsewhere.

claims.statement: Fragmentation and evidence density are interchangeable levers on attribution, at a measured exchange rate. Holding OCR read VOLUME fixed at today's level (the physically invariant quantity -- fragmenting a track does not create legible frames), attribution precision falls monotonically with fragmentation: 0.610 at 0.63 fragments per 30 s of on-screen time, 0.361 at the measured 4.27, 0.351 at 5.31, 0.346 at 6.19. Coverage at precision 0.85 is 0.505 with perfect within-chunk association versus 0.124 at today's fragmentation (VAL 0.501 / 0.082). So 4x the OCR reads and a ~7x reduction in fragmentation buy about the same thing. This qualifies Stage 1's negative result: its connector moved fragmentation 5.87 -> 4.72, a 24% step on a curve whose payoff lives between 4.7 and 1.0.
claims.unit: coverage at precision 0.85 with perfect within-chunk association at today's read volume (vs 0.124 today)
evidence: results/EVIDENCE_DENSITY_LAW.md#5. The fragmentation interaction, and the confound in it
claims.method: tools/evidence_sweep.py fragc/* arms: the fragmentation rate is swept over 0.63 / 4.27 / 5.31 / 6.19 fragments per 30 s of on-screen time with the per-tracklet read density rescaled so that reads per 30 s of on-screen time stay at the measured 0.370. The uncontrolled arms (density fixed per tracklet) show the OPPOSITE sign and are reported alongside as the confound they are.
caveats: The zero-fragmentation arm is one tracklet per player per 2-minute chunk -- an upper bound no real tracker will reach; the usable result is the exchange rate, not the endpoint.
Same simulator caveats as ident-013 (oracle gate on which tracklet acted, no contaminated tracklets, independent appearance draws across a player's fragments).

claims.statement: 18.5% of FOOTPASS player-centric action events are committed by a player who is not in the broadcast frame at the annotated instant (actor on-screen at the event frame: 0.8151 over all 97,397 events; players are on screen for only 33.4% of player-frames overall). This is a hard ceiling on any from-pixels attribution system: maximum achievable coverage is 0.815, and the measured full-coverage arms land at 0.81, i.e. they already answer for essentially every event that is physically answerable.
claims.unit: fraction of PCBAS action events whose actor is on-screen at the annotated frame
evidence: results/EVIDENCE_DENSITY_LAW.md#1. The substrate: what FOOTPASS actually contains, and one hard ceiling
claims.method: Direct count over all 102 TRAIN+VAL half-datasets of data/footpass/digest/*.npz: an event's actor counts as on-screen when its (player, frame) falls inside a visibility run, where visibility is roi_x/y/width/height being non-NaN (all four are NaN together exactly when the player is not in the broadcast frame; tracking x,y is always present).
caveats: FOOTPASS is Ligue 1 / Bundesliga / Serie A / La Liga / UCL 2023-24 broadcast; the on-screen fraction varies 0.201-0.517 across halves, so a different broadcast style would move this number.
The official FOOTPASS baseline (46.41) consumes ground-truth game state and therefore does not pay this cost; an honest from-pixels number must.

claims.statement: The measured jersey-read density of 0.087 was largely an AGGREGATION artifact, not an evidence shortage. generator.jersey_id.aggregate_votes pools every crop of a tracklet, and KoshkinaRecognizer.crop_probs gives each crop that fails legibility/pose/OCR a one-hot on the ILLEGIBLE class whose peak is 1.0 -- the maximum weight the confidence-weighted mean can assign -- so a tracklet must be MAJORITY legible-and-agreeing before it commits a number. Counting only crops that actually read a number, at the identical 20-crop budget and identical models, read density on GSR TEST-38 rises 0.0877 -> 0.2147 (2.45x) at read precision 0.8457 against the shipped 0.8618.
claims.unit: multiplier on read density from the aggregation change alone, matched crop volume
evidence: results/OCR_DENSIFICATION.md#1.1 The finding that changes the build: **0.087 is largely an aggregation artifact**
results/OCR_DENSIFICATION.md#5.1 Which lever did it - aggregation or crops
claims.method: Per-crop OCR evidence (legibility score, pose-torso flag, PARSeq positional softmaxes) persisted for all 197,175 crops of the 58 GSR valid sequences (eval/gsr_jersey.py --percrop), then re-aggregated offline with generator.jersey_id.percrop_votes. The matched-volume control sub-samples each track's persisted crops back to 20 evenly-spread rows, so the crop budget is held at the on-record value and only the pooling rule changes. Read precision graded against the per-track dominant GT jersey; the grader reproduces the on-record 425/4,870 = 0.0873 at 327/375 = 0.872 exactly.
caveats: d is per ORIGINAL player/GK track, the same denominator as the on-record 425/4,870.
The matched-volume control re-samples 20 of the 60 persisted crops, which is not bit-identical to the on-record 20-crop frame grid; it is a matched-VOLUME control, not a matched-FRAME control.
Measured on SoccerNet-GSR broadcast; the real-match close-up-anchor funnel is a different mechanism and is reported separately.

claims.statement: OCR densification gate on SoccerNet-GSR TEST-38: PASSED on the arms declared for DEV->TEST shrinkage, FAILED on the arm labelled primary. Read density d = 0.2083 at read precision 0.8578 (DEV-0.85-floor rule) against the on-record 0.0877 at 0.8618 -- 2.38x the density at statistically indistinguishable precision, clearing the pre-declared d >= 0.174 at precision >= 0.80. The pre-declared PRIMARY arm (DEV-0.80-floor rule) reached d = 0.2889 but read precision 0.7993 (685/857), short of the 0.800 floor by one read, and is recorded as a FAIL.
claims.unit: fraction of original player/GK tracks carrying >= 1 jersey read (GSR TEST-38)
evidence: results/OCR_DENSIFICATION.md#5. PRIMARY gate - d and read precision on TEST-38
claims.method: Three aggregation rules frozen on the 20 DEV sequences only (one per DEV read-precision floor 0.80/0.85/0.87), written to results/ocr_density_rule.json at 21:37:27, then measured once on the 38 TEST sequences at 21:38:04. Knobs: per-crop confidence floor, minimum agreeing crops, offline ResNet34 legibility floor, emit-all. GPU pass: 60 crops per track (on record: 20), 197,175 crops, ~2.3 h, one job.
caveats: The single-floor DEV selection criterion originally written down (0.85) was changed to three declared floors on DEV evidence before TEST was read; the change and its ordering evidence are in section 3 of the results file.
The law's bar is d = 0.347 at read precision 0.86; 0.2083 does not reach it. The gap closed from 4.0x to 1.7x.
Read precision is graded against the dominant GT jersey of each original track, so a read on a contaminated tracklet (Stage 1 measured 10.96% of fragments as contaminated) is charged as an error.

claims.statement: Stage 2's Gate 1, which FAILED on the aggregated OCR (+0.0045 identity accuracy, Wilcoxon p = 0.566), PASSES decisively on the densified evidence with the SAME frozen solver weights: per-row identity accuracy on GSR TEST-38 goes 0.2559 (appearance-only baseline) -> 0.4488 (+0.193), 34 sequences helped / 4 hurt, Wilcoxon p < 1e-6. Coverage at jersey-precision 0.85 goes 0.1739 -> 0.4141 and GS-HOTA 24.19 -> 33.20 (35 helped / 3 hurt). Stage 2's own diagnosis - the binding cause is evidence, not inference - is confirmed by the intervention it predicted, and its 0.365 evidence ceiling is exceeded because that ceiling was a property of the reads the old aggregation committed.
claims.unit: row-weighted coverage at jersey precision >= 0.85, GSR TEST-38
evidence: results/OCR_DENSIFICATION.md#6. SECONDARY gate - the frozen Stage-2 solver on densified evidence
claims.method: Frozen results/identity_solver_config.json, unchanged except the digit-confusion prior refit on DEV-20 per-crop reads (348 reads, 55 wrong, 573 aligned digit observations against Stage 2's 129/214). Coverage/precision curve traced by dialling the assignment posterior, computed by the same code on both arms; the on-record arm reproduces Stage 2's published numbers exactly (0.2559 -> 0.2604, p = 0.566) as a harness check. GS-HOTA via the unchanged official sn-trackeval SoccerNetGS scorer.
caveats: The 0.1739 on-record baseline is a GSR TEST-38 number computed here; the 0.124 quoted in the research plan is the FOOTPASS SIMULATOR's number and is not directly comparable.
A second declared arm that also refits p_correct on DEV scores marginally higher (0.4510 identity, 0.4182 coverage@0.85, GS-HOTA 33.32); both are reported.
The solver still runs at the r_abstain = 0 operating point Stage 2 warned against shipping for per-player facts; the coverage dial, not the point estimate, is the usable output.
GSR labels no goalkeeper jersey numbers, so nothing here grades the GK case.

claims.statement: Qwen2-VL-2B as a second jersey voter: REJECTED on the pre-declared adoption rule. It fits the 4 GB GPU at 4-bit (1.62 GiB peak) and is fast (0.29 s/crop against a 2 s bar), but on the crops where the shipped chain abstains it produces a number for 34% of them at precision 0.265 (9/34) -- far below the >= 0.80 bar, and exactly the low-precision-evidence-is-worse-than-none case. Not adopted. Separately and not claimed: on crops that already pass the legibility gate it is more accurate per crop than PARSeq (0.800 against 0.700, McNemar 14 vs 4 discordant, p = 0.031, n = 100), i.e. a re-ranking role rather than a densification one.
claims.unit: precision of the reads Qwen2-VL-2B adds where the shipped chain abstains
evidence: results/OCR_DENSIFICATION.md#7. Qwen2-VL-2B trial (boxed) - VERDICT: DROP as a second voter, keep as a re-ranker candidate
claims.method: 200 crops from SNGS-021 + SNGS-024, stratified 100 where the chain reads a number and 100 where it abstains, graded against the GT jersey of each crop's track. Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct, 4-bit NF4 via bitsandbytes 0.50.0, greedy decoding, 8 new tokens, prompt asking for the number or NONE.
caveats: n = 100 per stratum on two sequences; the added-read precision has a wide interval (roughly 0.14-0.43) but is nowhere near 0.80.
Per-CROP precision, not per-track: the shipped chain's track-level precision is much higher than the 0.700 shown here.
The re-ranker result is a by-product of the trial, was not its pre-declared question, and has not been measured end-to-end; pursuing it costs ~16 GPU-hours over the 197k persisted crops.

claims.statement: On real broadcast (manutd_liverpool, all 11 chunks, 8,345 player/GK tracklets), running the per-track crop OCR with the GSR-frozen densifying rule raises jersey-read density from 0.0265 (221 tracks, the shipped close-up-anchor chain) to 0.1150 (960 tracks) at the gate-passing rule and 0.2171 (1,812 tracks) at the looser one -- 4.3x and 8.2x. Goalkeeper-role tracks carrying a read go from 3 to 11 (of 182). Only 89 of the 221 close-up-anchor tracks are also read by the per-crop pass, so the two mechanisms are substantially complementary rather than nested.
claims.unit: fraction of manutd_liverpool player/GK tracklets carrying >= 1 jersey read
evidence: results/OCR_DENSIFICATION.md#8. Real-match spot-check (report only, no ground truth)
claims.method: tools/ocr_match.py: crops cut from the chunk videos with generator.team_anchor.estimate_player_box (no re-detection), 20 per track, every crop's legibility / pose / PARSeq evidence persisted to outputs/manutd_liverpool/final/ocr_percrop/*.parquet (94,244 crops, 1 h 46 m GPU), then aggregated with the rule frozen on the GSR DEV split. 'Before' is the shipped close-up-anchor chain outputs/identity/manutd_liverpool_named_tracks_both2_prtreid.parquet.
caveats: STATUS PENDING because there is NO per-track ground truth on this match: this is a density number with no measured precision. The rule's 0.858 read precision was measured on SoccerNet-GSR, whose crops come from a re-detected box rather than estimate_player_box, so it does not automatically transfer.
One match only. manutd_tottenham and manutd_brighton were not run (a further ~3.5 GPU-hours at the measured cost).
The union of the close-up-anchor chain and the per-crop pass was not measured, though the 89/221 overlap says it would be larger than either.

CORRECTED 2026-07-29: the '89 of the 221' overlap quoted next to the 0.85-floor row is the 0.87-floor number. At the floors as labelled the overlap is 158/221 (0.80), 114/221 (0.85), 89/221 (0.87). See results/OCR_REALMATCH.md section 2.2.

claims.statement: Per-crop jersey OCR replicates on all three labelled ManU matches: read density d goes 0.0265 -> 0.1150 (liverpool), 0.0316 -> 0.1053 (tottenham), 0.0179 -> 0.1263 (brighton) against the shipped close-up-anchor chain, pooled 0.0253 -> 0.1143 (669 -> 3,075 tracklets read, 4.60x); and on the 345 tracklets both mechanisms read, the per-crop number agrees with the 98.6%-verified anchor number 318 times (0.9217, Wilson 0.889-0.946) -- above the 0.8578 read precision the same frozen rule measured on SoccerNet-GSR TEST-38.
claims.unit: fraction of player/GK tracklets carrying >= 1 jersey read, pooled over 3 matches
evidence: results/OCR_REALMATCH.md#2. Read density `d` on all three matches
claims.method: tools/ocr_match.py, 20 crops per track cut from the chunk videos with generator.team_anchor.estimate_player_box, 306,569 crops over 26,573 tracklets in ~5.8 GPU-hours (one match at a time), aggregated with the 0.85-DEV-floor rule frozen on GSR in results/ocr_density_rule.json. Agreement measured against outputs/identity/<match>_named_tracks_both2_prtreid.parquet.
caveats: The 0.9217 is an AGREEMENT rate on the subset both mechanisms read (345 of 3,075 read tracklets), not a precision estimate. It is the easy subset by construction and the anchor chain is itself fallible. No per-track ground truth exists on these matches.
Density is still far below the d* = 0.347 the measured law asks for (results/EVIDENCE_DENSITY_LAW.md); 0.1143 pooled is a third of it.
GK-role tracklets carrying a read go 3/1/0 -> 11/9/7, but this buys nothing for goalkeeper NAMING (see ident-023): the role gate already did that work.

claims.statement: NEGATIVE: the frozen Stage-2 identity solver at its r_abstain = 0 operating point is SIGNIFICANTLY WORSE than the greedy arms at real-match identification, on per-crop evidence as well as on close-up evidence. Gallery leave-one-group-out top-1 falls 0.6251 -> 0.3591 against the Stage-1 connector control (paired McNemar n = 2,910, 949 control-only-right vs 175 arm-only-right, p = 4.5e-129) and 0.6373 -> 0.3523 against the zero-merge control (p = 8.2e-99). The close-up-evidence arm is the same, 0.3300.
claims.unit: LOTO gallery top-1 identification rate, Stage-2 solver names, 3 ManU matches
evidence: results/OCR_REALMATCH.md#6. THE POWERED TEST -- LOTO gallery leave-one-group-out, as pre-declared in section 0
claims.method: tools/gta_carrier.py --loto: every gallery crop scored against the rest of its team gallery with its whole merge group removed; queries restricted to crops whose source tracklet carries a direct close-up-anchor OCR read and graded against THAT anchor player name, never the arm own gallery label. Exact paired McNemar on identical query keys (match, chunk, src_track, frame).
caveats: The truth labels come from the anchor chain, which is also the label source for the two control arms but not for the solver arm -- the test is biased AGAINST the solver, so -0.27 is a generous estimate of its deficit, not a harsh one.

This measures the r_abstain = 0 operating point specifically. results/IDENTITY_SOLVER_STAGE2.md section 5c shows the solver traces a coverage/precision dial; an abstaining operating point was not re-measured here.
The one real Stage-2 win is untouched by this: it still fills 2 of 4 keeper slots with the correct starters in all three matches where the baseline fills 0.

claims.statement: The pre-declared powered test of whether denser OCR moves attribution on our own broadcast FAILS. Best arm (Stage-1 naming rule fed per-crop reads) gains +0.0302 LOTO gallery top-1 over the Stage-1 connector control (0.6777 -> 0.7079, paired n = 1,756, 210 arm-only-right vs 157 control-only-right, McNemar p = 0.00656) against a Bonferroni alpha of 0.00625 -- short by 0.0003 -- and shows nothing against the zero-merge control (p = 0.585). The 78-moment label set reads naming 0.609 -> 0.800 with coverage RISING (40 -> 45 assigned moments), the first arm to move both together, but that set is Fisher p = 0.207 and cannot referee it.

claims.statement: THE PRICE OF LEGITIMACY, DECOMPOSED. On the valid TEST-38 subset at the frozen 33.20 recipe, replacing the GT team map alone costs -1.06 GS-HOTA (33.20 -> 32.14), replacing the GT roster alone with the self-roster costs -1.47 (-> 31.73), and doing both costs -2.48 (-> 30.72) -- additive to within 0.05. The team map is worth 7.07 GS-HOTA in total (a no-information {0:left,1:right} map scores 26.12) and the geometric resolver recovers 6.01 of that, 85%. An unconstrained 1..99 x 2-side roster is strictly worse than the self-roster at every measurement point (TEST-38 29.58 vs 31.73; DEV-20 27.01 vs 30.87): it names 2513 of 2541 tracklets against 1536 and drops identity accuracy 0.4239 -> 0.3676, because 198 slots dilute the per-identity prior 12x and remove the solver's abstention pressure. All of the loss lands in GS-DetA; GS-AssA moves by at most 0.8 across all seven arms.

Seven arms were scored on the declared local TEST-38 partition. That is a deliberate instruction from the campaign (measure the leak there), not a tuning pass -- the GT-free config was chosen on DEV-20 and frozen before this matrix was run.

claims.statement: THE DEEPER CLUSTER IS THE LEFT TEAM. A team defends one goal, so over a 30 s clip the side being attacked keeps its defensive line deepest and the two kit clusters' centroids are ordered by the goal they defend. Assigning 'left' to the cluster with the smaller mean pitch-x over all player rows (goalkeepers excluded -- their kit is a third colour and the two-way KMeans assigns them at random) resolves the cluster->side permutation with NO ground truth at 56/58 = 0.9655 on the valid split and 45/49 = 0.9184 on the held-out official test split, 101/107 = 0.9439 pooled. Four co-tied variants of the same family (trimmed mean, frame-paired Mann-Whitney U, mean of per-frame centroid gaps) all score 56/58; per-track means score 45/58 and a GK-only signal 2/12, worse than chance. A flip is not a degradation but an annihilation -- the clip keeps its positions and jerseys and scores ~5 GS-HOTA -- so at 91.8% the team-side permutation is now the binding constraint on a legitimate GSR number, ahead of both jersey evidence and association: 91.8% -> 98% is worth about +2.4 GS-HOTA on test.
claims.unit: fraction of the 49 official test sequences whose cluster->side permutation the geometric resolver gets right (vs the GT-agreement map)

The statistic was chosen from a five-member family measured on the valid split; the test split was never used to choose anything and is the held-out measurement.

All six failures have healthy clustering (GT purity 0.878-0.966, kit minority share 0.434-0.486) -- they are genuine geometric counterexamples, clips where the attacking team's centroid sits behind the defending team's for the whole 30 s.
The statistic was selected on valid, so the valid 0.9655 carries selection exposure (one binary choice among four tied variants). The test 0.9184 does not.

claims.statement: NEGATIVE -- A THIRD OF THE GSR TRAIN SPLIT IS UNUSABLE FOR TEAM WORK. 18 of the 57 train sequences (SNGS-060 through SNGS-077, one contiguous block) drive the pipeline's CIELAB-KMeans JerseyColorTeamClassifier to a degenerate fit: minority cluster share 0.056-0.161 against a median of 0.448 on valid and 0.450 on test, and on the seven that were fully extracted the GT team-agreement purity sits at chance (0.504-0.537). Valid has 0/58 such sequences and test 0/49. Any team-side or team-attribute study on those clips measures noise. The remaining 39 train sequences are healthy and would give a third, fully untouched measurement of the team-side resolver for about 4.5 GPU hours of stride-1 extraction; that was not spent. Two cheaper probe designs were measured and both fail: stride 10 collapses ByteTrack (119 rows per clip against ~11,000 at stride 1) and clip truncation destroys the resolver's own signal (accuracy 0.9655 over 750 frames, 0.9310 over 375, 0.8621 over 250, 0.7931 over 150).

claims.method: Per sequence, _collect_team_crops + JerseyColorTeamClassifier().fit().predict() on the fit crops themselves (~11 s/clip, all 57 train sequences); valid and test measured from the cached stride-1 positions parquets' team column. GT purity computed on the seven train sequences extracted at stride 1 by nearest-GT matching within the 5 m tolerance, the same rule resolve_team_map uses.
caveats: Train balance is measured on the classifier's own fit crops, valid/test on the post-tracking parquet rows -- consistent where both were available (SNGS-060: 0.056 vs 0.03) but not the identical statistic.
The cause was not diagnosed beyond 'these clips' kit pair is not separable in CIELAB at k=2'. It is one contiguous ID block, so probably one or two matches.

claims.statement: THE TEAM-SIDE RESOLVER IS ALREADY AT ITS OWN CEILING. Running the shipped rule -- the kit cluster with the smaller mean pitch-x is 'left' -- on the GROUND-TRUTH positions (perfect detection, perfect team clustering, perfect calibration) scores 112/115 = 0.9739 on the train+valid development sequences and 45/49 on the official test split, the same 45/49 our estimator gets. Pooled over all 164 labelled GSR sequences the oracle is 157/164 = 0.9573. The residual failures are not estimation errors: they are clips whose ground-truth geometry inverts, where the team defending one goal has its visible players deeper into the opposite half than the team that defends it (SNGS-038, -092, -111 on dev; SNGS-126, -131, -195, -197 on test; inversion magnitudes 0.69 to 8.81 m). Ground-truth annotations only cover players visible in the broadcast frame, so the GT geometry inherits the camera's framing. The N1b target of 0.98 is therefore above the oracle ceiling of the entire positional family and the +2.4 GS-HOTA prize costed for it does not exist inside that family. Every depth variant measured is WORSE on ground truth than the incumbent: median 0.9652, per-frame paired mean 0.9565, paired t 0.9565, Welch t on centroids 0.9565, per-frame sign vote 0.9478, three-deepest 0.9217, three-highest 0.8870, extreme-owner 0.8783, single-deepest 0.8000, single-highest 0.7652.

claims.method: tools/gsr_teamside.py --ceiling re-codes each sequence's Labels-GameState.json into a positions-shaped table (GT sides left/right as clusters 0/1, bbox_pitch shifted out of the centred frame into the pipeline's [0,105]x[0,68] frame) and runs the identical side_scores battery on it, so a rule graded on GT and on our parquets is literally the same code. --dev runs the battery on our cached positions; --verify reads the test split once for the frozen rule only.
caveats: The oracle is the accuracy of the RULE given exact inputs, not a hard bound on our estimator: a noisy estimator can beat it by being wrong in a compensating way, and does (we get SNGS-038 and SNGS-195 right, and SNGS-034/-097/-105/-129 wrong, where the oracle does the opposite). The counts coincide on both graded splits; the clips do not.

The early GT-oracle scan was run over all 164 sequences in one pass, so the fact that three of four test failures are GT inversions was seen before the freeze. It set no threshold and selected no candidate -- every selection was computed on train+valid -- but the exposure is on record.
18 train sequences (SNGS-060...077) have a degenerate kit clustering and are excluded from the our-positions pools; they are kept in the GT oracle pool, where kit clustering plays no part.

CORRECTED 2026-08-13 by gsr-gt-001: the 'ground-truth geometry inverts because GT inherits the broadcast's framing' explanation holds for SNGS-038 (+0.95 m) and SNGS-195 (+0.69 m) only. SNGS-092, SNGS-111, SNGS-126, SNGS-131 and SNGS-197 are whole-clip GT team side SWAPS (second-half clips carrying the first-half convention), confirmed by a 164-sequence cross-clip scan and independently stated by the WACV 2026 Broadcast2Pitch paper for the three test clips. The 112/115 and 45/49 oracle counts are unaffected; only the diagnosis of the residuals changes.

claims.statement: THE ONLY RULE THAT CLEARS THE CEILING IS THE KEEPER, AND WE CANNOT REACH IT. 'A goalkeeper's own team defends the goal he stands in' is 113/113 = 1.0000 on ground-truth positions across the 115 train+valid GSR sequences, including all three clips where the depth ordering inverts -- it is what the GSR left/right attribute means, not a correlate of it (on SNGS-092 the GT keepers sit at pitch-x -48.0 'left' and +37.4 'right' while the outfield means invert by 3.76 m). It is not shippable because it needs the keeper's TEAM. Over 5,384 keeper detections matched to GT keepers within the 5 m tolerance on 57 development sequences, the two-way CIELAB kit KMeans puts a keeper in his OWN team's cluster in only 1,313 rows = 0.2439, and by sequence majority in 13 of 57 = 0.228. The error is systematic, not random: the keeper lands in the OPPONENT's cluster 75.6% of rows and 44/57 = 77.2% of sequences, which is what a kit chosen to contrast with one's own outfield strip produces. Inverting the assignment gives a real rule at about 0.75, far below the incumbent's 0.94, and it cannot be used as a gated override because no confidence flags the clips that need it. The PROXIMITY keeper rule -- which is what 'keepers sit deepest, use role not kit cluster' reduces to -- is a depth rule in disguise: 0.6903 on ground truth, inheriting every inversion.
claims.unit: fraction of matched goalkeeper detections whose kit cluster is the keeper's own team, 5,384 rows over 57 GSR development sequences

claims.method: tools/gsr_teamside.py --gklink matches every role=goalkeeper detection carrying a kit cluster to the nearest GT goalkeeper within GSR_DIST_TOL_M (5 m) in the same frame and compares the sequence's GT-agreement cluster->side map applied to that kit cluster with the GT keeper's own side. The gk_self ceiling comes from --ceiling, where GT keepers carry their true side as the cluster index.
caveats: Measured with this pipeline's CIELAB two-way JerseyColorTeamClassifier only. A three-way or keeper-aware clustering was not built or measured; the 0.2439 is the starting point for that work, not a property of the problem.
gk_self is graded on 113 of 115 dev sequences -- two clips have no GT keeper with a pitch position at all.

claims.statement: NEGATIVE -- THE TWO REMAINING TEAM-SIDE FAMILIES CARRY NOTHING. (1) Solve-both-and-vote carries exactly zero bits: the identity solver reads Identity.team (a cluster index), Identity.number and Identity.role, never the left/right side string, and the self-roster is built in cluster space and only named through the side map, so the objective is invariant under the permutation. Measured on six valid sequences under both maps: identical assignment 6/6, identical roster slots 6/6, max absolute posterior delta exactly 0.0, identical summed posteriors to 16 significant figures. Every criterion the brief listed -- total objective, summed posteriors, OCR/roster consistency, coverage-at-abstention -- is a function of that objective and so is invariant too. (2) Attack direction is not recoverable from a 30-second clip: possession-conditioned ball drift scores 60/115 = 0.5217 on GROUND TRUTH, i.e. chance with perfect ball, perfect players and perfect teams. (3) Ensembles are selection noise: of 1,470 vote combinations, 112 beat the incumbent on the 67 whole dev clips and 15 beat it on the 204-window stress pool, but the two winners are different ensembles and each loses on the pool it was not chosen on (whole-clip winner 0.9701 -> 0.7941 on windows against the incumbent's 0.8284), and NO ensemble beats the incumbent on ground truth. (4) The metre margin is a ranking signal but not a gate: AUC 0.948 on dev and 0.867 on test, yet catching all four test failures costs abstaining on 13 of 49 clips and GSR admits no abstention. Dev failures are mostly weak evidence and test failures are mostly inversions -- strong evidence pointing the wrong way -- which is why a confidence fitted on one split mis-describes the other.

The window stress pool's failures are the estimation mode, not the inversion mode, so it can rank rules but cannot be used to build a whole-clip confidence.

claims.statement: The SoccerNet-GSR association deficit is a LINKING deficit, not a detection deficit: an oracle connector that merged our existing tracklets correctly would score raw GS-AssA about 67.9 on the valid split -- inside the leaderboard's 62-82 band -- without one extra detection, against the 39.8 raw ByteTrack measures and the 47.9 the GTA connector at tau 0.040 reaches. The GTA connector therefore realises only 24.5% of the available linking headroom. The share structure, not the fragment count, is what AssA prices: 5.75 predicted fragments per ground-truth identity but only 2.40 carrying >=5% of it, with the largest holding 0.453 and the second 0.146; tracks shorter than 25 frames are 30.6% of all tracks and 2.3% of all rows.
claims.unit: projected raw GS-AssA under a perfect tracklet linker on our own current detections, SoccerNet-GSR valid split (58 sequences)

claims.method: tools/gsr_assoc_diag.py rebuilds HOTA's own association score A(i,g)=n/(N_g+M_i-n) from a greedy nearest-GT assignment at the evaluator's 5 m tolerance, then re-scores three counterfactuals (perfect link / perfect detection / both). Validated against the official scorer's per-sequence loc_assoc GS-AssA: Spearman +0.971 over 58 sequences, constant scale factor 1.083, which is the factor used to put the counterfactual on the measured scale.
caveats: assa_hat is a greedy per-frame one-to-one proxy at a hard 5 m gate; trackeval runs a Hungarian assignment over a Gaussian similarity averaged across alphas. Read counterfactual levels as +-2 AssA points, not to the decimal.

The 67.9 ceiling is conditional on our current detections and calibration; it is not a claim that a linker exists which can reach it. GTA_LINK_STAGE1 measured PRTreID within-identity cosine p90 0.093 against cross-identity p10 0.040-0.083, i.e. the appearance signal that would have to drive it is already overlapping.

claims.statement: NEGATIVE ON THE PREMISE -- the FOOTPASS stride/tracker lever does not exist on SoccerNet-GSR. The GSR extraction already runs at sample_every=1 (every one of the 750 frames), so there is no stride to lower; the ByteTrack knobs FOOTPASS found worth +0.259 tracked recall were measured at stride 5 (200 ms gaps) and at stride 1 the same table gives them +0.0135 recall for WORSE fragmentation (1.16 -> 1.23). Crowding and camera motion carry no signal either: Spearman against per-sequence measured GS-AssA is +0.004 for ground-truth people per frame and -0.138 for median per-frame ground-truth box displacement.

claims.statement: A silent, gate-passing calibration failure discards 14.4% of all SoccerNet-GSR valid ground-truth player rows that we had ALREADY detected and tracked: image-space coverage of GT players is 0.843 but pitch-space coverage is only 0.745, 25.0% of frames emit no pitch position at all, and 8 of 58 valid sequences emit one on under half their frames. It is not a rejected calibration -- on SNGS-034's 645 dead frames the keypoint reprojection error is 0.365 m median, BETTER than on its 102 live frames (0.434 m), so MAX_REPROJ_ERROR_M=2.0 passes them; the homography is self-consistent on the pitch keypoints and still projects every player more than 2 m outside the touchline, where clamp_to_pitch NaNs them. claims.statement: The goalkeeper->team link does NOT reopen via a trained PRTreID embedding, so the ~+2.4 GS-HOTA side-resolver path named in docs/CLUSTER_RUNBOOK.md S4b stays shut. The CONTROL on the very same clusters separates outfield teams at 0.9128-0.9637 purity (n=16776), so the machinery is sound and the keeper failure is real. A goalkeeper's kit is required to differ from both outfield kits, so appearance similarity to outfield players carries no usable team signal for keepers -- future GK->team work needs geometry/position or an explicitly GK-aware objective, not kit similarity.

claims.statement: Two independent architectures now agree that SoccerNet-GSR train (57 clips, 20,067 crops, 1343 identities) is too small to build a competitive identity embedding from a generic initialisation. The gate caught it immediately: the evaluator read 35.31 identity mAP instead of 56.93, and reached 56.91 once fixed. Re-running the GK probes under RGB changed EVERY number and flipped the ordering between two models. The verdict of prtreid-003 survives -- no embedding links keepers to teams above the majority floor -- but its 'anti-informative' mechanism claim does not, and has been corrected.
