The 21.6-point shortfall localised to input channel order by reading FeatureExtractor.__call__, which branches on input type. All session-1 GK probes were then re-run with the channel order corrected.
caveats: The bug affected only probes that passed cv2 arrays (the two GK probes and the first evaluator attempt). Session 1's training runs and their valid evaluations went through prtreid's own dataloader and are unaffected -- the floor, run 1, probe 1 and probe 2 numbers all stand.
The corrected GK figures are in CLUSTER_SESSION1.md S10a/S10b; the withdrawn ones are recorded there too rather than deleted.

claims.statement: Scaling the identity corpus clears the shipped PRTreID floor, confirming clip-s3-002's inference. Merging GSR train (20,067 crops / 1,343 ids) with SoccerNet re-ID train (140,003 crops / 58,697 ids) gives 160,070 crops over 60,040 identities -- 44.7x the identities -- and the SAME CLIP ViT-B/16 + heads recipe that peaked at 53.75 on GSR alone reaches valid identity mAP 58.75 with R1 76.70, against the floor's 56.93 / 73.95. That is +1.82 mAP and +2.75 R1 over the floor and +5.00 mAP over the GSR-only run, from the same code with a different manifest. It is a plateau, not a spike: epochs 6/8/10/12 read 58.00 / 58.75 / 58.53 / 58.41, so even the unselected final epoch clears the floor by +1.48, and the overfitting decay that defined the GSR-only run (peak epoch 10 of 40, decaying to 49.32) is gone. Team mAP is marginally sacrificed at the identity optimum (77.3-78.0 vs 78.17) and peaks earlier at 81.81 (epoch 2) and 78.72 (epoch 4).
claims.unit: best valid-split identity mAP, CLIP ViT-B/16 + heads on the unified GSR + sn-reid corpus (shipped PRTreID floor 56.93; same recipe on GSR alone 53.75)
evidence: results/CLUSTER_SESSION3.md#3. Arm (a) -- CLIP ViT-B/16 + heads on the unified set
claims.method: sn-reid train fetched and verified (12,112,383,260 B, 248,234 crops, 290 matches), merged with the GSR crop manifest by filename parse only. 12-epoch run, batch 128, bf16, 2 frozen epochs then last 6 CLIP blocks at lr 1e-5 against heads at 1e-3, cosine LR; 41 min on one shared A100. Scored every 2 epochs on the full 58-video GSR valid split (query 2845 / gallery 11376) with the session-2 evaluator, which reproduces the floor to within 0.02 mAP.
caveats: The within-run eval series spans 58.00-58.75, so the honest interval for the gain over the floor is about +1.1 to +1.8, not +1.82 as a point estimate.
Best-epoch numbers are selected on the same valid split they are reported on. The unselected final epoch reads 58.41 and is the number to quote if only one is allowed.

Team mAP is NOT strictly preserved at the identity optimum: 77.45 at epoch 8 vs the 78.17 floor. Epoch 4 (56.17 identity / 78.72 team) is the balanced compromise if both axes must clear simultaneously.
This is re-ID mAP on a crop-retrieval protocol, NOT GS-HOTA; it does not license any comparison against Broadcast2Pitch Table 5's 60.13.
Valid split only -- no test-split run and no submission. One seed, one recipe.

sn-reid identities are within-action only, so cross-action crops of the same real player are separate classes (false negatives). Mild for this within-video eval protocol; would matter much more for long-horizon naming.

claims.statement: SoccerNet re-ID's data shape forces two departures from the documented GSR crop law, both load-bearing. (a) Its identities are same-action CROSS-VIEW PAIRS, not tracklets: over 150,803 identities the crops-per-id histogram is 92,106 with 1, 43,480 with 2, 10,541 with 3, and only 4,676 with 4 or more. Applying the GSR law's min-4-samples-per-id would discard 91% of the corpus (21,420 of 248,234 crops), so min_per_id=2 is the correct operating point -- it keeps every identity that has a genuine positive pair and drops only the 92,106 singletons, which can contribute no positive. (b) Its jersey field must be used ASYMMETRICALLY: a letter means the number is invisible in EVERY frame of the action, which is a sound per-crop no-number label (78,895 crops -> abstention class), whereas a number only means 'visible at least once in the action' and is NOT valid for the crop in hand, so it is ignored (61,108 crops) rather than used. A third finding corrects the repo sweep: the filename's clazz field encodes role AND team side together (Player_team_left, Goalkeeper_team_right, Main_referee, Side_referee, Staff_members), so sn-reid supervises identity, role and team, not identity alone.
claims.unit: correct min-samples-per-id for SoccerNet re-ID (GSR's documented law uses 4; at 4, 91% of the sn-reid corpus is discarded)
claims.method: Full scan of the 248,234 extracted sn-reid train crops by filename only (no image opened), using sn-reid's own extract_sample_info field split. Crops-per-identity histogram computed over all identities passing the 30 px size floor; clazz vocabulary counted directly.
caveats: Measured on the train split only (290 matches); valid/test/challenge were not fetched because the evaluation is the GSR valid split.

The jersey asymmetry is a design decision justified by the label semantics, not an ablation -- using the numeric labels anyway was never measured, so the cost of the discarded 61,108 labels is unknown.
The trailing filename size field is HxW, not WxH as the schema docstring suggests; our size floor is symmetric so nothing downstream depended on it.

claims.statement: prtreid / sn-gamestate's training stack cannot ingest SoccerNet re-ID data without replacing its sampler AND its loss, so the planned 'fine-tune the shipped PRTreID checkpoint on a larger corpus' arm is blocked. Five distinct structural failures were hit in sequence, four fixed and the fifth not: (1) the dataset class must expose get_masks_config; (2) it must expose a column_mapping of int->str inverse maps for the sampler; (3) PrtreidSampler is TEAM-AWARE and needs >=2 identities per (video, team) bucket, while sn-reid actions often have exactly 1; (4) this fork's RandomIdentitySampler is also camid-scoped and needs >= batch/num_instances (16) identities per camid; (5) GiLt's part_averaged_triplet_loss returns None for the resulting batch composition, at num_instances 2 and 4 alike. The stack assumes GSR's shape throughout -- long tracklets, many identities per video, team-balanced batches from one match. Our own trainer, which assumes nothing beyond (crop, labels), ingested the identical corpus with no change at all.
claims.unit: distinct structural incompatibilities hit when feeding SoccerNet re-ID crops to prtreid's training engine (4 fixed, the 5th unresolved at timebox)
evidence: results/CLUSTER_SESSION3.md#6. Arm (b) -- WALL: prtreid's training stack cannot ingest cross-view-pair data
claims.method: Wrote a prtreid ImageDataset shim serving the unified manifest for training and the persisted GSR valid split for query/gallery, then ran their own engine (build_torchreid_model_engine + engine.run) at probe-1's gentle-LR recipe. Each failure was diagnosed from the traceback and fixed until failure 5, then timeboxed.
caveats: Failure 5 was not root-caused, only reproduced at two sampler settings; a deeper read of GiLt_loss might yield a sixth fix. The claim is that the arm is not a config change, not that it is impossible.
Consequence: no second-architecture confirmation of clip-s3-005 exists. The corpus-scaling result rests on the CLIP arm alone.

claims.statement: The session-3 CLIP encoder's crop-retrieval advantage converts to GS-HOTA, but weakly and not significantly. Swapping ONLY the appearance embedder into the frozen v4 pipeline (row-identical per-detection caches; every other stage byte-identical) moves held-out valid TEST-38 GS-HOTA from 36.7090 to 37.0344, +0.33, with the control re-derived in the same harness and reproducing its on-record 36.71 exactly. The gain is entirely association -- GS-AssA 55.8787 -> 57.2018 (+1.32) against GS-DetA 24.1180 -> 23.9789 (-0.14) -- which is exactly where a better appearance embedding must act, so the mechanism checks out. The significance does not: paired over 38 sequences the mean is +0.5719 and the median +0.3941, but 23 helped against 15 hurt, the worst sequence loses 4.38, and Wilcoxon gives p = 0.0629. +1.82 crop-retrieval mAP (clip-s3-005) therefore buys about a third of a GS-HOTA point, damped because the connector consumes tracklet-MEAN embeddings, because GS-DetA is untouched by this swap, and because the metric rewards more merging almost regardless of precision.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA points on held-out valid TEST-38 from swapping PRTreID for the session-3 CLIP encoder in the frozen v4 pipeline (37.0344 vs a re-derived 36.7090 control)
evidence: results/CLUSTER_SESSION4.md#5. Valid TEST-38 -- the verification, once
results/CLUSTER_SESSION4.md#6. Why crop mAP converted so weakly
claims.method: tools/clip_embedder.py implements PrtreidEmbedder's exact contract, so generator.gta_link.detection_embeddings runs unchanged and only the 256 floats per row differ; verified row-identical (track_ids and frames match element-for-element). Connector tau retuned on DEV-20 only and frozen (results/gsr_v5_frozen.json, declared before the TEST-38 run, checkpoint hashed), then TEST-38 run exactly once with the v4 control re-derived rather than quoted.
caveats: PENDING, not confirmed: Wilcoxon p = 0.0629 over the 38 paired sequences does not clear the conventional 0.05 bar. 15 of 38 sequences got worse, one by 4.38 GS-HOTA.

The recipe is knowingly HALF-TUNED: the solver's appearance term (app_gain 10.0, sim_none 0.92) is in cosine units fitted to PRTreID and was NOT retuned for the wider CLIP scale (estimated equivalents sim_none ~0.67, app_gain ~3). The +0.33 is a LOWER bound on this embedder, not its optimum.
No official test-49 run was spent, so this is a valid-split result only; it is not a leaderboard number and must not be compared to the 39.02 test figure.
tau was chosen on DEV-20, a 20-sequence tuning split, and TEST-38 is a single verification run at one frozen configuration.

claims.statement: An appearance-embedder swap CANNOT be done without retuning every cosine-scaled knob downstream, and skipping that would have inverted the conclusion. The CLIP embedding space is ~4.8x wider in absolute cosine distance than PRTreID's (DEV-20: within-track p90 0.2311 vs 0.0395, cross-track p10 0.4287 vs 0.0931) while its separation RATIO is comparable, so the GTA connector's absolute merge ceiling tau must scale with it. At the inherited tau=0.080 the CLIP arm scores 32.71 on DEV-20 -- nearly 4 points BELOW the 36.4488 control, with only 77 merges surviving -- and would have read as a decisive failure. Retuned to tau=0.450 the same arm scores 37.0711, +0.62 over the control. The correct tau was predicted as 0.38 from the distance quantiles alone before any sweep (placing 0.080's relative position between within-p90 and cross-p10 onto the new scale), and the measured optimum is a broad plateau: tau 0.320-0.520 all land within 0.18 GS-HOTA.
claims.unit: ratio of CLIP to PRTreID absolute cosine-distance scale on DEV-20 (cross-track p10 0.4287 vs 0.0931); connector tau 0.080 -> 0.450
evidence: results/CLUSTER_SESSION4.md#3. The similarity scale moved ~4.8x -- the whole reason a retune was mandatory
claims.method: Within-track distances measured over consecutive same-track detections and cross-track distances over random detection pairs, on the 20 DEV cache files of each embedding. tau swept over {0.080, 0.250, 0.320, 0.380, 0.450, 0.520} on DEV-20 at the v4 bundle (floor 0.80 + jersey merge gate), each arm re-running the connector, rebuilding bundles and scoring GS-HOTA with the official scorer.
caveats: The DEV GS-HOTA curve flattens rather than turning inside the swept range (0.450 and 0.520 differ by 0.03), so 0.450 is the conservative interior of a plateau, not a sharp argmax.
As in v4, GS-HOTA keeps improving while merge precision falls (0.636 -> 0.548), which is a warning about the metric as much as about the connector.
The same rescaling logic applies to the solver's sim_none/app_gain and was NOT carried out; see clip-s4-001.

claims.statement: Two latent path bugs would have silently mixed two embedding spaces in one run, and both were found by auditing consumers before trusting a number rather than by any test. (a) eval/gsr_identity.py hardcoded the literal 'detembed_cache_prtreid' instead of the module constant, so the GTA connector would have run on CLIP embeddings while the solver's OCR-anchored gallery scored PRTreID ones. (b) tools/gsr_v4.config_key omitted the embedder, so a CLIP arm at tau 0.080 -- a value an on-record PRTreID arm already used -- would have silently reused that arm's cached bundles and submission directory. Both are now resolved through one switch (env GSR_EMBEDDER) that drives the cache subdirectory and the arm key together, with the default contributing no suffix so every on-record artifact name stays byte-identical. Per-detection embeddings were already 256-d on both sides, so no consumer needed a dimension change.
claims.unit: latent embedding-space mixing bugs found and closed before the first scored run
evidence: results/CLUSTER_SESSION4.md#1. The swap is controlled -- and two silent-mixing bugs were closed first
results/CLUSTER_SESSION4.md#8. Repo changes (all additive or default-preserving)
claims.method: Grepped every consumer of the per-detection cache and every directory-naming function in the v4 arm path before running. Row-identity of the two caches verified on SNGS-021 (track_ids and frames equal element-for-element over 5,515 rows), which is what makes the arms a controlled swap rather than merely comparable runs.
caveats: Neither bug was reachable before this session -- the second embedding space is what makes them live -- so this is a latent-defect finding, not a retraction of any on-record number.

The fixes are default-preserving by construction but no regression test pins that; the evidence is that targeted tests stay green (22 passed, 1 skipped) and the default CACHE_SUBDIR string is unchanged.

claims.statement: Fine-tuning the pipeline's detector on SoccerNet-GSR train is a large BOX win and a ROLE regression, and the role half blocks it. The pipeline's detector is a YOLOv8s (11,137,148 params, classes {0 ball, 1 goalkeeper, 2 player, 3 referee}, HF uisikdag/yolo-v8-football-players-detection, itself trained 25 epochs at imgsz 800 on a Roboflow set) inferred by generator.extract at ultralytics' default imgsz 640 with person acceptance at DETECT_CONF 0.20. Fine-tuned 10 epochs on all 57 GSR train sequences (42,750 frames, 690,618 person + 40,928 ball boxes) at lr0 0.002 in 32 min on one A100, and evaluated on GSR valid (58 seq, 8,700 frames, 141,512 person GT) through the same evaluator as the control: class-agnostic person precision at conf 0.20 rises 0.7966 -> 0.8891 (+9.25) and recall at MATCHED precision 0.9031 -> 0.9270 (+2.40), better precision on 55/58 sequences. But role-correct coverage of GT persons falls 0.8404 -> 0.7384 (-10.20) because 20,142 ground-truth players are classed 'referee' (control: 644). Since eval/gsr_score.py writes the detector class straight into the submission's attributes.role AND nulls the team attribute for non-player/GK roles, one class error costs two GS-HOTA-gated attributes. Pre-declared gate (recall at matched precision +2.0 OR mAP@0.5 +3.0) is MET on the first criterion; the recommendation is still NO re-extract, because the gate as written omitted role.
claims.unit: points of role-correct coverage of GT persons lost on GSR valid (0.8404 -> 0.7384), against +2.40 points of person recall at matched precision gained
evidence: results/CLUSTER_SESSION5A.md#7 GATE VERDICT -- met, and the recommendation is still no
claims.method: Server-side (a100server1, GPU 1). ~/work/det/build_det_data.py converts Labels-GameState.json to YOLO txt using the detector's own class ids; ~/work/det/train_det_ft.py fine-tunes from the shipped weights at imgsz 640 / batch 64 / SGD lr0 0.002 / warmup 1 / close_mosaic 3 / 10 epochs; ~/work/det/det_eval.py runs BOTH ultralytics model.val (box mAP) and a class-agnostic PERSON evaluator (union of goalkeeper|player|referee, exactly generator.extract's selection) matching greedily by confidence at IoU 0.5, applied identically to the control first and then every fine-tune. Recall at matched precision is read off the fine-tune's PR curve at the control's own operating-point precision.
caveats: The gate was declared before the role decomposition existed and measured only the box. It passed and it was the wrong gate; any re-run must add a role criterion.

Evaluation is the public GSR valid split at frame stride 5, not the withheld official test. No GS-HOTA was scored end to end in this session -- the -10.20 role coverage is an input to GS-DetA, not a measured GS-HOTA delta.
Valid was never trained on, but it is ultralytics' val set, so best.pt is selected on it; the gate was judged on last.pt for that reason (best.pt happened to be epoch 10).

Inference-side resolution is not an alternative lever: the control at imgsz 1280 recovers small players (+14.1 points under 40 px) but collapses on large ones (-30.8 at >=110 px) for a net -9.7 recall.

claims.statement: The detector fine-tune's role collapse is a TRAINING-DIVERSITY failure with a colour mechanism, not a recipe failure. The player->referee leak is bimodal by sequence (median 0.0002, 21 of 58 sequences over 10%) and falls entirely on ONE of the three games in the GSR valid split -- all 21 sequences of game_id 3 -- with BOTH of its teams leaking (left 0.504, right 0.440 of matched players classed referee), while games 2 and 5 (37 sequences) leak zero and gain +5.8 recall / +7.8-12.1 precision. Game 3 is markedly desaturated (mean HSV S 72.4) versus every training game (167.4 / 107.7 / 97.9), so a detector fine-tuned on three saturated games learns saturated kit appearance as the player signature and dumps washed-out players into the neutral-coloured class. Raising hue/saturation/value augmentation (hsv_h 0.015->0.3, hsv_s 0.7->0.9, hsv_v 0.4->0.6) confirms the mechanism and only partly fixes it: mAP@0.5 goes 0.4950 -> 0.5532 (+5.29 over the 0.5003 control, i.e. it flips a loss into a clear win and clears BOTH gate criteria), recall at matched precision +2.73, the leak drops 20,142 -> 14,989 (-27%) and game-3's rate 0.477 -> 0.348 -- but role-correct coverage is still 0.7799, 6.05 points below the control. Neither per-track majority voting over GROUND-TRUTH tracks (which makes it worse: 0.8090 -> 0.8053 plain, 0.8460 -> 0.8319 colour) nor relabelling every predicted referee as player (0.8256 / 0.8335, both below 0.8404) recovers it. 57 GSR train clips = 3 games is not enough visual diversity -- the same corpus wall sessions 1-3 hit for identity.
claims.unit: points of box mAP@0.5 gained over the control by the colour-hardened fine-tune (0.5532 vs 0.5003), while role-correct coverage stays 6.05 points below it
evidence: results/CLUSTER_SESSION5A.md#6 Diagnosis: it is one game, both teams, and the mechanism is colour
results/CLUSTER_SESSION5A.md#8 Follow-up run -- colour-hardened augmentation confirms the mechanism and does not fix it
results/CLUSTER_SESSION5A.md#5a The leak is not epoch-dependent
claims.method: ~/work/det/role_vote.py matches detections to GT annotations carrying track_id and role, then reports role accuracy per detection and after a majority vote over GROUND-TRUTH tracks (an oracle-association upper bound), plus the per-sequence player->referee rate; sequences are grouped by info.game_id from Labels-GameState.json. Team-side split re-runs inference over game 3 only, bucketing matched GT players by their attributes.team. Colour statistics are mean HSV over frame 000100 of six sequences per game. The colour-hardened run is identical to the gated run (same seed, same 10 epochs, same lr) except the three hsv_* values.
caveats: The leak is present after ONE epoch and flat thereafter, so no early-stopped checkpoint carries the box gain without the role loss.
Game 3 has both a desaturated broadcast AND unseen kits; the two are not separated here, so 'colour' is the best-supported mechanism rather than an isolated cause.
The proposed fix (SoccerNet-v3 boxes, 400 games / 6 leagues, MIT) is untested and needs a ~60 GB fetch with Sid's per-fetch approval.

The ball class also changed a lot (mAP@0.5 0.0581 -> 0.2065); no ball-track validation was run, so the ball-metric rule (only the post-link_ball usable track counts) means that gain must not be quoted as ball coverage.

claims.statement: Two knobs on top of the v3 (calibgate) recipe lift the official SoccerNet-GSR test-49 score from GS-HOTA 35.3991 to 39.0215 (+3.62): the jersey-aggregation floor moves 0.85 -> 0.80 (read density d 0.2621 -> 0.3243 at read precision 0.868 -> 0.810) and the GTA connector runs at tau 0.080 instead of 0.040 behind a new jersey-compatibility merge gate that forbids merging two tracklets whose confident reads disagree. Nothing else changes: same positions, same solver config, same free team map, same self roster, no GPU artifact touched. GS-DetA 24.02 -> 26.47, GS-AssA 52.18 -> 57.53, GS-LocA 93.400 -> 93.595 (up, not paid), IDF1 34.09 -> 40.03. Paired per sequence n=49: mean +3.41, median +3.00, helped 43, hurt 6, worst -2.96, Wilcoxon p=8.6e-10. On valid TEST-38 the same frozen bundle scores 36.7090 against v3's 34.0028 (+2.71, 31 helped / 7 hurt, p=8.7e-06). Both controls were re-derived inside the same runs and reproduce their on-record numbers at every printed digit. Zero ground-truth reads in the prediction chain (0 legitimacy violations over 424654 predictions); the shipped zip re-scores to itself at every digit.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA on the official SoccerNet-GSR test split (49 sequences), GT-free recipe at the frozen v4 bundle (v3 baseline 35.3991)
evidence: results/GSR_V4.md#8 The one test run -- official test-49 GS-HOTA 35.3991 -> 39.0215
results/GSR_V4.md#7 Valid TEST-38 -- the verification run
results/GSR_V4.md#1 Component table -- DEV-20, one variable at a time
claims.method: tools.gsr_v4: --dev scores each candidate arm on the declared valid DEV-20 through one harness (24 arms, component-alone and in combination), --freeze pre-declares the winning bundle (results/gsr_v4_frozen.json, written 02:02:32 -- before the TEST-38 run at 02:17 and the test-49 run at 02:36), --valid and --test each run once and re-derive the v3 control rather than quoting it. The aggregation rules themselves were frozen on 2026-07-28 by results/ocr_density_rule.json and were not refitted here. CPU only: the frozen bundle moves no GPU-side knob, so every cached test-49 artifact is consumed unchanged.
caveats: The 0.80 aggregation floor is a BENCHMARK-ONLY adoption. It destroys facts-grade identity coverage: coverage at jersey precision 0.85 collapses from 0.2693 to 0.0013 on DEV-20 and from 0.3118 to 0.0282 on valid TEST-38. Anything reporting per-player facts must keep the shipped 0.85-floor rule; results/ocr_density_rule.json is unchanged and the benchmark arm writes its own votes directory.

Merge precision falls to 0.771 on test-49 (0.636 on DEV-20) against the 80% bar GTA_LINK_STAGE1 A4 set for any solver consuming merged tracklets. GS-HOTA rewards the trade because AssA's fragmentation penalty outweighs the contamination; the facts chain must not inherit tau 0.080 without its own validator.

tau was chosen from 10 swept values on 20 DEV sequences and the DEV curve is still rising at tau 0.250 (merge precision 0.495 there). 0.080 is the conservative end of the flat region, not the argmax. Honest interval for the bundle: +2.5 to +3.6 GS-HOTA (DEV +3.62, valid-38 +2.71, test-49 +3.62).

On test-49 coverage@0.85 moves the OTHER way (0.4342 -> 0.4707) because that split's precision curve happens to clear the floor. The facts decision rests on the two pessimistic measurements (DEV and valid-38), not on this one.
The digit-confusion-prior refit was measured and dropped: worth +0.49 GS-HOTA at tau 0.040 and -0.005 at tau 0.080, so the shipped solver config stays byte-identical to v3's.
SNGS-190's team-side coin-flip is untouched and remains the largest single-sequence risk.
Nothing has been uploaded to codabench. 39.02 is a locally-scored number on the official split with the official scorer.

claims.statement: The crop_scale 1.25 OCR widening -- worth 1.37x reads at held precision on our three ManU EPL matches and 2.3x on FOOTPASS game_18 -- does NOTHING on SoccerNet-GSR, and the reason is that it was never a property of jersey OCR. Measured on 67224 exactly-paired DEV-20 crops (same tracks, same sampled frames, same detections; 67224 shared (track_id, frame) keys, zero unmatched): confident reads (p_number >= 0.99) 7220 -> 7264 = 1.006x, legibility >= 0.5 12814 -> 11433 = 0.892x, 1189 reads gained and 1145 lost, and 6057 of the 6075 crops both arms read confidently return the identical number. Read density d FALLS 0.2218 -> 0.2137 at the shipped 0.85 floor (precision 0.8678 -> 0.8690) and 0.3026 -> 0.2939 at the 0.80 floor; the full solver arm loses 0.38 GS-HOTA on DEV-20 (32.8276 -> 32.4472). The mechanism: on our broadcast the OCR crop is RECONSTRUCTED by generator.team_anchor.estimate_player_box, measured at 0.814x the annotated player height, and x1.25 repairs that undersizing; on GSR eval.gsr_jersey.extract_track_crops crops the football detector's own xyxy, so there is nothing to repair and the multiplier only adds background.
claims.unit: ratio of confident per-crop jersey reads at crop_scale 1.25 vs 1.0, 67224 exactly-paired GSR DEV-20 crops (EPL measured 1.36x at crop level, 1.37x in d)
claims.method: eval.gsr_jersey --percrop --max-crops 60 --crop-scale 1.25 --variant _w125 over the 20 DEV sequences (GPU, 51 min), then tools.gsr_v4 --cropscale for the paired crop/tracklet comparison and tools.gsr_v4 --dev for the downstream solver arm. Crop selection is deterministic from the cached positions table, so the two passes are paired at the crop level rather than sampled.
caveats: DEV-20 only; the 38 valid TEST sequences and the 49 test sequences were never run at 1.25, because the DEV read-level result is a null and the downstream arm is negative.

This does not retract ident-031 or the EPL/game_18 measurements -- it bounds them. The 1.25 constant calibrates one crop ESTIMATOR and must not be transferred to a pipeline that crops from real detector boxes.
A narrower crop on GSR was not tested.

claims.statement: The truncation-aware digit prior proposed by OCR_DOMAIN_SHIFT (where 44.2% of wrong confident FOOTPASS game_18 reads are exactly the first digit of the true 2-digit number, the '81 -> 8' mode) was NOT built, because the mechanism is absent on SoccerNet-GSR. Measured on GSR DEV-20 reads before any code was written: at the shipped 0.85 floor 46 of 348 graded reads are wrong, 8 are length mismatches and only 3 (6.5% of wrong) are truncations; at the 0.80 floor 88 of 464 wrong, 18 length mismatches, 7 truncations (8.0%). 74.9% of GSR's auditable GT jerseys are 2-digit (2658 of 3549), so the opportunity exists and the reader simply does not take it -- the dominant GSR error is digit substitution on both positions (42->62 x14, 11->17 x9, 13->33 x8). Fitting a truncation parameter on 3 observations would be worse than not having one, and the confusion prior it would live inside is worth -0.005 GS-HOTA at the v4 operating point.
claims.unit: share of wrong confident GSR DEV-20 jersey reads that are a truncation (prefix) of the true number, shipped 0.85-floor rule (FOOTPASS game_18: 0.442)
evidence: results/OCR_DOMAIN_SHIFT.md#3.1 The mechanism: 2-digit shirt numbers truncate
claims.method: tools.gsr_v4 --trunc-probe: grades every emitted (track, number) read of the 20 DEV sequences against the dominant GT jersey of that track under both frozen aggregation rules, and classifies each error as a substitution, a length mismatch, or a truncation (the read is a prefix of the true number). CPU, seconds.
caveats: DEV-20 only, and the truncation counts are small (3 and 7) -- which is the finding, not a limitation of it.
This does not contradict ident-029: truncation is a domain property of FOOTPASS's soft 4.8 Mbps Constrained-Baseline Serie A encode, and GSR's own encode does not produce it.

claims.statement: The GTA connector's linking ceiling DID rise on the calibration-repaired positions, answering the half of GSR_ASSOCIATION negative #7 that was measurable. On the repaired positions (20.7% more pitch rows, so the connector's speed/reachability constraint has far more geometry) every tau from 0.045 to 0.250 beats the on-record 0.040 on DEV-20 and tau 0.030 is measurably WORSE (-0.58 GS-HOTA, 6 helped / 13 hurt, p=0.027) -- the tighter direction is wrong once the positions are repaired. A new jersey-compatibility merge gate (generator.gta_link.connect(..., numbers=): two components that both carry a confident read and disagree may never merge, whatever appearance says) restores merge precision at every tau (0.040: 0.766 -> 0.786; 0.050: 0.726 -> 0.741; 0.060: 0.659 -> 0.680; 0.080: 0.612 -> 0.636) and is worth +0.09 GS-HOTA at the tight tau it is not needed at and +1.47 at tau 0.080, which is the point of it: it is an appearance-orthogonal gate that lets a looser tau be spent. At the frozen tau 0.080 the connector makes 1253 merges on test-49 at 77.1% precision against v3's 650 at 86.8%, and fragments per GT identity fall 5.51 -> 4.97.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA gained on valid DEV-20 by the jersey-compatibility merge gate at connector tau 0.080 (34.4734 with, 33.0041 without; +0.09 at tau 0.040)
evidence: results/GSR_V4.md#4 Component 3 -- the linking ceiling did rise on repaired positions
results/GSR_V4.md#1.2 The shape check that decided tau
claims.method: tools.gsr_v4 --dev sweeps tau in {0.030, 0.040, 0.045, 0.050, 0.060, 0.070, 0.080, 0.100, 0.150, 0.250} with the gate on and off, each arm re-running the connector, rebuilding the solver bundles at the matching partition, and scoring GS-HOTA with the official scorer. Merge precision is the GT-audited generator.track_relink.merge_precision the connector already reports.
caveats: The DEV GS-HOTA curve does not turn inside the swept range: 0.080 = 36.44 and 0.250 = 36.90 at merge precision 0.636 and 0.495. tau 0.080 is frozen as the conservative end of the flat region, not the argmax. That GS-HOTA still rises when half the merges join two different players is a warning about the metric as much as about the connector.

The linking CEILING itself (tools.gsr_assoc_diag --diag on the repaired positions) was still not re-measured, so how much headroom remains at tau 0.080 is unknown. GSR_ASSOCIATION negative #7 is half-answered.
Merge precision at the frozen point is below the 80% bar GTA_LINK_STAGE1 A4 set for the facts chain.

claims.statement: The shipped Koshkina/PARSeq jersey reader is BEATEN on its own chain by a PARSeq fine-tune whose only added ingredient is a legibility-filtered SoccerNet-v3 digit corpus. Through an identical harness -- same shipped ResNet34 legibility gate at 0.5, same pose torso RoI, same decode fold, uniform last.ckpt rule -- arm 4t reads 0.8344 per-crop precision at emit 0.2761 over the 4,965 numbered-GT DEV-20 crops, against the incumbent's 0.7022 at emit 0.2759. That is +0.1322 precision at equal coverage, and it clears the pre-declared dominance gate on BOTH axes. The harness is validated, not assumed: replaying the shipped chain through it reproduces the published DEV-20 figures exactly (1,370 reads, emit 0.2759, precision 0.7022 vs the recorded 0.7029 -- one crop, from re-encoding torso JPEGs). Secondary criterion, jersey-2023 test tracklet accuracy: arm 4t 0.8365 vs incumbent 0.8084 on the same harness (+2.81, and +3.97 on the 856 numbered tracklets), but BOTH fall short of Koshkina's published 0.874 -- a harness-reproduction gap (no occlusion/outlier removal, no re-ID Gaussian fitting), not an arm regression, since it also fails for the very checkpoint that published 87.4.
claims.unit: per-crop jersey precision on DEV-20 numbered-GT GT crops at emit 0.2761 (incumbent 0.7022 at emit 0.2759)
evidence: results/CLUSTER_SESSION_S2.md#3.1 The harness, validated by exact reproduction
claims.method: Server a100server1, GPU 1. ~/work/jersey/dev20_arm.py scores one (legibility x PARSeq) arm over the 7,055 DEV-20 GT crops (20 sequences = every 3rd of the sorted 58 valid, per eval.gsr_identity.split_sequences), of which 4,965 carry a GT number. The pose torso RoI is built ONCE by ~/work/jersey/dev20_torso.py and shared by every arm, so only the swapped weights move. Arm 4t = PARSeq from Koshkina's shipped SoccerNet fine-tune, 25 epochs on plus_v3_torso (75,154 train / 3,955 val crops: jersey-2023 + GSR-train + SoccerNet-v3, all legibility-filtered at 0.7, then pose torso-cropped). Decode matches tools/koshkina_str_sidecar.py and generator.jersey_id.parseq_positions_to_probs verbatim.
caveats: DEV-20 only. TEST-38 confirmation is not done and is S3's job.

Arm 1 (legibility retrain) was NOT run -- the sn-reid negatives component was not resolvable from verifiable assets. Emit rate is still the SHIPPED legibility model's, so the dominance is on the precision axis with coverage held fixed.

The jersey-2023 secondary number is from a simplified reproduction of Koshkina's tracklet chain (100 crops/tracklet sampled, top 30 by legibility, majority vote at min_conf 0.30); it reproduces the incumbent at 0.8084, not the published 0.874.
An earlier full-body variant (arm 4, 0.7330) also passed but geometry-asymmetrically; arm 4t supersedes it and needs no pipeline geometry change.

claims.statement: SoccerNet-v3 is the ENTIRE effect behind the jersey-reader gain, and the S1 synthetic digit pretrain is not. Holding corpus, harness, emit rate and checkpoint rule fixed, adding the legibility-filtered v3 digit crops moves DEV-20 per-crop precision from 0.4252 to 0.7330 (+0.3078) against a synthetic-initialised control, and from 0.4469 to 0.7330 (+0.2861) against a shipped-initialised one. The same experiment prices S1 NEGATIVELY as an initialisation: synthetic init 0.4252 vs shipped init 0.4469 on the identical planned corpus, -0.0217. S1's 0.9826 synthetic-holdout accuracy (worth +25.99 points over the base STR checkpoint's 0.7226 on that holdout) therefore does NOT transfer into a better starting point for the real corpus, and arm 4t was built from the shipped init instead. The v3 gain is not a vocabulary artifact: the planned corpus already covers 44 distinct numbers against DEV-20's 35-37 (v3 takes it to 89).
claims.unit: DEV-20 per-crop precision added by the v3 corpus at identical emit (0.4252 -> 0.7330)
claims.method: Four PARSeq arms, 25 epochs each, batch 128, max_label_length 2, uniform last.ckpt rule: (2) synthetic init x planned, (3) shipped init x planned, (4) synthetic init x planned+v3, (4t) shipped init x planned+v3 in torso geometry. Arms 2/3/4 are compared in full-body geometry (their training geometry) at a common emit of 0.2866; the synthetic-vs-shipped init comparison (arm 2 vs arm 3) is like-for-like in corpus, geometry and emit.
caveats: The v3 delta is measured in full-body geometry (arms 2/3/4). Arm 4t re-confirms the level in torso geometry but there is no torso-geometry no-v3 control, so the exact +0.31 is a full-body number.
Single seed per arm; no repeats, so small deltas like the -0.0217 init effect are indicative rather than significant. The v3 effect (+0.29 to +0.31) is far outside any plausible seed noise.

n=4965 assumes the arm-2/3/4 emit rate (0.2866) is computed over the same 4,965 numbered-GT DEV-20 crops as the incumbent bar (section 3.1); CLUSTER_SESSION_S2.md does not restate the denominator for the full-body arms explicitly.

claims.statement: SoccerNet-v3's per-box jersey `ID` field IS the jersey number (verified against pixels: 40 crops from a held-out game, every legible shirt matched its label), giving 106,591 digit-valued labels over 400 games and 6 leagues -- roughly 5x our previous per-crop digit corpus (GSR train, 20,067 crops from 3 matches). But the labels are per-player-WITHIN-ACTION, not per-crop-legible: the annotator carried identity across an action, so a label persists on crops where the player is facing away from his own number. Running the shipped ResNet34 legibility classifier over all 105,702 extracted digit crops shows the scale of that: at threshold 0.7 only 45,620 survive -- **56.8% of v3's digit labels sit on crops with no visible number**. Unfiltered they would be an identity-shortcut generator rather than digit supervision, which is exactly campaign risk #2. Visual inspection of both sides confirms the filter is behaving and is conservative (some faint-but-readable numbers are discarded).
claims.unit: share of SoccerNet-v3 digit-labelled crops carrying NO visible number (60,082 of 105,702)
evidence: results/CLUSTER_SESSION_S2.md#1.2 The ID field is the jersey number
claims.method: ~/work/jersey/v3_crops.py cuts every Player/Goalkeeper box with a 1-2 digit ID from the 400 v3 games (105,702 crops; 889 dropped below 40 px height), streaming one game's zip at a time. ~/work/jersey/legibility.py runs the shipped legibility_resnet34_soccer_20240215.pth with the pipeline's exact preprocessing (Resize 256x256, ImageNet normalisation) and sweeps the threshold.
caveats: The 56.8% is the legibility MODEL's opinion, not human ground truth; the visual check is a 40-crop sample, not an annotated audit.
Threshold 0.7 is the coordinator-set operating point, not a tuned optimum; the sweep (0.3 -> 0.9 keeps 49.7% -> 35.7%) is recorded so it can be revisited.

claims.statement: The Koshkina chain's pose-confidence gate in generator/jersey_id.py is DEAD CODE. `_write_torso_crops` passes `out["keypoints"][0]` to `torso_from_keypoints`, whose third channel is torchvision KeypointRCNN's visibility PLACEHOLDER (always 1.0), not a confidence -- the per-joint scores live in the separate `keypoints_scores` tensor. So the `_POSE_CONF = 0.4` test never rejects, and a torso RoI is produced whenever a person box is detected at all. Discovered while porting the chain server-side: substituting sigmoid(keypoints_scores) made the harness STRICTER than the chain that set the 0.7029 bar and under-emitted against it (1,335 reads vs 1,370; torso rate 0.7821 vs 0.8333). Matching upstream verbatim reproduced the bar exactly. FLAGGED, NOT FIXED: every incumbent number on record was measured with the gate inert, so activating it is a separate, re-baselining decision rather than a bug fix.
claims.unit: share of DEV-20 GT crops receiving a torso RoI with the gate inert (0.7821 if activated)
evidence: results/CLUSTER_SESSION_S2.md#3.1 The harness, validated by exact reproduction
claims.method: Two builds of the DEV-20 torso set over the same 7,055 crops, differing only in whether the keypoint third channel is the visibility placeholder (upstream) or sigmoid(keypoints_scores); each scored end-to-end with the shipped legibility model and shipped PARSeq against the recorded 1,370-read / 0.7029-precision baseline.
caveats: Whether activating the gate would help or hurt end-to-end is UNMEASURED -- only that it currently does nothing and that turning it on cuts torso coverage by ~5 points.

n not stated independently in results/CLUSTER_SESSION_S2.md: the claim's own method text names 7,055 DEV-20 GT crops as the denominator, but that figure does not appear anywhere else in the source doc, so it is recorded as null here rather than re-asserted unverified.

claims.statement: The v5.1 solver retune (app_gain 10.0 -> 3.0, sim_none unchanged at 0.92) buys +0.6118 GS-HOTA on DEV-20 (37.0711 -> 37.6829) but -0.0527 on held-out TEST-38 (37.0344 -> 36.9817, 7 helped / 9 hurt, Wilcoxon p = 0.438). Session 4's sim_none~0.67 estimate for the CLIP-scaled solver is refuted -- 0.67 costs 0.28 GS-HOTA against the inherited 0.92 on DEV-20, which is itself the DEV optimum. DEV-20 cannot support sub-point decisions: only 11 of 20 sequences move at all, and 2 sequences (SNGS-093 +5.50, SNGS-090 +4.44) supply 9.94 of the pooled +13.25 positive DEV delta, i.e. about 75% of the gain. The pre-declared gate (TEST-38 >= 37.2 spends the test-49 run) is NOT met; no test-49 run was spent, no submission built, no GPU booked.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA delta on held-out TEST-38 from the v5.1 solver retune vs the frozen v5 recipe (36.9817 vs 37.0344), against a DEV-20 gain of +0.6118 that did not transfer
claims.method: tools.gsr_v4.solver_config(app_gain=, sim_none=) override swept on DEV-20 (21 arms) with the connector/embedder/positions/jersey stages frozen at v5; best arm (app_gain 3.0, sim_none 0.92) declared and hashed in results/gsr_v5_1_frozen.json before the single TEST-38 verification run against a re-derived v5 control.
caveats: PENDING-style negative reported as the headline, not a footnote: the largest single-knob DEV move available in this recipe (+0.6118) did not survive contact with 38 unseen sequences (p = 0.438).
Gate 37.2 not met; no test-49 spend; public leaderboard number stays the v5/v4 figures (37.03 / 36.71), not v5.1's 36.98.
re-minted 2026-08-05 after the checkout incident; original record lost, statement reconstructed verbatim from the cited documents.

claims.statement: The session-3 CLIP jersey head, tested as a second voter, scores 0.151 precision on the crops where the shipped chain abstains -- worse than Qwen2-VL-2B's 0.265 on the same crops, against a pre-declared floor of 0.80. Neither candidate is usable. The mechanism is diagnosable, not guessed: the head is 0.863 precise per crop on its own training split but collapses to 0.125 on held-out valid sequences built by the same crop builder from the same dataset -- a boundary that changes only which players are in frame -- meaning it learned to recognise a player and recall his number rather than to read digits. Its abstention (no-number) class carries near-zero information: precision 0.318 against a 0.275 base rate is only a 1.16x lift on valid, versus 1.95x on its own training split, confirming the abstention behaviour is also memorised rather than learned.
claims.unit: read precision of the session-3 CLIP jersey head on DEV-20 chain-abstain crops (Qwen 0.265, floor 0.80)
claims.method: 42-way jersey head from outputs/gsr/clip_ckpt/epoch8.pt scored on DEV-20 crops where the shipped Koshkina-chain OCR abstains, against the pre-declared 0.80 second-voter floor set in results/OCR_DENSIFICATION.md #7 (Qwen2-VL-2B baseline 0.265). Train-vs-valid collapse measured on crops built by the identical crop builder from the identical dataset, split only by sequence.
caveats: REJECT verdict: the football-trained head is 0.11 worse than the generic VLM it was meant to beat on the same 0.80 bar; the second-voter question is closed for both trained-head and VLM candidates for now.
The 1.16x abstention lift and 0.125 read precision are both measured against same-subset baselines (0.275 base rate; 0.102 modal-number baseline), not chance alone.
re-minted 2026-08-05 after the checkout incident; original record lost, statement reconstructed verbatim from the cited documents.

claims.statement: The S2 retrained PARSeq reader (arm 4t) clears the pre-declared S3 tracklet gate on both floors, measured on DEV-20 GSR jersey GT with an identical 1,596-track denominator: read density d = 0.4148 at read precision 0.8228 (gate: d >= 0.35 at prec >= 0.80; incumbent 0.3026 at 0.8103) and d = 0.3872 at precision 0.8620 (gate: d >= 0.26 at prec >= 0.85; incumbent 0.2218 at 0.8678). d = 0.4148 is the first measurement in this project to clear the EVIDENCE_DENSITY_LAW target of d = 0.347. The comparison is paired at the CROP, not sampled: crop extraction, the ResNet34 legibility gate and the KeypointRCNN torso RoI all run upstream of PARSeq and are unchanged, so the two evidence caches align 1:1 over 67,224 DEV-20 crops with the legibility score identical to 5 decimals and the torso flag identical on every row -- only the PARSeq weights differ. The mechanism is decisiveness, not just accuracy: at a 0.99 per-crop confidence floor the v6 reader commits to a number on 1.289x as many crops (9,305 vs 7,220), which lets the rule sweep collapse min_votes from 3-5 to 1 while holding precision.
claims.unit: DEV-20 tracklet read density d at read precision >= 0.80 (incumbent 0.3026 at 0.8103; gate 0.35)
claims.method: eval.gsr_jersey --percrop --variant _v6 --max-crops 60 --parseq-ckpt <arm4t> over the 20 DEV sequences (55 min laptop GPU, 60 crops/track matching the on-record cache), then tools.ocr_density --sweep --variant _v6: the same 96-point rule grid and the same pick-highest-d-clearing-the-floor rule used for the on-record freeze, written to a variant-suffixed file so the on-record freeze is untouched.
caveats: The shipped 2024 ResNet34 legibility model is unchanged and is still the binding emit gate: 12,814 of 67,224 DEV-20 crops (19.1%) pass it. CLUSTER_SESSION_S2.md section 4 records that arm 1, the legibility retrain, was never run.

Read precision is graded against the dominant GT jersey per track, so a correct read on the minority identity of a contaminated track is charged as an error -- a floor on true per-read precision, not a point estimate.
DEV-20 only; no TEST-38 or test-49 evidence was scored.

claims.statement: Dropping the S2-retrained PARSeq weights into the shipped chain -- a weights-only swap, with the aggregation rule, connector, solver and association all held at their frozen values -- moves GS-HOTA on the S5-frozen EIoU partition from 39.0820 to 42.7449 (+3.6629) on DEV-20, with 18 of 20 sequences helped, 2 hurt, worst -1.74, best +14.02, Wilcoxon p = 0.00021. The pre-declared DEV gate (>= +1.0 GS-HOTA, >= 12/20 helped, DetA carrying the gain) PASSES on all three criteria, and the DetA criterion emphatically: GS-DetA +4.7592 against GS-AssA +0.5686, i.e. 89% of the movement is detection accuracy, which is what a jersey lever must move under a metric that deletes any detection whose number is wrong. Per-row identity accuracy goes 0.4756 -> 0.5463 and jersey accuracy 0.5302 -> 0.6050 over 190,899 auditable rows. This is the largest single-lever DEV gain of campaign v6. The refactor that carries the swap was verified default-preserving by re-deriving the S5 frozen point through it first: 37.0711 control / 39.0820 arm, matching GSR_EIOU.md to four decimals.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA delta on DEV-20 from the v6 reader swap, on the S5-frozen EIoU base (39.0820 -> 42.7449)
claims.method: tools.gsr_eiou --run --split dev --embedder clip --grid 0.3:1:0.5:0.3 --percrop-variants ',_v6': one invocation crosses the frozen association point with both per-crop OCR variants, so control and arm share the identical relabelling map, positions, embeddings and downstream configuration and differ ONLY in which per-crop parquet supplies the jersey evidence. Aggregation held at the on-record 0.80-floor rule (min_crop_conf 0.90, min_votes 3), tau 0.450, jersey-compatible merge gate on, no confusion refit. Paired per sequence.
caveats: DEV-20 only. No TEST-38 scoring was spent and the test-49 split was not touched; S7 owns the combined freeze. The v5/v5.1 precedent is a DEV win shrinking to +0.33/-0.05 on TEST-38, which is why the gate was sized at +1.0.
The connector tau was not re-swept on the changed evidence, so this is a lower bound on the lever (the GSR_EIOU.md section 8.4 caveat applies unchanged).
The digit-confusion prior was not refit on v6 reads; crop-level agreement with the incumbent is only 0.755 at the 0.50 floor, so the error pattern differs and a refit is an untested S7 candidate.
Two sequences regress (SNGS-090 -1.74, SNGS-033 -0.88).

claims.statement: The aggregation rule that MAXIMISES read density subject to the precision floor is NOT the rule that maximises GS-HOTA, and the gap is worth about a point. On identical v6 evidence and an identical EIoU partition, the v6-swept rule (min_crop_conf 0.50, min_votes 1; d = 0.4148 at read precision 0.8228) scores GS-HOTA 41.8014, while reusing the incumbent's own rule (min_crop_conf 0.90, min_votes 3; d = 0.3139 at read precision 0.9256) scores 42.7449 -- 0.94 LOWER for 32% MORE read tracklets. The denser arm is worse on both terms, DetA -0.71 and GS-AssA actually negative against the control (-0.69), and it names 875 tracklets to the sparser arm's 729 while scoring a lower identity accuracy for them (0.5316 vs 0.5463); mean identities per sequence rises 13.25 -> 16.85 at flat merge precision, i.e. the extra votes split identities across more slots rather than consolidating them. The reason is structural: under GS-HOTA a wrong number is not a missing number -- it deletes a detection that a null would have let match -- so a retrained reader's precision headroom should be banked as precision, not spent on density. The tracklet-density gate and the scored objective disagree about where to sit on the frontier.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA delta on DEV-20 from spending the v6 reader's precision headroom on density (42.7449 -> 41.8014)
claims.method: Two tools.gsr_eiou runs at the same frozen association point on the same _v6 per-crop evidence, differing only in which frozen aggregation rule tools.gsr_v4.rule_for resolves (the on-record freeze vs the variant's own DEV sweep). Both compared to the same EIoU + incumbent-reader control, paired per sequence.
caveats: TENTATIVE: arm B vs arm A is not statistically separated on 20 sequences (paired mean -0.850, 7 helped / 13 hurt, Wilcoxon p = 0.216). The ordering is directional on DEV, not proven.
Both arms clear the pre-declared DEV gate; this claim is about which to ship, not about whether the reader works.
Only two points on the frontier were measured; the optimum may lie between them and was not searched.
status pending: A-vs-B not separated at n=20 (p=0.216); S7's held-out runs decide.

claims.statement: SoccerNet-v3 breadth confirms gsr-det-002's causal claim and nearly closes the role leak -- the S4 gate still FAILS by 0.0004 on its per-game criterion. Fine-tuning the pipeline detector (YOLOv8s, classes {0 ball, 1 goalkeeper, 2 player, 3 referee}) for 10 epochs at lr0 0.002 with 5A's colour-hardened aug (hsv 0.3/0.9/0.6) on a UNION of GSR train (42,750 video frames, 3 games) and SoccerNet-v3 (33,986 stills, 400 games / 6 leagues, 366,081 boxes = 98.52% of v3 kept; Staff/Wall/objects dropped), 1.258:1 GSR:v3, 48 min on one A100, evaluated on GSR valid (58 seq, 8,700 frames, 141,512 person GT) through the same evaluator as a re-derived control: box mAP@0.5 0.5003 -> 0.6853 (+18.50), recall at MATCHED precision 0.9031 -> 0.9572 (+5.41), ball mAP@0.5 0.0581 -> 0.2066, recall better on 58/58 sequences, and -- reversing 5A -- role-correct coverage of GT persons RISES 0.8403 -> 0.9038 (+6.35) where 5A's best run lost 6.05. The game-3 player->referee leak falls 0.348 (5A colour) -> 0.0504, a 6.9x cut, and misses the pre-declared <=0.05 by 20 detections in 46,053. All four gate criteria were required, so the verdict is FAIL and v6 ships without A2 at zero sunk cost (the ~5 h valid + ~9 h test laptop re-extract was deferred to S7 and never run). Two further reversals of 5A: per-track majority voting over GT tracks now REPAIRS the fine-tune (coverage 0.9038 -> 0.9197, leak 2,359 -> 258, -89%) instead of worsening it, i.e. the residual errors are per-frame flicker rather than track-consistent conviction; and the leak is NOT flat after one epoch but falls monotonically (0.0915 ep1 -> 0.0615 ep4 -> 0.0626 ep7 -> 0.0504 ep10) with the valid mAP curve still rising at epoch 10 -- the 10-epoch budget ran out before convergence, so this is a dose shortfall, not a wall.
claims.unit: game-3 player->referee rate at last.pt vs the pre-declared <=0.05 criterion (2,322 of 46,053 matched players; 2,302 would have passed) -- the single failed axis of four
evidence: results/CLUSTER_SESSION_S4.md#0 PRE-DECLARED GATE (written before any S4 evaluation was run)
results/CLUSTER_SESSION_S4.md#6 Epoch trajectory -- the leak is falling and had not converged
results/CLUSTER_SESSION_S4.md#7 GATE VERDICT -- FAIL on (c), by 0.0004
claims.method: ~/work/det/build_det_data.py gained a --v3-root ingester: v3 class strings mapped per ~/logs/v3_audit.md section 9, frames written pre-scaled to the training imgsz long side (640, INTER_AREA, JPEG q90) because ultralytics' loader does exactly that rescale at load time -- so the 1280x720-majority v3 stills and the 1920x1080 GSR frames (both ~16:9) get identical geometry inside the network, at 1.9 GB instead of 45 GB. Sampling is a plain union (no sampler), 42,750:33,986 = 1.258:1, since the raw ratio was already the intended ~1:1. Training via ~/work/det/train_det_ft.py, judged on last.pt (best.pt was epoch 10 = last.pt). Evaluation via ~/work/det/det_eval.py (ultralytics model.val for box mAP + a class-agnostic PERSON evaluator matching greedily by confidence at IoU 0.5, at the pipeline's imgsz 640 / iou 0.7 / max_det 300 / DETECT_CONF 0.20) and ~/work/det/role_vote.py (role accuracy per detection and after a majority vote over GROUND-TRUTH tracks, plus per-game player->referee aggregation added this session). The control was re-derived first through the identical evaluator and reproduced 5A to the digit (0.5003 / 0.0581 / 0.7966 / 0.9031 / 0.8403457 / 645).
caveats: The failed criterion misses by 0.0004 -- 20 detections of 46,053 -- which is inside single-seed noise. The gate was declared before the evaluator ran and is NOT re-drawn; any re-run needs a fresh pre-declared gate, and selecting an epoch by its leak on the reported split is the selection the anti-selection rule forbids.

The +14.85 ball mAP@0.5 is a box-level number on stride-5 valid frames. Per the ball-metric rule, only the post-link_ball usable track counts as coverage; no ball-track validation was run, so this must not be quoted as ball coverage.
The per-track vote repair (leak -89%) uses GROUND-TRUTH track ids -- an oracle-association upper bound. A real tracker-side role vote is unmeasured.

GSR clip metadata carries no league or date, so game-level overlap with v3 cannot be checked directly; the seasons are disjoint (v3 2014-2017, GSR 2019-era) and v3's own valid/test games were not excluded, which is harmless since nothing v3 is evaluated on.
Role coverage on game 3 specifically still falls (0.8682 -> 0.8413) even though the aggregate rises; the fine-tune's win is carried by games 2 and 5 (+11.7 and +12.5 points of role coverage).
Single seed, single mix ratio, 10 epochs. Neither longer training nor a v3-oversampled mix was tested.

SEQUEL: S4b re-ran the identical four-criterion gate after 10 more epochs and PASSED all four (game-3 leak 0.04576, role coverage 0.9130, mAP@0.5 0.7069, ball 0.2222) -- see gsr-det-004. The S4 FAIL recorded here stands as measured; the two verdicts straddle a within-run noise band of ~0.036 on the criterion-(c) quantity.

claims.statement: Ten more epochs on the same GSR+SoccerNet-v3 mix clear the SAME four-criterion detector gate that S4 failed: A2 is recommended for S7. S4b resumed from S4's last.pt with an identical recipe (warm restart, lr0 0.002, hsv 0.3/0.9/0.6, batch 64, seed 0, 10 epochs, 48.6 min on one A100; 20 epochs and 1.61 GPU-h cumulative) and was judged on the new last.pt against the ORIGINAL control through the same evaluator. Box: mAP@0.5 0.5003 -> 0.7069 (+20.66), recall at MATCHED precision 0.9031 -> 0.9589 (+5.58), person precision at conf 0.20 0.7966 -> 0.9124, better recall on 58/58 sequences and better precision on 57/58, and every height bucket up including <40 px (0.3996 -> 0.5528). claims.statement: FAIL. A pre-registered 18-arm solver retune on the v6 GSR chain moves DEV-20 GS-HOTA by at most +0.0577 against a gate of >= +1.0 AND >= 12/20 sequences helped, so the incumbent solver calibration ships unchanged. 11 coordinate arms (p_correct {0.926,0.95}, r_abstain {0.02,0.05,0.10}, pi_none {0.5,0.85}, topk 5, app_gain 5, sim_none {0.90,0.95}) plus a 6-arm r_abstain x pi_none joint grid, each a full DEV-20 run paired against the V0 control (51.808280888021784, reproduced EXACTLY by the harness before any arm and again by a confirmatory repeat run, per-sequence identical both times). Best arm pi_none 0.5 + r_abstain 0.05 = 51.8660 (+0.0577), 7/20 helped, Wilcoxon p 0.841, and its top-2 sequences carry 192% of its net per-sequence gain, so it is demoted by the concentration guard as well as failing both gate legs. This is the evidence-density law's dense-regime test and it returns a SPLIT verdict: the chain IS in the dense regime the law predicts a payoff in -- read density d = 0.386 reads per merged tracklet (336/870) at ~0.926 read precision, against the law's d* = 0.347 at 0.86 precision and 0.268 at 0.95 -- and the precision/coverage dial the law describes is demonstrably live (jersey precision 0.6518 -> 0.6648 as r_abstain rises). What is refuted is the conversion step this session pre-registered: the dial does not convert into GS-HOTA, because GS-HOTA's per-row identity gate prices coverage above precision (r_abstain 0.10 buys +0.61 GS-AssA and +0.5 jersey-precision points for -1.10 GS-DetA, net -0.50 GS-HOTA). The mechanism of the null is structural, not statistical, and was measured at the label level: over 870 merged tracklets, p_correct 0.8837->0.926 changes 0 labels, pi_none 0.7->0.5 changes 0, sim_none 0.92->0.90 changes 0, topk 3->5 changes 6, app_gain 10->5 changes 21, while r_abstain 0->0.02 changes 330 (328 of them names being withdrawn). solve_bundle_scored pins the unknown column's payoff to r_abstain, and pi_none and sim_none only rescale the whole identity block against that column, so at r_abstain = 0 they cannot re-order any argmax -- pi_none 0.85 and sim_none 0.95 are measurably THE SAME intervention (identical GS-HOTA 51.7364, identical named/GK/jersey columns, both moving exactly 5 of 870 labels). At r_abstain = 0 the solver is already in the name-everything-admissible corner and the only knob that leaves it leaves in the losing direction; what binds is the admissible set (13.2 self-roster identities per sequence), not the calibration.

claims.statement: A learned team-side detector does NOT beat the positional ceiling -- the first measurement of learned side assignment in SoccerNet-GSR, and it is a negative. A YOLOv8s detector was fine-tuned from the shipped S4b checkpoint on SoccerNet-v3's side-preserving labels (6 classes {0 ball, 1 gk_left, 2 gk_right, 3 player_left, 4 player_right, 5 referee}; 366,081 boxes = 98.52% of v3 kept; 32,532 train frames / 380 games, 1,454 holdout frames / 20 games; v3 ONLY, because 39 GSR train sequences are in the grading pool), 30 epochs / 57.8 min on one A100 at the S4b recipe with the one mandatory change fliplr=0.0 (a horizontal flip inverts the label semantics and ultralytics cannot swap paired detection classes). Run as an OVERLAY on the cached v6 detections (boxes matched by foot point at max(0.5*width, 12 px); validated as an IoU match -- 566,800 pairs, mean IoU 0.8608, 98.61% at IoU>=0.5), one side vote per matched row per kit cluster, 873,883 votes over 97 dev sequences: side accuracy 91/97 = 0.9381, which is EXACTLY the free incumbent meanx's score on the identical pool (91/97 = 0.9381), with 89/97 agreement. Pre-declared gate (>=0.94 AND correct on the three GT-inversion clips SNGS-038/092/111) FAILS on both criteria: 0.9381 < 0.94, and only SNGS-038 is correct -- SNGS-092 and SNGS-111 are wrong with vote shares 0.7123 and 0.7613 over 10,298 and 8,462 votes, i.e. strong evidence pointing the wrong way, the same inversion signature GSR_TEAMSIDE measured for meanx. VERDICT KILL; the V2 fusion session is cancelled and eval/gsr_score.py is untouched. The negative is sharp, not soft: (a) the model is CONVERGED -- holdout mAP@0.5 flat at ~0.822 from epoch 17 to 30 -- so unlike S4 this is not a dose shortfall; (b) it did learn something -- per-box side accuracy 0.7713 in-domain against a pure image-x shortcut worth only 0.5983 on the same corpus -- but what it learned is per-frame pitch geometry, the same information calibration already gives meanx, estimated worse; (c) the +4/-4 split is diagnostic -- every clip it fixes is one where meanx's margin is under 1.9 m (its estimation-error family: 0.01, 0.62, 0.87, 1.84) and every clip it breaks it breaks at its own low vote share 0.53-0.63 while meanx is confident (up to 7.1 m); (d) its vote-share margin is no better a correctness ranking than |meanx| (AUC 0.8388 vs 0.8425). The training corpus cannot grade numbers at all: arm-4t was fine-tuned on it, so the trunk reads the player-disjoint holdout at 0.9930 and the head's 0.9969 there is a measurement of the trunk's memory. Every number-class figure quoted is DEV-20 (GSR validation), unseen by both.

DEV-20 per-crop GT is inherited from the track, so a crop whose number is genuinely hidden still counts as numbered -- every per-crop precision here is a pessimistic bound, identically for every arm.

claims.statement: The Grad CVPRW2025 claim that an evidential recognizer's big gains live on INVISIBLE detection does NOT reproduce on SoccerNet-GSR, and the reason is a supervision defect that retires the 'free illegible labels at scale' idea. Separating DEV-20 crops whose GT track carries no number (2,090) from those that do (4,965), the learned no-number class scores ROC AUC 0.6200 -- BELOW the frozen trunk's own p_illegible (0.6429) and well below the shipped 2024 ResNet34 legibility classifier it was built to replace (0.7038). The total-evidence uncertainty u scores 0.5553, barely above chance. On the training corpus's player-disjoint holdout the same head scores 0.9718, a 0.35-AUC gap with a clean explanation: the no-number supervision was DEFINED by the legibility classifier (leg <= 0.7), so the head learned to predict its own teacher's decision and is a lossy copy of it wherever 'invisible' is defined by ground truth instead. 56.8% of SoccerNet-v3's digit crops failing a legibility filter is a large, cheap, per-crop-sound signal about THAT FILTER, and only indirectly about whether a number is visible.

The incumbent aggregation rule emits ZERO reads on evidential evidence (min_crop_conf 0.90 is unreachable for a Dirichlet mean, which is capped near 0.68 by construction), so the rule had to be re-swept per arm. Evidential outputs are not drop-in for a chain calibrated on softmax confidences.

max_u and max_p_none are INERT in the voting family -- percrop_votes already gates on argmax != ILLEGIBLE plus a confidence floor, which subsumes both. The uncertainty channel only acts inside fusion.

claims.statement: CAMELTrack does NOT transfer to the SoccerNet-GSR chain: every arm fails the pre-registered DEV-20 gate (>= +1.0 GS-HOTA AND >= 12/20 helped vs the pinned control 51.8083), and the binding constraint is the appearance cue, not the matcher. The released weights' appearance tokenizer is a Linear(128, 512) fitted to KPReID's 6-part embedding space, which a 256-d global CLIP vector cannot fill, so every multi-cue checkpoint had to run through its own trained drop_app path (bbox-only): camel_bbox_bee24 @0.6 scores 38.1984 (-13.6098, 0/20), camel_bbox_app_kps_sportsmot @0.1 scores 31.6038 (-20.2045, 0/20) and @0.5 scores 36.6114 (-15.1969, 0/20). A CAMEL trained from scratch on GSR train-57 with OUR cues (bbox + 256-d CLIP, PartsEmbeddingsLinProj use_parts=False emb_size=256) reaches 92.2% held-out association accuracy on ground-truth tracklets and still scores 33.2207 (-18.5875, 0/20) end-to-end. The mechanism is measured, not inferred: row purity on the tracker's own partition is 0.6097 (sportsmot @0.1, 242 of 467 tracklets contaminated), 0.7043 (@0.5), 0.7701 (trained arm @0.7) and 0.8336 (bee24 @0.6), against the incumbent EIoU's 0.9395 at 2,116 tracklets; assa_merge_only sits barely above assa_hat on the contaminated arms (0.3593 vs 0.3342) because contamination cannot be un-merged, and the GTA connector correctly refuses those partitions (26 merges at 0.400 precision against 1,380 at 0.5432 on the control). sim_threshold is inert between 0.1 and 0.3 (bit-identical remaps) and trades purity against fragmentation thereafter without ever reaching the incumbent's operating point. The pre-registered fallback -- one EIoU retune sweep, six points -- also fails: the best point e0.3 r1 w_app0.7 app_max0.30 is +0.4853 at 12/20 (p 0.0401 uncorrected, Bonferroni 0.0083), and the live knob is the APPEARANCE weight (w_app 0.5->0.7 = +0.49) while every geometry move is <= +0.27 and tightening app_max 0.30->0.20 costs -7.7698 by exploding the partition to 11,723 tracklets. The v6 association ships unchanged.

A faithful zero-shot arm needs KPReID part embeddings plus a pose model for its keypoint prompts.

Arm F's training corpus is GROUND-TRUTH boxes with GT ids, not our detector's boxes matched to GT. The arm-F training loop is a reimplementation: upstream's is coupled to tracklab TrackerState pickles and its README still lists training-code cleanup as an open TODO. The batch format was reverse-engineered from cameltrack/camel.py and validated only by the toy check and the val curve.

Gate: level FAIL (50.1252 < 50.5), significance FAIL (0.0421 > 0.025), breadth PASS (23 >= 22). Per the pre-declared ship rule neither registered arm clears its full gate, so the push ends: v7 ships nothing, the v6 bundle (TEST-38 49.4970, test-49 53.0846) stands, and no test-49 run or submission package was produced. Isolating the association knob on identical evidential evidence, ARM 2 minus ARM 1 is +0.2530 pooled GS-HOTA, per-sequence mean +0.1874, 20/38 helped, one-sided p 0.1102 -- about half the +0.4853 the same knob was worth on DEV-20 over the v6 reader.

claims.statement: The mechanism claimed by results/GSR_V7_V3.md 2.9 -- that the Dirichlet evidential reader buys transferable READ PRECISION at matched read density, and that on this chain 0.0073 of read precision is worth ~1.26 GS-HOTA -- does NOT reproduce on held-out data: the precision advantage reverses sign. Graded against the GSR jersey GT on the identical positions_gate_v6det track partition, each reader at its own arm's rule: DEV-20 (on record) v6 reader d 0.4114 at precision 0.9365 vs evidential d 0.4104 at 0.9438 (+0.0073); TEST-38 (this session) v6 reader d 0.3512 (834/2,375 tracks) at 0.9079 vs evidential d 0.3528 (838/2,375) at 0.9009 (-0.0070), i.e. density matched to 0.0016 and precision worse by 0.0070. The 450-point DEV rung-2 aggregation sweep that selected fuse94 was fitting DEV's density/precision frontier, not a property of the reader. What DID transfer is a small coverage effect the same V3 session had declared unsupported: GS-DetA +0.566 with GS-AssA -0.045, named tracklets 1,197 -> 1,206, admissible slots per sequence 13.26 -> 13.34 -- i.e. GSR_V7_V1.md's admissible-set hypothesis, not V3's read-precision one.

Read precision is measured only over auditable tracks carrying a GT number (793 and 797 respectively).
caveats: The DEV-20 row is quoted from GSR_V7_V3.md 2.9, where grading used the ungated positions_v6det ids rather than positions_gate_v6det; the TEST-38 comparison between the two readers is internally consistent (one partition, one GT cache), but the DEV-vs-TEST density levels are not strictly comparable across that difference.

Both readers lose density and precision going from DEV-20 to TEST-38 (0.41 -> 0.35, and 0.9365/0.9438 -> 0.9079/0.9009), so part of the shift is split difficulty. What split difficulty does not explain is the sign flip of the DIFFERENCE between the two readers measured on one split.
Single measurement per reader per split; no bootstrap on the precision estimate.

claims.statement: FIVE SoccerNet-GSR SEQUENCES CARRY A WHOLE-CLIP TEAM SIDE SWAP IN THE GROUND TRUTH, AND THE THREE ON THE TEST SPLIT ARE EXACTLY THE THREE THE BENCHMARK LEADER NAMES. This is OUR measurement plus THEIR published statement, and the two agree independently. THEIR statement: the WACV 2026 Broadcast2Pitch paper (GS-HOTA 61.48 test, the current leader) writes that test samples SNGS-126, SNGS-131 and SNGS-197 'have incorrect team annotations in the SoccerNet-GSR test set'; the paper names no mechanism, no dev-split clip and no count. OUR measurement, made without reading their code: all 164 labelled GSR sequences were scanned with a cross-clip test -- teams change ends once, at half time, so every clip of one (game, half) must give the same kit the same left/right label. 159 of 164 clips obey it. The five that do not are SNGS-092 (valid), SNGS-111 (train), SNGS-126, SNGS-131, SNGS-197 (test). The error has a signature: all five are SECOND-half clips and each carries its own game's FIRST-half team-to-side mapping, i.e. the annotator's convention was not updated after the ends changed. Zero first-half clips dissent. Each dissenter is a confident assignment (kit-prototype margin 29.3 to 52.1 against a per-game kit separation of 33.9 to 54.1; 0 of 164 clips degenerate). The swap is a WHOLE-CLIP swap, not scattered mislabelling: in all ten clips audited crop-by-crop, kit clustering agrees with the GT team split at 1.00 track-level and 0.915-0.993 crop-level, so not one individual player is filed under the wrong team.
claims.unit: sequences of 164 with a swapped team-to-side convention
evidence: results/GSR_GT_AUDIT.md#3. The decisive scan: all 164 sequences
results/GSR_TEAMSIDE.md#3. Family 2 -- the rules, on our positions and on ground truth
claims.method: tools/gsr_gt_audit.py, laptop CPU. Three instruments. (1) Every side rule of tools.gsr_teamside.side_scores run on GT positions, including gk_self ('a keeper's own team defends the goal he stands in'), whole clip and per third. (2) Player crops sampled every 15th frame from boxes >= 40 px tall, summarised by generator.teams.jersey_color (median CIELAB of non-grass torso pixels) and clustered KMeans(2) against the GT team split, with a separability ratio and per-track majority. (3) The decisive one: per-clip median CIELAB per GT side, then per-GAME KMeans(2) over those side-signatures to name each clip's left side by which of the match's two kits it wears, then a majority vote within each (game, half). Two alternative explanations were tested and closed: a 180-degree rotated GT pitch frame (the per-frame correlation of GT bbox_pitch x with GT bbox_image x_center is POSITIVE on all 49 test clips, 0.37 to 0.96) and a reverse-angle camera (the per-frame correlation of GT pitch-y with image foot-y is POSITIVE on all 49, 0.79 to 0.97). Contact sheets written for visual confirmation. Self-check: python -m tools.gsr_gt_audit --demo.
caveats: gk_self -- the definitional keeper rule, 113/113 on dev -- returns 'consistent' on ALL FIVE swapped clips and would have closed this audit with the opposite answer. A whole-clip swap moves the keeper's label with everyone else's, so a rule that compares a keeper only with his own position cannot see it. The first pass of this act did exactly that and reported 'their claim is not reproduced'.

The cross-clip test cannot grade a clip in isolation and assumes the error is a MINORITY event within a game-half. A whole game-half annotated with a swapped convention would be adopted by the majority vote and missed. Detecting that needs a physical anchor outside the annotation.

An earlier version of the kit handle ('the redder side', higher a*) produced one false positive, SNGS-160, whose two kits differ in lightness but have identical a* (2.0 vs 2.0). Every number quoted is from the fixed per-game LAB-prototype version.
Game 4 has weakly separated kits (prototype separation 8.1 vs 33.9-54.1 elsewhere); it is unanimous in both halves anyway, but its evidence is weaker than the rest.

We have not read the leader's predictions. Whether their submission emits the physically correct side on these clips (and therefore loses them, as their paper implies) is checkable in their public repo and was NOT checked here.

claims.statement: SNGS-130 -- OUR FOURTH TEST FLIP, AND THE ONE THE LEADER DOES NOT NAME -- IS NOT A GROUND-TRUTH ERROR. IT IS OURS. Its GT is consistent by every instrument: it sits with the majority of game 7's second half (6 of 8 clips), its keeper is labelled by his own goal (gk_self -47.75), its kit clustering agrees with the GT team split 1.00 at track level, and its gk_anchor is correctly signed (-0.73) where the three swapped test clips are wrong (+2.76, +3.77, +1.51). What makes it lose is that its GT mean-pitch-x separation is -0.11 m -- eleven centimetres over 750 frames, the tightest margin in the whole test split (next tightest correct clip: SNGS-191 at -2.30 m). Our estimator landed on the wrong side of a knife edge, and no better side rule reaches it: meanx is already at its GT-oracle ceiling. The mirror-image case is SNGS-195, GT-consistent with a +0.69 m depth inversion (broadcast framing, like SNGS-038 at +0.95 m) that the GT ORACLE gets wrong and our noisy estimator gets right by luck. This splits the shared 45/49 of GSR_TEAMSIDE into three distinct failure modes: three annotation errors (126, 131, 197), one framing artefact (195), one noise-floor coin flip (130).
claims.unit: GT mean pitch-x separation on SNGS-130, metres (negative = label correct)
evidence: results/GSR_GT_AUDIT.md#3. The decisive scan: all 164 sequences
results/GSR_GT_AUDIT.md#4. SNGS-130 vs SNGS-195 -- the discrepancy in our list against theirs
claims.method: Same three instruments as gsr-gt-001, applied to the v6 flip set (SNGS-126, 130, 131, 197) plus controls SNGS-116 (healthy), SNGS-129 (the v4/v5-era flip the v6 detector fixed), SNGS-195 (GT-oracle inversion that is not one of our flips) and the three dev inversions SNGS-038 / 092 / 111. GT meanx values are tools.gsr_teamside.side_scores on GT positions.
caveats: SNGS-130 has no measured correct-side GS-HOTA counterfactual at v6; the DELEAK per-clip table predates the v6 detector, whose flip set moved from SNGS-129 to SNGS-130.
gk_anchor is corroboration, not proof: its GT ceiling is only 0.690 and it is positive (wrong) on two healthy clips in this pool, SNGS-129 and SNGS-195.

claims.statement: THE ANNOTATION ERROR COSTS US ~2.45 GS-HOTA THAT NO CORRECT METHOD CAN RECOVER -- AND IT COSTS THE LEADER MORE, SO IT WIDENS THE GAP RATHER THAN CLOSING IT. Using the only measured correct-side counterfactual we have (results/GSR_DELEAK.md, v4-era leaky vs GT-free arms, leak-adjusted by the -1.94 the roster leak is worth on the 45 non-flipped clips), the three swapped test clips cost SNGS-126 -45.83, SNGS-131 -26.44 and SNGS-197 -47.58 on their own sequences, i.e. -2.45 on the 49-clip mean: our v6 test score 53.09 would be ~55.5 against a corrected ground truth. Recovering that means predicting the wrong side on purpose, so it is unreachable by construction, not by weakness. The leader's 61.48 is scored on the same three clips; a flipped clip does not degrade but annihilates (GS-HOTA identity is (team, jersey), so ours score 5.36-6.78 when flipped), so if they lose all three their 46 healthy clips average ~65.1 and the three cost them ~-3.6 -- MORE than us, because the penalty scales with how good the clip would otherwise have been. Annotation-corrected, the gap goes from 8.39 to ~9.6. Dev-pool consequence: 2 of 115 dev sequences carry the same error, so any side rule graded on dev has a hard ceiling of 113/115 = 0.9826, BELOW the 0.98 target the N1b brief set, and meanx's true error rate on well-annotated dev clips is 1 in 113, not 3 in 115.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA of our test-49 mean attributable to the three swapped clips
evidence: results/GSR_GT_AUDIT.md#5. Implications -- how much of the loss is unreachable by anyone
claims.method: Arithmetic on measured per-clip GS-HOTA, not a new measurement. Our figure uses the v4-era DELEAK per-clip pair (leaky side-correct vs GT-free side-flipped) minus the -1.94 roster-leak term, summed over three clips and divided by 49. The leader's figure assumes their flipped clips score in the same 5-7 band ours do and that they do not reproduce the annotation error.
caveats: STATUS PENDING BECAUSE THIS IS AN ESTIMATE, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The established fact is the annotation error (gsr-gt-001); everything downstream of it here is arithmetic.
Our -2.45 rests on a v4-era counterfactual. The v6 chain is stronger, so the true recoverable figure is probably larger, not smaller.

The leader's ~-3.6 assumes they LOSE those clips. If their pipeline instead reproduces the annotation error, up to ~3.6 of the 8.39 gap is unreachable-by-correct-methods and the true capability gap is ~4.8. We have no evidence for that reading; publishing the observation is weak evidence against it.
SNGS-130 (a further -0.5 to -1.0 at the same per-clip scale) is NOT in this figure: it is our own error and it is real headroom.
No action follows. Nothing was rebuilt, no GT was edited, and deliberately emitting a wrong side to match a buggy label is not proposed.

claims.statement: THE SEAM IS REAL, VIA CONFIDENCE-WEIGHTED COUNTING RATHER THAN DIRICHLET FUSION: at the leader's own shipped operating point, replacing Counter.most_common(1) with our percrop_votes confidence-mass aggregation on the SAME per-crop outputs and the SAME 350 read tracklets raises tracklet read precision 0.3107 -> 0.4175 (+0.1068, +34% relative; 96 -> 129 correctly named of 309 auditable reads). 13 of 20 sequences helped / 1 hurt / 6 tied, Wilcoxon p = 0.00172; tracklet flips 37 vs 4, binomial p = 1.03e-7. The gap is monotone in the per-crop confidence floor and reaches zero at floor 0.7-0.9, i.e. it lives entirely in the crops whose confidence their torch.max discards. It survives 28x more crops: at full density (29,765 crops, ~425/tracklet, 3 sequences) 0.4286 -> 0.4898 (+0.0612), and our aggregation on 15 crops (0.4681) still beats their aggregation on 425 (0.4286).

evidence: results/GSR_V8_W1.md#2.6 The result that survives: at their OWN operating point, mass beats counting
results/GSR_V8_W1.md#2.9 The crop-density objection, tested -- and the sharpest single number in the session
