DEV-20 GT crops (7,055 crops / 473 tracks / 331 numbered), GSR jersey GT.
caveats: This is tracklet read precision on GT tracks, NOT a GS-HOTA delta. Nothing end-to-end was run (GSR_S3_READER.md section 6: a better tracklet rule can score worse end-to-end).
The effect is 4x smaller on our own (stronger) reader: +0.0275 at the same operating point. Confidence-weighted aggregation buys most where the per-crop reader is worst.
The leader's 61.48 headline uses their LLaMA variant, which emits free text and has no per-crop confidence, so this seam does not exist on their shipping configuration.
Full-density probe is 3 sequences / 49 auditable tracklets: the +0.0612 is 3 tracklets.

claims.statement: HEAD-TO-HEAD: our v6 reader outreads the leader's CLIP identity head by 2.4x per crop on the identical 7,055 DEV-20 GT crops -- 0.8330 vs 0.3406 precision at the matched emit rate 0.2761, and 0.9919 vs 0.8105 on each head's top 5% of reads. At tracklet level our reader carries 10-11x their coverage at every read-precision floor from 0.90 up (d 0.7160 vs 0.0634 at 0.90). Their head is measurably complementary but only weakly: an ORACLE union would add 99 correct crops (+8.7% relative) that ours misses, buried in 1,367 wrong reads, so no ensemble was built. Their role head is strong (0.9015 crop accuracy) and their colour->team rule reaches 83.8% of player/GK tracks with an oracle side permutation.
claims.unit: their per-crop read precision at emit 0.2761 (ours 0.8330 on the same crops)
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W1.md#2.4 Their head on our DEV-20 GT crops -- per-crop
results/GSR_V8_W1.md#2.8 Head-to-head -- their identity head vs our v6 reader
claims.method: Both heads run on the identical crop set; our side reproduces the on-record S2/V3 bar first (1,371 reads at emit 0.2761, precision 0.8330 vs the recorded 0.8344). Each side is measured as its authors ship it: theirs on the whole person crop at CLIP 224x224, ours behind the ResNet34 legibility gate and a KeypointRCNN torso RoI.
caveats: Their head is fitted on GSR train and generalises worse off it (train 0.4730 vs validation 0.2681 read precision, role 0.9877 vs 0.9015) -- legitimate, but it means these are validation-generalisation numbers. Ours is also train-fitted (3,888 GSR-train rows) and validation-tested.
Preprocessing differs by design; the 12 of 7,055 crops our 256x128 crop law aspect-distorts (0.17%) were measured and no control run was made.
GT crops, 15 per tracklet; their pipeline sees every frame.

claims.statement: MECHANISM / TRANSFER NEGATIVE: additive Dirichlet evidence fusion collapses on a head whose abstention class is diffusely over-weighted. The leader's CLIP head puts mean 0.5740 per-crop mass on its no-number sentinel (72.3% of crops argmax to it); summing that mass across a tracklet makes the fused no-number class win on 375 of 426 tracklets (88.0%), so fuse_tracklet abstains. Per-crop argmax is invariant to how much mass the loser holds and is therefore ROBUST to exactly this miscalibration. The winning hybrid is what percrop_votes already is: a relative per-crop argmax gate plus confidence-mass accumulation over the survivors. Our V3 fusion was fitted against a learned calibrated p_none and is NOT drop-in for a foreign head.
claims.unit: fraction of tracklets abstaining under unfiltered additive fusion on their head
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W1.md#2.7 Why the Dirichlet fusion fails on their head -- the negative worth keeping
claims.method: Direct measurement of per-crop and fused no-number mass on 426 DEV-20 player/GK tracklets, plus a 90-rule post-hoc max_p_none sweep (0.4-0.9) that failed to move the frontier by a single point.
caveats: The max_u channel remains useful even here: it is the only knob that raises fusion coverage on their head (d 0.3967 -> 0.4366 at max_u 0.6), consistent with GSR_V7_V3.md section 2.9's isolated +0.3598 GS-HOTA.
Says nothing about fusion on our own reader, where it ties or beats votes.

claims.statement: PRE-REGISTERED READ FAILS BY 0.0117: swapping the benchmark leader's calibration (Broadcast2Pitch SFR, SoccernetGSR_EfficientNet_Best.pth, kpts.py @ dbfb65c0, run as a private instrument) into our v6 chain on a 10-sequence DEV probe moves GS-HOTA by a mean paired +0.4883 at best of three pre-declared arms, against a >= +0.50 escalation bar. Our calibgate campaign already captured whatever their +10.28 homography ablation represents; no SFR build is commissioned.
claims.unit: mean paired GS-HOTA gain over 10 DEV sequences (bar: +0.50)
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W2.md#2.5 THE DECISIVE TABLE -- paired GS-HOTA on the probe
claims.method: Pre-registered in results/GSR_V8_W2.md section 1.5 before any arm was built. Probe = the 10 DEV-20 sequences with the worst composite rank of control GS-HOTA and measured loc_assoc GS-AssA. Same detections, track ids, OCR evidence, CLIP embeddings, box cache, EIoU association (provably unchanged: 584->1323 tracks in all four arms), GTA connector at tau 0.450 and MILP solver; the pitch coordinate of each detection row is the only variable. Control re-derived this session and reproducing gsr_v7_control_dev.json per sequence to delta 0.0. Gate deliberately taken as the max over three arms (theirs-faithful / theirs+our fill / union), biasing toward escalation.
caveats: The margin is 0.0117 -- a fail by a hair, recorded as such; nothing was re-run.
The winning arm (T3, union) is a pure COVERAGE effect: it writes only the rows our chain leaves without any pitch coordinate. Its mechanism is reachable without their model.
T1 (the faithful swap) is a coin toss: mean +0.4687 but median -0.7430, 4 helped / 6 hurt, Wilcoxon p = 1.000, its mean carried by SNGS-024 (+11.84) against SNGS-039 (-6.21).
Probe is the hard half of DEV-20 (mean control 42.94 vs 51.88); no DEV-20, TEST-38 or test-49 number was produced.

claims.statement: Our calibration is MORE accurate than the benchmark leader's on the probe. On 95,927 GT-matched player/GK detections across 10 DEV sequences, our on-record pitch coordinate (PnLCalib + the calibgate trust rule + fill) sits 0.475 m from ground truth (p90 1.379, 99.722% inside the evaluator's 5 m gate); the SAME detections through their homography sit 0.536 m away (p90 1.554, 99.049% inside the gate). 844 rows clear the 5 m gate under ours alone against 199 under theirs alone.
claims.unit: median GT-anchored position error, metres (theirs: 0.536)
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W2.md#2.4 GT-anchored accuracy -- the table that says which one is *right*
claims.method: Our player/GK detections matched to the nearest GT person in image space (accepted under 60 px), then the error in metres against that GT row's bbox_pitch computed for BOTH coordinate sets on the identical matched rows. Their kpts.predict was called unmodified; the axis convention was fixed once against GT (0.414 m vs 13.35 m under a flipped y) before any comparison.
caveats: Per sequence it splits: theirs is better on SNGS-024 and SNGS-048, ours on 027/039/051/054/057; pooled, ours wins (paired Wilcoxon p ~ 0, mean 0.692 m vs 0.814 m).

The matcher is an image-space 60 px nearest neighbour, not the evaluator's Hungarian assignment; identical for both sides by construction, so the paired comparison is safe and the absolute level inherits the gate's bias.
Rows with no GT partner (~19% of people rows) are excluded from both sides.

claims.statement: MECHANISM: the per-sequence outcome of a calibration swap is a read-out of which calibration is more accurate on that clip -- Spearman +0.903 (p = 0.0003) between the GT-anchored p90 error advantage and the end-to-end GS-HOTA delta over 10 sequences (+0.794 on the median, +0.855 on share-within-5 m). The team-side map is NOT the mechanism: resolve_team_map_free returns the GT-correct side on 10 of 10 probe sequences in every arm.
claims.unit: Spearman rho (p90 accuracy advantage vs GS-HOTA delta)
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W2.md#2.6 Mechanism -- the swap's per-sequence outcome is a calibration-accuracy read-out
claims.method: Rank correlation over the 10 probe sequences between (theirs minus ours) GT-anchored accuracy and the T1 paired GS-HOTA delta; free team maps recomputed per arm from the arm's own positions and compared against resolve_team_map on GT.
caveats: n = 10 sequences; the correlation is carried at the ends (SNGS-024 +11.84, SNGS-039 -6.21).
SNGS-054's free-map margin does drop 0.42 m -> 0.08 m under the swap and still resolves correctly -- a near-miss on the campaign's known coin-flip risk.

claims.statement: A frame's own homography beats an interpolated neighbour's, measured against an external calibrator: on the frames our chain leaves dead (coordinate present only via fill_calibration_gaps), their per-frame homography is more accurate on 8 of the 9 probe sequences that have such frames -- on SNGS-024, 1.97 m -> 0.45 m and 94.2% -> 100% inside the 5 m gate over 703 rows. Their model emits a usable homography on 7,500/7,500 probe frames (line-based path 100%, DLT point fallback 0, identity fallback 0 -- the Issue-#1 failure mode never fires at dbfb65c0) and reaches 1,324 of the 1,693 detection rows (78.2%) our chain leaves with no pitch coordinate.
claims.unit: % of our un-calibrated detection rows their calibration reaches
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W2.md#2.7 The bridged frames -- the one place their calibration is clearly better than ours
claims.method: Bridged frames identified as those absent from the pre-gate positions_v6det live set; GT-anchored error computed on that subset for both coordinate sets. Branch tagging by wrapping their Levenberg-Marquardt estimator and testing the emitted matrix for exact identity.
caveats: The coverage advantage is worth +0.4883 GS-HOTA (v8-w2-001) and does not clear the escalation bar.
Their projections are not free of cost: 478 of 118,224 (0.40%) are rejected off-pitch by our clamp_to_pitch, and the swap loses 109 rows our control has.
SNGS-057 is the counter-example: theirs covers 849 bridged rows to our 289 but at 2.57 m median against our 1.47 m.

claims.statement: The dead-frame line-calibration fallback FAILS its pre-registered read: on the same 10-sequence probe as W2, the best registered arm (line-support gate + donor-seeded line solve, dead frames only) is worth mean paired +0.3020 GS-HOTA against a >= +0.40 bar (7 helped / 2 hurt, worst -0.0056, Wilcoxon p = 0.098; pooled 42.9371 -> 43.1756). A post-registration bug fix to the seed chain lifts it to +0.3894, still short by 0.0106. The component does not enter the W5 bundle; fill_calibration_gaps stays. Both sides of the calibration-coverage term are now priced and agree it is real, small and concentrated in two sequences: an external SFR network was worth +0.4883 (v8-w2-001), our own CPU line solver 62-80% of that.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA, mean paired gain over the 10-sequence probe (bar +0.40)
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W2B.md#2.6 THE DECISIVE TABLE -- paired GS-HOTA on the probe
claims.method: Four arms re-derived through tools.gsr_eiou.run_point at the frozen v6 point, only the pitch coordinates of dead-frame rows varying; the control reproduces gsr_v7_control_dev.json to 0.0 per sequence and the rebuilt control chain is byte-identical (max 0.000000 m) to the on-record positions_gate_v6det.
caveats: The >= 7/10-helped clause passes vacuously: four of the seven move by <= +0.01 GS-HOTA.
The shortfall is one clip: SNGS-024 gains +1.150 (arm c) where the external calibrator gained +3.004, and 66 of its 107 dead frames are unrecovered.
No DEV-20 confirmation was run -- the registration conditions it on a probe pass.
METRICS_VERSION was NOT bumped: the stage is default OFF and no shipped artifact moves.

claims.statement: A classical line-based homography solver -- pitch-model lines, a grass-restricted top-hat ridge mask, and point-on-line constraints l^T (H p) = 0 solved by SVD from a neighbouring frame's homography (ICP) -- recovers 90.6% of the detection rows our chain leaves empty on dead frames, on the CPU, with no new dependency and no weights. On the 62 SNGS-057 frames the keypoint chain could not solve (41 of them measured as returning ZERO hypotheses, the other 21 alive only through the fill), it writes 719 rows -- 570 GT-matched -- at median 0.35 m / p90 0.73 m / 100% inside the evaluator's 5 m gate -- more accurate than our shipped chain's pooled 0.475 m and than the benchmark leader's 0.536 m. On fill-bridged frames it reproduces the 'a frame's own homography is sharper than its neighbour's' effect with our own estimator: SNGS-057 1.53 m -> 0.39 m over 272 paired rows, and GS-LocA rises in every arm.
claims.unit: m, median GT-anchored error of line-solved rows on SNGS-057 (n = 570 GT-matched)
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W2B.md#2.4 Accuracy of what was written -- GT-anchored, on the rows each arm added
claims.method: Detections matched to the nearest GT person in image space under 60 px (the W2 instrument); error in metres against that GT row's bbox_pitch. Ground truth read only to score. Recovery counted on frames carrying no pitch coordinate before the stage.
caveats: Accuracy is population-dependent: SNGS-024's recovered rows are 0.57 m median but p90 3.35-4.65 m with 4-7% outside the 5 m gate. 0.35 m is the best clip, not the method.
Every recovery is seeded from a neighbouring frame's homography; a sequence that opens dead, or a dead run longer than the ICP's 40 px coarse radius can absorb, gets nothing.
min_support = 0.804 and the image knobs (21 px top-hat, ridge >= 24) are sized for 1080p SoccerNet frames and were not swept.
The end-to-end value of all this is +0.3020 GS-HOTA and fails its bar (v8-w2b-001).

claims.statement: Line evidence is worth more as an ACCEPTANCE TEST than as the relaxation it guards. generator.postprocess.onpitch_plausible refuses any frame with fewer than TRUST_MIN_PLAYERS foot points whatever its homography is, so 79 probe frames whose hypothesis fits the pitch keypoints to 0.17-0.21 m (median 0.46 m from GT) are dead for lack of players -- but 4 of those 79 carry a catastrophic homography (up to 127 m) and no player-based test can tell them apart. Relaxing the rule alone is a coin toss (+0.1125 mean, 2 helped / 2 hurt, one clip at -0.712); additionally requiring line support >= 0.804 refuses 30 of the 88 relaxed frames and turns that -0.712 into +0.001 (worst case -0.026). On 400 frames the chain already trusts, line support is median 0.981 / p05 0.804 -- the instrument validating itself, GT-free.
claims.unit: median line support of homographies the shipped chain already accepts (n = 400)
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W2B.md#3.1 The line-support instrument validates itself on frames we already trust
claims.method: Support = share of in-image pitch-model line samples within 8 px of a ridge pixel. Live-frame homographies re-derived from their own projected rows by the DLT fill_calibration_gaps uses to pick donors; threshold fixed at the pooled p05 before any arm was built, without ground truth and without a score.
caveats: Per-sequence p05 ranges 0.710 to 0.978, so the pooled threshold is already a compromise.
Support is conservative by construction: a correct homography on a frame showing little marked pitch scores low, which is one source of the 66 unrecovered SNGS-024 frames.
This is a component measurement; the end-to-end arm still fails its bar (v8-w2b-001).

claims.statement: The 'sn-banner NBJW weights we did not know existed' escalation is a mechanical no-op: the NBJW v1.0.0 release assets SV_kp (264,964,645 B) and SV_lines (264,857,893 B) are byte-for-byte the size of the weights our PnLCalib calibrator already loads from ~/PnLCalib/weights -- same author (mguti97), served from PnLCalib's own release of the same files. Running them as a 'second fallback calibrator on dead frames' would re-run the exact network whose failure created those frames. ~2 GPU-h not spent. Confirmed at the frame level: on the 59 probe dead frames never cached, PnLCalib returns ZERO hypotheses (all 18 solves fail), the same population GSR_CALIBGATE.md sized at 13.2% of dead frames.
claims.unit: hypotheses PnLCalib returns on the 59 uncached dead probe frames
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W2B.md#1.0 Two facts established before registration, and how they changed the plan
claims.method: curl -sIL on the two NBJW release URLs for Content-Length against the local weight files; PnLCalibCalibrator.candidates() re-run on the 59 dead frames (GPU, 37 s), counting emitted hypotheses.
caveats: The size match was not verified by hash -- the files were deliberately not re-downloaded (nothing to gain, ~530 MB to spend).
The rest of the sn-banner sweep entry stands: the Mask2Former SoccerNet weights and the stacked cam-param filter are untouched by this.

claims.statement: REGISTERED FAIL. Per-sequence BatchNorm test-time adaptation of the detector (full cumulative recomputation of all 57 BatchNorm2d running_mean/running_var on each test sequence's own frames, stride 5, momentum=None, reset per sequence, no labels, no gradients) costs -17.5645 mean paired GS-HOTA on the 10-sequence v8 DEV probe against a same-stack control, 0 sequences helped / 10 hurt, worst -31.54, best -6.58, Wilcoxon p=0.00195. The registered kill bar was >= +0.10, so DEV-20 was not run. Pooled over the probe: GS-HOTA 41.6728 -> 25.1791, GS-DetA 29.7643 -> 14.4075. Against the on-record control the arm reads -18.7041 (same verdict). The stage ships default OFF (generator.extract.BN_STATS is None) and METRICS_VERSION was not bumped.
claims.unit: mean paired GS-HOTA vs same-stack control, 10-sequence DEV probe
claims.method: generator/bn_adapt.py adapt_yolo: ultralytics fusion suppressed for the adaptation pass (it folds Conv+BN in place at first predict, leaving 0 BN modules), BN layers reset + train mode + momentum=None, frames through the detector's normal call so preprocessing matches inference, predictor dropped so the next predict re-fuses with the adapted buffers. Stats cached per sequence and re-applied in EVERY GPU stage (extract, per-crop OCR, box cache, CLIP embeddings), since all of them re-detect and match back to the persisted foot points. Both lineages (adapted and flag-OFF control) re-extracted on this laptop, scored through the frozen v6 EIoU chain (e=0.3, rounds=1, w_app=0.5, app_max=0.30, floor 0.80, tau 0.450), paired per sequence.
caveats: Registered arm only. Momentum-damped, layer-subset and larger-batch variants were NOT run: any of them would have been chosen by looking at the probe deltas.
The adaptation pass runs one frame per forward, so each BN's per-batch variance estimate comes from a single image; the pass structure was registered a priori.

Corpus-specific: the S4b detector was fine-tuned on SoccerNet GSR train, so the DEV probe is in-domain and there is little train->test shift for the lever to close. This is not evidence about a genuine domain transfer (e.g. EPL/ManU footage).

claims.statement: Mechanism of the W4 failure, measured at the detector: recomputing BN statistics on a sequence's own clean frames drops 4.7-25.7% of per-frame person detections, cuts the median detection confidence from ~0.76 to 0.56-0.66, and raises the share of people classified as referee by 2-6 points. End to end that is -23.5% positions rows (120,763 -> 92,433) and +37% raw tracks (750 -> 1,029) over the probe. The downstream chain's thresholds (DETECT_CONF, ByteTrack's high/low split, the EIoU appearance gate, the connector tau) are all calibrated against the shipped detector's confidence distribution, so a uniform confidence drop is read as weak evidence and tracks fragment. Statistics only move a median 3.9-5.1% (means) and 17-22% (variances).
claims.unit: percent change in positions rows, probe total, adapted vs flag-OFF control
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W4.md#2.4 Mechanism -- measured at the detector, not inferred
claims.method: 50 frames per sequence (stride 15) on SNGS-024/039/045/057, the shipped detector built twice via generator.extract._build_detector with and without the sequence's cached BN snapshot, same thresholds, no tracking and no scoring; row/track counts from the two positions lineages; BN shift = relative L2 of each buffer against the checkpoint's.
caveats: The per-frame probe covers 4 of 10 sequences and 50 frames each; it explains direction and rough magnitude, it is not a detection benchmark and no mAP was computed.

Attribution to YOLO's mosaic/HSV/scale augmentation (training-time BN statistics are the statistics of augmented batches, not of clean letterboxed frames) is a mechanism argument, not a measured ablation.

claims.statement: SECONDARY ARM, FAIL. The CLIP appearance embedder is NOT BatchNorm-free: the ViT-B/16 trunk is LayerNorm-only, but the trained head is Linear(768->256) -> BatchNorm1d(256) -> L2 (a BNNeck), and the epoch-8 checkpoint carries its running stats (num_batches_tracked=10000). Per-sequence recomputation of those 256 buffers, on the SHIPPED detections, costs -13.5219 mean paired GS-HOTA on the same probe, 0 helped / 10 hurt, p=0.00195. The per-sequence statistics are wildly different from the checkpoint's (relative L2 shift of running_mean 0.87-0.97), and under the frozen app_max=0.30 cosine gate the re-association shattered: 584 tracklets in, 11,977 out, against 1,422 for the control.
claims.unit: mean paired GS-HOTA vs on-record control, 10-sequence DEV probe
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W4.md#2.3 The secondary arm fails too, but for a different and partly instrumental reason
claims.method: generator.bn_adapt.recomputing on ClipEmbedder.bn; two passes over the sequence's own crops (pass 1 at frame stride 10 collects the statistics and discards its embeddings, pass 2 embeds at the shipped stride 2), BNNeck state reset from the checkpoint before each sequence. Detections, boxes and OCR evidence are the on-record v6det artifacts, so the arm differs from the control in 256 BN buffers alone.
caveats: Part of the loss is threshold coupling, not representation quality: re-whitening the features moves every cosine distance while app_max and tau stay frozen. A re-calibrated operating point was NOT tested (the registration forbids tuning against the probe), so no claim is made about BNNeck adaptation with re-fitted thresholds.

claims.statement: CAMPAIGN HAZARD. The on-record v6det DEV GPU artifacts cannot be reproduced on the current laptop stack (python 3.14.0, supervision 0.30.0, ultralytics 8.4.56, torch 2.11.0+cu128) - a flag-OFF re-extraction differs from positions_v6det on ALL 10 probe sequences (rows +1.3% to +2.6%, tracks systematically higher, e.g. SNGS-039 87 vs 58). End to end that stack drift is worth -1.1395 mean paired GS-HOTA (3 helped / 7 hurt, p=0.105). Extraction is nevertheless bit-deterministic run to run on one stack (same sequence extracted twice: identical=True, max_abs 0.0 over 7,704 rows, 48/48 tracks), so the experimental noise floor is exactly zero. Any session that RE-EXTRACTS must build its own same-stack control instead of pairing against gsr_v7_control_dev.json; sessions that reuse the cached detections (W2, W2b) are unaffected.
claims.unit: mean paired GS-HOTA of a flag-OFF re-extraction vs the on-record control
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W4.md#2.1 Control obligations -- one failed, one passed, and both matter
claims.method: tools.gsr_w4_bnstats stage 'repro': row-for-row parquet diff of positions_w4off (BN_STATS None, the identical shipped code path) against positions_v6det, and against a second independent flag-OFF run of SNGS-024; the end-to-end cost from scoring the w4off lineage through the frozen v6 chain and pairing per sequence.
caveats: Which package changed (supervision's ByteTrack, ultralytics' NMS, torch kernels) was NOT isolated - the session only needed to know that pairing across stacks is invalid.
The -1.1395 is measured on the hard 10-sequence probe; the drift on full DEV-20 or on TEST-38 was not measured.

claims.statement: CORRECTION to a repeatedly cited prior. The repo's 'BN-stats adaptation +0.18 free' gem (STATUS.md, and the W4 brief's 'precedent: +0.18 from BN-stats on the detector') was never a detector result and never a GS-HOTA result: CLUSTER_SESSION1.md section 8 measured +0.18 VALID IDENTITY mAP (56.93 -> 57.11) on the prtreid re-ID backbone, as a by-product of frozen-backbone training leaving BN in train mode. Measured on the detector end to end for the first time in W4, the same operation is worth -17.56 GS-HOTA.
claims.unit: valid identity mAP on prtreid (the actual scope of the cited precedent)
claims.method: Read of the on-record cluster-session log against the claim as cited in STATUS.md and in the W4 task brief.
caveats: The +0.18 prtreid number itself is not disputed; only its scope (re-ID mAP, not detector, not GS-HOTA) is corrected.

claims.statement: SoccerNet-GSR's jersey label is identity-carried with zero exceptions: of 1,224 GSR-train player/GK tracklets, 0 mix numbered and un-numbered boxes and 0 carry two different numbers. The field is a property of the identity, replicated to every box of it, and contains no per-frame visibility information -- the same hazard CLUSTER_SESSION_S2.md section 1.2 found in SoccerNet-v3's ID field.
claims.unit: tracklets with mixed or multi-valued jersey labels (of 1,224)
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W3_PREP.md#3.1 GSR train: identity-carried, with zero exceptions
claims.method: Label-only pass over all 57 GSR-train Labels-GameState.json, grouping every player/GK bbox_image annotation by track_id and counting distinct jersey values and null/non-null mixes per track. No image opened.
caveats: Measured on GSR train and (for the goalkeeper split) validation; GSR test was not opened.
Confirms rather than refutes the task premise; it fixes the resolution at 'zero exceptions' rather than 'mostly'.

claims.statement: SoccerNet-GSR never labels a goalkeeper's jersey number: 0 of 79 train GKs and 0 of 77 validation GKs carry one, against 933 of 1,145 train players. 27% of the unnamed-tracklet pool that campaign v8 targets is therefore an annotation-policy absence, not a legibility failure -- no reader or filter can recover those numbers from this dataset, and they cap the ceiling of every reader measured on it.
claims.unit: goalkeeper tracklets carrying a jersey number (of 79 train + 77 validation)
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W3_PREP.md#3.3 The goalkeeper policy -- the finding that resizes the W3 target
claims.method: Same label-only pass as v8-w3-001, cross-tabulating the attributes.role field against jersey presence per tracklet, on GSR train and validation.
caveats: GSR_S3_READER.md section 7.8 noted the policy in passing; this is the first exact count and the first confirmation that it holds on both splits.
GSR test was not opened, so the policy is confirmed on 2 of 3 labelled splits.

claims.statement: The server-side S2 glyph-only corpus figure reproduces exactly on the laptop: 4,175 of 13,994 numbered GSR-train GT crops pass the shipped ResNet34 legibility classifier at the shipped 0.7 threshold, matching CLUSTER_SESSION_S2.md section 3.3's 'GSR train: 4,175 of 13,994' to the crop, on a different machine through an independently written scorer.
claims.unit: GSR-train crops admitted glyph-only (of 13,994 numbered)
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W3_PREP.md#4.1 GSR train, assembled and validated against the server number
claims.method: tools/gsr_w3_corpus.py --legibility train over the 20,067 GT crops of tools/gsr_crops.py's published crop law, then --manifest restricted to player/GK crops carrying a GT number. Shipped weights legibility_resnet34_soccer_20240215.pth, threshold 0.7.
caveats: The filter is reproduced; the corpus it fed is not -- SoccerNet-v3 (42,479 of the S2 corpus rows) is 45 GB and server-only against 33 GB free locally.
Full-body crops. S2 section 3.4 measured a geometry crossover, so these rows are not trainable against the arm-4t chain until a pose-torso pass converts them.

claims.statement: The shipped legibility classifier and human tracklet-level abstention judgments agree 99.5% on the negative class: of jersey-2023 train crops belonging to the 403 tracklets a human marked illegible (-1), only 0.51% score above the 0.7 threshold. This validates the 0.7 gate as a glyph-only proxy against an independent human label, and means ~171,000 human-sourced no-number crops are already on disk -- the anti-teacher-imitation rule can be honoured without any model-derived abstention labels.
claims.unit: share of human-marked-illegible crops scoring above legibility 0.7
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W3_PREP.md#3.2 jersey-2023: also identity-carried, but its abstention class is human and usable
claims.method: tools/gsr_w3_corpus.py --j2023-sample 20000 (seed 0) over the 733,001-crop jersey-2023 train split; 4,722 of the sampled crops belong to -1 tracklets. Shipped legibility weights at 0.7.
caveats: Sampled, not exhaustive: 20,000 of 733,001 crops. The companion numbered-crop pass rate 0.2533 agrees with S2's 0.2590 to within 1.6 standard errors.

A -1 is a tracklet-level human judgment ('no number legible anywhere in this tracklet'), not a per-crop one; it is a stronger claim than per-crop, but its provenance is the sn-jersey annotation process and is not independently verifiable here.

claims.statement: A further SoccerNet-GSR ground-truth error, found the same way W0's five side-swaps were: in SNGS-065 at frame 000254, player track 6 (772,352,38,85) and referee track 22 (773,354,36,92) are the same body, IoU ~0.85, with both boxes smooth across their temporal neighbours. Existence proof only -- no systematic duplicate-box audit was run.
claims.unit: duplicate-identity GT box pair found (unaudited population)
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W3_PREP.md#7 Negatives, limits, and what was NOT done
claims.method: Visual inspection of a generated annotation contact sheet, then a label-only check of the two tracks' box trajectories around the frame and an overlap search over all player/GK/referee boxes at that frame.
caveats: One instance, found by eye while checking sheet usability. Not a count, not a rate, and not evidence about any other sequence.
The cheap systematic version (all-pairs IoU between player/GK and referee tracks per frame over the 57 train sequences) was NOT run.

claims.statement: MEASURED, replacing the sampled estimate carried in v8-w3-004's caveat: the full legibility pass over jersey-2023 train's numbered tracklets admits 140,278 of 560,744 crops at the shipped 0.7 threshold -- pass rate 0.2502, against the 20,000-crop sample's 0.2533 (optimistic by 0.31 pp) and inside GSR_V8_W3_PREP.md section 7.3's ~142,000 +/-2,000 projection. 926 of 1,024 numbered tracklets keep at least one admitted crop and 98 lose every crop; 909 keep >= 4 and 871 keep >= 15, so the 4-per-id and 15-per-tracklet sampling laws are satisfiable on almost all of it (median 121 admitted crops per surviving tracklet, max 702). All 44 distinct numbers survive the gate but the tail is thin: 7 numbers hold < 100 admitted crops and 9 are backed by a single tracklet, which is identity-shortcut risk rather than digit supervision. The three populations stay distinct by construction: 140,278 admissible numbered crops, 420,466 model-REJECTED numbered crops (not relabelled as no-number, per v7-v3-002's teacher-imitation refutation), and the 172,257-crop human-abstention pool of the 403 illegible tracklets. Zero decode failures; 560,744 + 172,257 = 733,001 accounts for the whole train split.
claims.unit: jersey-2023 train crops admitted glyph-only at legibility > 0.7 (of 560,744 numbered)
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W3_PREP.md#11 Addendum (2026-08-13) -- pass FINISHED on the cluster
claims.method: tools/gsr_w3_corpus.py --full-jersey23 over every crop of every numbered jersey-2023 train tracklet, in 29 resumable 20,000-crop shards, shipped weights legibility_resnet34_soccer_20240215.pth at threshold 0.7, batch 128. Shards 0-20 scored on the laptop RTX 3050; shards 21-28 on a100server1 GPU 1 (A100-40GB, 5 min 44 s for 160,744 crops) after verifying the shard partition is machine-independent -- rows are keyed by relative (tracklet, file) and the enumeration hashes identically on both machines (md5 5b77db76f8de97da53cbe80802a4b6dd over 560,744 rows). Manifest built locally by --j2023-full-manifest; server-side and laptop-side merges return the same 140,278.
caveats: The 0.7 gate is a model judgment on the POSITIVE side: an admitted crop is one the shipped legibility classifier believes shows a number, not one a human verified. Only the abstention side has human provenance (v8-w3-004).
Full-body crops. No torso RoI pass has been run, and S2 section 3.4 measured a geometry crossover, so this manifest is not directly trainable against the arm-4t chain yet.
Label is identity-carried at the tracklet level, so an admitted crop's number is the tracklet's number; the gate is what makes it a per-crop claim.
Corpus counts only. Nothing here has been shown to move a GS-HOTA.

claims.statement: Sid answered all 499 rows of the W3 annotation queue with zero blanks and zero 'unsure', and the tier-A result is mostly a NEGATIVE: of the 289 GSR-train player/GK tracklets SoccerNet's own annotators left without a number, a human reading 12 stratified closest-views per tracklet recovered a number on only 15 (5.2%) and returned 'none' on 274 (94.8%). This is not a view-size artifact -- 206 of the 274 'none' tracklets had a median shown view of >= 89 px (median 97 px, median 413 GT boxes), and every one of the 15 numbered tracklets cleared 89 px (median view 109 px). Read the other way it validates the benchmark: SoccerNet's unnumbered pool is overwhelmingly unnumbered because the glyph is genuinely unreadable in broadcast, not because its annotators gave up. The 15 numbers sit behind 5,938 GT boxes (2,988 at >= 89 px) and span 8 distinct values.
claims.unit: GSR-train tracklets given a human jersey number out of 289 unnumbered (274 none)
claims.method: tools/gsr_w3_corpus.py --queue built 12-cell time-stratified contact sheets (tallest box per twelfth, MIN_VIEW_H 89 px); labelled via tools/annotate_w3.py (417 rows) and Excel (72 pre-tool rows, A0001-A0072); consumed with --ingest. Counts recomputed independently from the CSV and reconciled row-for-row against sid_labels.parquet.
caveats: Single annotator, no second pass, no inter-annotator agreement.
7 of the 15 numbers are '1' and 6 of those 7 are goalkeepers -- the most common real GK number, but also the shortest keystroke; not independently re-checked.

2 of the 15 (A0085='30', A0103='36') carry a stray 'u' in their note field, committed in the same audit event as the label -- most plausibly an 'unsure' keypress that landed in the note box, so treat those two as annotator-flagged.
'none' is a statement about the 12 views shown, not about the whole tracklet.
labels_audit.jsonl carries 437 records over 427 queue ids.

claims.statement: First goalkeeper jersey numbers ever attached to SoccerNet-GSR: 7 of the 79 GSR-train GK tracklets now carry a human-read number (six '1', one '18'), against the 0 of 79 the benchmark ships (v8-w3-002). 72 GKs returned 'none'. The 7 sit behind 2,368 GT boxes (933 at >= 89 px). GK numbers exist nowhere in SoccerNet-GSR train or validation, so this is supervision no competitor can have from the benchmark alone -- but it is 7 tracklets and 2 distinct values, an existence proof and a GK-'1' prior, not a GK number distribution.
claims.unit: GSR-train goalkeeper tracklets given a human jersey number (of 79; benchmark has 0)
claims.method: Same queue and sheets as v8-w3-007, filtered to manifest rows with role == 'goalkeeper': A0054 SNGS-153 t3 ='1', A0061 SNGS-106 t7 ='18', A0077 SNGS-165 t26 ='1', A0128 SNGS-105 t24 ='1', A0144 SNGS-108 t26 ='1', A0192 SNGS-158 t26 ='1', A0204 SNGS-163 t25 ='1'.
caveats: 6 of 7 are '1'. A reader trained on this alone would learn 'goalkeeper -> 1', a role shortcut rather than glyph reading.
Not cross-checked against any external squad list; no second annotator.
A0054 and A0128 were labelled in Excel before the tool existed and never re-confirmed through the tool's audit log.

claims.statement: The project's first per-crop glyph-visibility supervision: all 210 tier-B tracklets were answered (189 cell-lists, 21 'none', 0 'all', 0 'unsure'), yielding 2,520 human-judged crops -- 771 positives (the known GT number is readable in that exact view) and 1,749 negatives (it is not). Base rate 30.6%: even on tracklets whose number the benchmark knows, and even at the CLOSEST view of each twelfth of the clip, the digits are unreadable in ~7 of 10 views. Visibility rises monotonically with box height across quartiles of the shown median view: 0.244 / 0.235 / 0.330 / 0.414 (77-111, 111-124, 124-139, 139-210 px). Unlike jersey-2023's abstention pool (v8-w3-004), which is a tracklet-level human judgment, these 1,749 negatives are per-crop.
claims.unit: human per-crop glyph-visibility labels (771 visible / 1,749 hidden)
claims.method: tools/gsr_w3_corpus.py --queue tier B: 210 numbered GSR-train tracklets ranked by ascending mean |legibility - 0.5| (gate-uncertainty selection -- the model chooses who is SHOWN, never the label), 12 cells each; --ingest expands each answered row to 12 per-crop rows in sid_labels.parquet.
caveats: The 210 tracklets were selected to sit near the legibility gate's decision boundary, so 30.6% is NOT the GSR-train visibility rate -- it is the rate on the gate's hardest tracklets.
Single annotator, no agreement measurement.
2,396 of the 2,520 crops are not yet materialised on disk (see v8-w3-011).

claims.statement: SETTLED at full n (2,520 of 2,520 tier-B cells now scored; the n=124 read is confirmed in direction and close in magnitude). Against Sid's per-crop human visibility truth, the shipped 0.7 legibility gate scores: human-visible 771, gate passes 743 (recall 0.964, 28 misses); human-hidden 1,749, gate wrongly passes 278 (specificity 0.841). Precision 743/1,021 = 0.728, NPV 1,471/1,499 = 0.981. The gate's error is overwhelmingly ADMITTING unreadable crops, not discarding readable ones: it loses 3.6% of the glyphs a human can read, and 27.2% of what it admits shows no readable number to a human. The W3 HOWTO's 'the gate throws away 79% of our crops' framing is refuted -- what it throws away is mostly genuinely unreadable, and the cost of the gate is positive-class label noise. Prior n=124 numbers: recall 0.973, specificity 0.805, precision 0.679.
claims.unit: recall of the 0.7 legibility gate against human per-crop visibility (n=2,520 cells)
claims.method: Cut the 11,076 label-named full-density crops missing from outputs/gsr/gt_crops/train (tools/gsr_w3_corpus.py --cut-labelled, CPU), scored them with the shipped legibility_resnet34_soccer_20240215.pth on a100server1 GPU 1, merged into legibility_train.parquet (31,143 rows, 0 decode failures), re-ran --ingest, then a 2x2 of (label != '<none>') against (legibility > 0.7) over all 2,520 tier-B rows.
caveats: SELECTED, but only once now: the 210 tier-B tracklets were chosen for gate uncertainty (mean |leg - 0.5| ascending), so this is the gate's behaviour on its hardest tracklets. The second selection (re-ID subsampling) that made the n=124 read doubly-biased is gone -- every cell Sid judged is now scored.
Human base rate 0.306 on all 2,520 cells vs 0.298 on the old 124, and gate pass rate 0.405; the earlier subsample was not skewed on the label side, which is why the two reads agree.

Single annotator, no inter-annotator agreement, and 'visible in this exact view' is a stricter question than the tracklet-level legible/illegible labels the gate was trained on -- part of the 278 false admits may be definitional rather than model error.
95% Wilson CIs: recall [0.948, 0.975], specificity [0.823, 0.857], precision [0.700, 0.754].
legibility_train.parquet holds 31,143 rows.

claims.statement: REALISED, the propagation promise is now paid: the W3 ingest admits 6,470 crop rows (1,433 positive, 5,037 negative) of 11,746 label rows, every one of them materialised on disk and scored. Of the 5,938 GT boxes behind the 15 tier-A human numbers, 662 pass the 0.7 gate -- up from 31 when 5,713 of them had no score at all. The unblock was exactly the diagnosed one (score coverage, not the gate): 11,076 missing crops cut on CPU in 18.0 min (9,713 full-frame decodes), scored in 26.1 s on a100server1 GPU 1, 0 decode failures. The realised carried pass rate is 0.1115 (662/5,938) against the 0.138 projected from the 225 re-ID-subsampled crops -- the projection of ~820 was optimistic by 19%, because the re-ID subsampler favours temporal spread over the small boxes that dominate a full tracklet. 13 of the 15 numbered tracklets keep at least one admitted crop, 12 keep >= 4, 8 keep >= 15 (0, 0, 2, 9, 13, 14, 14, 18, 31, 34, 45, 57, 136, 138, 151), spanning 8 distinct numbers. Against the standing corpus (GSR-train 4,175 + jersey-2023 140,278 + server-side v3 45,620 = 190,073) the 662 genuinely-new positives are +0.35%; the 1,433 total positives +0.75%. The real contribution remains the 5,037 PER-CROP human negatives, a class the corpus previously held only at tracklet level.

The 662 are glyph-gated by a classifier now measured at precision 0.728 on human truth (v8-w3-010), so a comparable minority of them plausibly show no readable number.
Crops are full-body at the S2 crop law's geometry; the pose-torso conversion S2 section 3.4 requires before these rows train against the arm-4t chain has not been run.

claims.statement: Benchmark-audit yield from the annotation pass is ZERO: across 499 contact sheets (5,988 individual views) a human explicitly invited to flag wrong-person cells and cells contradicting gt_number filed no such note. The note column holds exactly two entries, both the single character 'u' (A0085, A0103), and labels_audit.jsonl shows each committed in the same event as a numeric label -- a stray 'unsure' keypress caught by the note box, not a finding. v8-w3-005's SNGS-065 duplicate-identity pair remains the only GT error surfaced by this route, and it was found before the queue existed.

caveats: Absence of evidence: the annotator's task was labelling, not auditing, and filing a note required leaving the keyboard flow for the note box -- whose awkwardness is itself evidenced by the two stray 'u' keystrokes. A zero here does NOT establish that the 499 tracklets are error-free.

claims.statement: The 140,278-crop jersey-2023 'admissible' corpus (v8-w3-006) carries an estimated 27% positive-class label noise, and the legibility threshold is a directly calibrated size/purity dial. Applying v8-w3-010's per-band precision of the same gate against human per-crop truth to the jersey-2023 admitted score distribution (band precisions 0.239 / 0.329 / 0.461 / 0.601 / 0.889 over [0.7,0.8) / [0.8,0.9) / [0.9,0.95) / [0.95,0.99) / >=0.99, holding 5,452 / 9,706 / 11,203 / 30,976 / 82,941 jersey-2023 crops) estimates 101,976 of 140,278 truly show a readable number -- 0.727, indistinguishable from the flat precision 0.728 because the two admitted-score distributions nearly coincide (mean legibility 0.967 tier-B vs 0.968 jersey-2023). Moving the gate to 0.99 cuts the corpus to 82,941 crops (-41%) at estimated precision 0.889 and holds ~73,700 true positives, i.e. 72% of the estimated true positives at 28% fewer than half the false ones; to 0.999 it collapses to 31,450 crops (precision 0.959). Threshold 0.5 buys 7,596 more crops at precision 0.689. The 0.7 default maximises estimated true-positive count (102,083), so it is the right choice for a recall-hungry corpus and the wrong one if positive-class purity is what a reader needs.
claims.unit: estimated share of jersey-2023's 140,278 admitted crops that truly show a number
claims.method: Bin the 1,021 tier-B crops the 0.7 gate admits by legibility band, take the human-visible rate per band as that band's precision, and reweight by the jersey-2023 full-pass score histogram above each threshold; repeat the 2x2 at thresholds 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.9 / 0.95 / 0.99 / 0.999.
caveats: TRANSFER, not a measurement on jersey-2023: the precisions come from 2,520 human-judged GSR-train broadcast crops on gate-uncertainty-selected tracklets, applied to a different dataset's crops. Band reweighting controls for the score distribution only -- crop geometry, resolution and annotation process all differ. PENDING until a human labels a jersey-2023 sample directly.
The band precisions rest on 46 / 70 / 76 / 218 / 611 tier-B crops; the two lowest bands are thin, though they carry only 15,158 of the 140,278 jersey-2023 crops.
jersey-2023's tracklet-level human -1 labels (v8-w3-004) already show the gate agrees 99.5% on the negative class there, so this noise estimate is about the positive class only.
Selection direction is not established: tier-B tracklets sit near the gate's decision boundary, which plausibly makes 0.728 a floor on the precision the gate reaches on an unselected population.

claims.statement: REFUTED, the registered primary hypothesis of the v8-W3 retrain: a purity-tiered jersey corpus does NOT produce a better reader than the volume corpus. Two PARSeq arms were trained on the identical S2 arm-4t recipe (shipped init, pose-torso geometry, 25 epochs, batch 128, last.ckpt, same caps) and differ only in the legibility admission tier: ARM P at >0.99 (51,803 train rows, 82 numbers) and ARM V at the shipped >0.7 (83,812 rows, 89 numbers). On DEV-20 -- GSR validation, in neither arm's nor the incumbent's corpus -- at the incumbent's own emit rate 0.2761 over 1,371 reads: incumbent arm-4t 0.8344, ARM V 0.8293, ARM P 0.8133. Head to head purity loses to volume by -0.0160 (paired exact McNemar 43 candidate-only-correct vs 65 incumbent-only-correct, p=0.0428) and loses to the incumbent by -0.0211 (40/69, p=0.0070); ARM V is indistinguishable from the incumbent (-0.0051, 38/45, p=0.51). The obvious artifact is excluded by measurement: only one DEV-20 GT number (59, 45 of 4,965 crops) falls outside ARM P's vocabulary, and removing those crops leaves both deltas and both McNemar tables unchanged (-0.0161 / -0.0212, identical discordant counts). Removing the ~27% positive-class label noise that v8-w3-013 estimates in the 0.7 pool therefore makes the reader WORSE, not better: the v6 'bank the headroom as precision' lesson (s3-reader-003) is about the tracklet aggregation operating point and does not transfer to the corpus admission threshold. HARDENED 2026-08-14 by the follow-up session: the -0.0160 is 2.7x the measured run-to-run seed spread (v8-w3-018, 0.0059) and the volume-matched purity arm still loses (v8-w3-019, -0.0255 at p=0.0020), so neither seed noise nor the volume cost explains it.
claims.unit: per-crop precision, ARM P (tier 0.99) minus ARM V (tier 0.7), DEV-20 at matched emit
claims.method: Corpora assembled server-side by ~/work/w3/build_w3_corpus.py reusing S2's build_corpus.cap_per_group verbatim; torso RoIs from dev20_torso.torso_from_keypoints over a cache shared by both arms (109,316 of 118,136 crops, 92.5%). Both arms trained on a100server1 GPU 1 under tmux. Scored by ~/work/w3/w3_component.py, which imports dev20_arm.py's decode and gating unchanged, on the fixed ~/data/dev20 torso set at legibility 0.5; the incumbent reproduces its on-record CLUSTER_SESSION_S2.md 3.5 numbers (emit 0.2761, precision 0.8344) to four decimals in the same run, which is the harness-validity check. Significance by exact paired McNemar on per-crop correctness; Wilson 95% intervals reported alongside.
caveats: PURITY AND VOLUME ARE CONFOUNDED and this was declared before training: ARM P holds 61% of ARM V's rows and ~55% of its per-number support. The result prices the purity tier as a package (purity plus its volume cost), not purity alone. The disentangling arm (0.99 tier with the per-tracklet cap raised to match volume) was NOT run. RESOLVED SAME DAY by v8-w3-019: the volume-matched purity arm was built and trained (ARM P100, 0.99 tier at 4x caps, 97,347 rows = 1.0227x ARM V) and still loses to ARM V by -0.0255 at p=0.0020, so the purity loss is not a volume artifact.

SUPERSEDED SAME DAY by v8-w3-018: run-to-run seed variance was unmeasured when this claim was written and is now measured at a spread of 0.0059 over three ARM V retrains, so the -0.0160 is 2.7x the seed noise and the verdict stands without a single-seed caveat. The McNemar p-values still quantify crop-level pairing only.
Measured at the component level only. The ladder stopped at rung 1, so no tracklet density and no GS-HOTA number exists for either arm.
DEV-20 is used here as the clean comparison; it is registered in the session's section 1.5 as a non-gating secondary, and the gating rung-1 slice (GSR train) was compromised by v8-w3-016.

claims.statement: NULL RESULT on the corpus the whole of v8-W3 was built to produce. ARM V retrains the shipped PARSeq reader on the full jersey-2023 legibility pass (48,567 rows against S2's 38,133 from a sample), plus SoccerNet-v3 42,479, plus 896 of Sid's human-sourced rows, minus 12 held-out GSR-train sequences -- 83,812 train rows at the identical arm-4t recipe -- and scores 0.8293 per-crop precision on DEV-20 against the incumbent's 0.8344 at the same 0.2761 emit: -0.0051, paired exact McNemar 38 vs 45 discordant, p=0.51. The expanded corpus neither helps nor hurts. W3's measured value is its two annotation findings (v8-w3-007, v8-w3-010) and the corpus itself, not a better component. STRENGTHENED 2026-08-14: the -0.0051 is smaller than the 0.0059 run-to-run seed spread measured on this exact corpus (v8-w3-018), so ARM V is indistinguishable from the incumbent at seed noise rather than slightly worse -- a retrain at seed 1 scores +0.0008.

ARM V differs from arm 4t in three ways at once (full jersey-2023 pass, Sid's rows, 12 sequences removed), so it prices the package and cannot attribute the null to any one of them.
Sid's human rows are 0.9% of ARM V; the session cannot say whether human labels help, only that nothing moves at this dose.
Single seed, no repeats (see v8-w3-014). -- MEASURED 2026-08-14 at a spread of 0.0059 over three retrains, v8-w3-018.

claims.statement: METHODOLOGY HAZARD, measured: a held-out GSR-train sequence slice cannot referee a new reader against the shipped incumbent, because the incumbent trained on all 57 train sequences. CLUSTER_SESSION_S2.md's build_corpus.gsr_train() applies no sequence filter, and re-running it shows that 831 of the 877 crops passing the eval gate on the registered 12-sequence holdout -- 94.75% -- are rows of arm 4t's own training corpus. The incumbent scores 0.9692 per-crop precision there against 0.8344 on DEV-20, i.e. the holdout measures training-set recall. The registered rung-1 verdict (both W3 arms FAIL, -0.0331 and -0.0752 against a +0.02 bar) stands as registered but is near-uninformative about reader quality; the informative read is the DEV-20 secondary of v8-w3-014. The risk was DECLARED a priori in the session's section 1.3 as an upward bias on the baseline; what was not anticipated was the magnitude, which makes the rung diagnostically weak rather than merely conservative.
Says nothing about DEV-20, which CLUSTER_SESSION_S2.md 3.3 records as never entering any corpus.

claims.statement: CORRECTION to the framing of v8-w3-006 and STATUS 2026-08-13: the '3.7x what the incumbent reader was trained on' headline does not survive the training recipe, because the arm-4t corpus builder caps jersey-2023 at 60 crops per tracklet. The full pass's 140,278 admitted crops over 926 tracklets yield 48,567 trainable rows after the cap, against the 38,133 S2 took from a 201,313-crop sample -- +27%, not +268%. At the 0.99 purity tier the same cap turns 82,941 crops into 37,098 rows, so a 41% cut in crops is only a 24% cut in rows. The binding constraint on corpus size is the per-tracklet cap, not the number of admitted crops, and any future 'the corpus is now N times larger' claim has to be stated after the cap.
