Confirmed against the corpora actually built this session.
caveats: This is a property of the arm-4t recipe, not of the data: raising the cap would convert more of the pool, and whether that helps is unmeasured (the volume arm at cap 60 is already a null, v8-w3-015).
Does not touch v8-w3-006's measured counts, only the 'x times larger' framing built on them.

claims.statement: MEASURED NOISE FLOOR for the project's PARSeq reader recipe: retraining the identical ARM V corpus (byte-identical LMDB, same arm-4t recipe, same command line) three times with nothing varying but the training RNG gives DEV-20 per-crop precisions of 0.8293 (seed U, the original unseeded run), 0.8352 (seed 1) and 0.8293 (seed 2) at the incumbent's emit 0.2761 over 1,371 reads -- a spread of 0.0059, i.e. 8 crops of 1,371. Two consequences were registered before the runs and both fire: (a) the ARM P minus ARM V head-to-head delta of -0.0160 (v8-w3-014) is 2.7x this spread, so it is NOT training-seed noise and H1 stays refuted; (b) ARM V's -0.0051 gap to the incumbent (v8-w3-015) is SMALLER than the spread, so the W3 corpus is indistinguishable from the shipped reader rather than slightly worse -- the sign of that gap is not even stable across retrains, since seed 1 scores +0.0008. The recipe sets no seed at all (no seed_everything call and no seed key in str/parseq's configs), so the original run drew default entropy and never recorded it; the two repeats were pinned with seed_everything(1) and seed_everything(2) by a wrapper that leaves train.py untouched.
claims.unit: max-min DEV-20 per-crop precision across 3 same-corpus ARM V retrains
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W3_TRAIN.md#11.2 Q1 -- seed variance of ARM V: spread = 0.0059
results/GSR_V8_W3_TRAIN.md#10.1 Q1 -- seed variance of ARM V (the binding unknown)
claims.method: Two extra trainings on a100server1 GPU 1 under tmux, corpus reused not rebuilt (armV train shards md5 b2f341e8f20872c3b7acbe231afdc656 / 016b42d78e7726be59b99a1581f68cbe / f00d3cdbf18cd2859d7883775ef48c38, val ca230adeda9a86121207a773d81f0f54), seeds pinned by ~/work/w3/train_seeded.py which calls pytorch_lightning.seed_everything and then execs the stock train.py with an unchanged argument list. Scored by ~/work/w3/w3_component.py unmodified on ~/data/dev20 at legibility 0.5 with the torso gate on; the incumbent was re-scored inside every pass and returned emit 0.2761 / precision 0.8344 / 1,144 correct every time, which is the harness-validity check. cuDNN non-determinism was left as the recipe has it, so the spread is run-to-run variance of the shipped recipe. Checkpoints md5 6227f9f9b4a2b856d74194da52250a55 (seed 1) and e4a830da571716c0f7f70cf76f906e8a (seed 2), both differing from seed U's 8b80904a099adafe8e3fe22a8a557f6b.
caveats: n=3 is a range, not a variance estimate with an interval; a fourth run could widen it.

Measured on one corpus (ARM V, 83,812 train rows) at one recipe. A smaller corpus need not share this noise floor, so the number should not be transferred to ARM P or to any future arm without re-measuring.

Two of the three runs are explicitly seeded and one is not, so these are three independent draws from the recipe's training randomness rather than a designed seed sweep; 'seed 1' is not bit-for-bit reproducible because cuDNN non-determinism was left in place.
Component level only: per-crop precision on DEV-20, not GS-HOTA. How seed noise propagates through tracklet aggregation is unmeasured.
The three runs were not paired against each other (no seed-vs-seed McNemar); only the precision spread was registered and run.

claims.statement: DECONFOUNDED, and the answer hardens the negative: the 0.99 legibility tier's loss is NOT a volume artifact -- purity itself is harmful. ARM P100 is the 0.99 tier with every per-group cap raised 4x (240 crops per jersey-2023 tracklet, per GSR track and per tier-A tracklet; 48 per SoccerNet-v3 game x number), the multiplier computed from the manifests and registered before training: 97,347 rows = 1.0227x ARM V's 95,184, inside the registered +/-10% band, and 86,400 train rows after torso conversion against ARM V's 83,812, so P100 is marginally the LARGER corpus. Same recipe, same shared torso cache, rung 0 clean (0 non-train-split rows, 0 held-out-sequence rows, 0 empty labels, 0 missing files). On DEV-20 at emit 0.2761 it scores 0.8038 against ARM V's 0.8293: -0.0255, paired exact McNemar 44 P100-only-correct vs 79 ARM-V-only-correct, p=0.0020; against the incumbent -0.0306 (43/85, p=0.00026). The delta is 4.3x the seed spread of v8-w3-018 and sits below the lowest of the three ARM V seeds, so no reachable seed reverses it. The registered softening branch ('purity buys nothing at matched volume') did not fire: filtering the corpus at 0.99 discards useful hard examples, and restoring the row count by sampling deeper into the same clean tracklets recovers none of the loss.
claims.unit: per-crop precision, ARM P100 (0.99 tier, volume-matched) minus ARM V, DEV-20 at emit 0.2761
evidence: results/GSR_V8_W3_TRAIN.md#11.3 Q2 -- ARM P100, the deconfound: purity itself is harmful
results/GSR_V8_W3_TRAIN.md#10.2 Q2 -- ARM P100, the purity/volume deconfound
claims.method: ~/work/w3/p100.py drives build_w3_corpus.build_rows unmodified with the per-group caps multiplied, so tier logic, cap_per_group(random_state=0), dedup and the holdout filter are the ones ARM P and ARM V used; the multiplier was chosen by the pre-registered rule (smallest |rows - 95,184| among multipliers inside +/-10%) from a full scan recorded before training. Torso RoIs came from the same shared content-addressed cache (28,303 new conversions, 62,644 reused, survival 0.9343). Trained on a100server1 GPU 1 under tmux at seed_everything(1), 25 epochs, batch 128, shipped-Koshkina init, last.ckpt, ckpt md5 ee62d21a6a68d65a1bff86f8d14cbe0e. Scored by w3_component.py unmodified with --ckpt-a = ARM V seed U, the same pairing H1_P_vs_V.json used; the incumbent context pass reproduced emit 0.2761 / precision 0.8344.
caveats: Total volume is matched but the source MIXTURE is not, and cannot be: the 0.99 tier holds only 18,535 SoccerNet-v3 crops in total, so P100 is 77.3% jersey-2023 / 20.0% v3 post-torso against ARM V's 49.3% / 46.3%. Since CLUSTER_SESSION_S2.md measured v3 as the dominant source of the reader's accuracy, part of the -0.0255 belongs to thinner v3 support. The defensible statement is 'at matched row count the best corpus the 0.99 tier can build is significantly worse than the 0.7 tier's', which is the practical question.

Matched rows are not matched diversity: P100 reaches volume by taking up to 240 crops from each of 831 jersey-2023 tracklets instead of 60 from each of 926, so its rows are more correlated. Unavoidable when volume-matching a purity tier.

P100 (-0.0306 vs the incumbent) lands FURTHER down than ARM P (-0.0211) rather than partway back, but P100 and ARM P were never paired in a McNemar pass and the 0.0095 gap is only ~1.6x the seed spread, so no claim is made from that ordering.
One seed for P100 (seed 1). Vocabulary is 82 numbers as ARM P's was; v8-w3-014's vocabulary control already measured that vocabulary is not the driver.
Component level only -- no tracklet density, no GS-HOTA, no TEST read, nothing shipped.

claims.statement: MODEL LINEAGE IS BUILDABLE, NOT CLEAN-ROOM. All three DanceTrack-lineage associators carry permissive licences with self-contained training code: TWiX (Guepardow/TWiX, arXiv 2403.08018, MIT (c) 2024 Mehdi Miah, 13 stars, last commit 2024-11-29, src/association/twix/{data,train,twix,loss}.py); MOTIP (MCG-NJU/MOTIP, CVPR 2025, Apache-2.0, 553 stars, last commit 2026-07-30, train.py + configs + vendored TrackEval); SUSHI (dvl-tum/SUSHI, CVPR 2023, MIT, 142 stars, last commit 2024-12-22, src/ + configs + scripts). Verdict USABLE-DIRECT for all three; W2 may build from the code rather than clean-room from the papers. Two source-level notes that change the port: TWiX is not a plain pairwise scorer (inter_pair attention scores each candidate pair in the context of the other pairs in its window), and its NormCoords rescales each window's coordinates to [-1,1] - correct for image coordinates, WRONG for metric ones where absolute scale (a 9 m/s bound, a 105x68 m pitch) is the signal.
claims.unit: repos cleared USABLE-DIRECT (permissive licence + self-contained training code)
evidence: results/GSR_V9_W1.md#2. Task A -- model-lineage licence check
claims.method: GitHub REST metadata (licence SPDX, stars, last commit date), repo file trees, LICENSE headers on each default branch, the TWiX README training recipe and a read of src/association/twix/twix.py. Nothing was cloned into this repo tree.
caveats: Licence of the CODE only; the benchmark datasets those repos train on (MOT17, DanceTrack, KITTI) carry their own terms and are not needed here.

claims.statement: THE ASSOCIATOR TRAINING SET EXISTS AND IS LEAKAGE-CLEAN. The frozen v6 chain (S4b detector -> ByteTrack -> PnLCalib -> calibration gate/fill -> EIoU e0.3 r1 w_app0.5 app_max0.30, NO GTA connector, NO solver; jersey reader ON) was extracted over all 57 GSR TRAIN sequences on cluster GPU 1 in 97.6 min = 1.63 GPU-h - nothing for train existed server-side beforehand (0/57 in every artifact directory). EIoU turns 3,061 ByteTrack tracks into 5,787 tracklets (1.89x). The dataset (outputs/gsr/v9_assoc/v1, 33 MB) holds 657,776 labelled detection rows, 4,709 tracklets (82.6 per sequence, 84.4% with a trusted GT identity), 1,342 GT identities and 121,106 candidate tracklet pairs: 5,561 positive / 72,936 negative / 42,609 unlabelled, a 7.08% positive rate among labelled pairs. The physics-only candidate generator (no temporal overlap, gap closable at 9 m/s + 2 m slack) keeps 98.51% of all true same-identity pairs, which is the associator's recall ceiling. Validation is held out BY SEQUENCE (every 5th, 12 sequences); DEV-20, TEST-38, test-49 and challenge were never read - the leakage check is code that raises before the manifest is written and reports zero overlap with the valid and test splits.
claims.unit: candidate tracklet pairs over the 57 GSR train sequences
claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_factory --stage eiou then --stage dataset, run on the cluster with the module md5-identical to the laptop copy. Per-row GT ids from eval.gsr_gta.gt_rows at the evaluator's 5 m tolerance (players/GKs via generator.track_relink.load_gt_ids_by_frame, referees via a referee-only map), majority label per tracklet behind a >=5 audited-row floor; pair features are metric kinematics, team/role, jersey evidence and the CLIP tracklet-mean cosine.
caveats: Labels are 5 m GT-proximity labels, not identity truth: 13.3% of tracklets audit below 0.8 purity, so W2 must weight or filter by purity and report the sensitivity.
35% of candidate pairs are unlabelled (one side has no trusted GT identity); they are kept because inference faces them, but treating them as negatives would be a silent labelling decision.
New-stack extraction (see v8-w4-004): fine as training data, but any W3 evaluation must build its own same-stack control.

claims.statement: PREMISE CORRECTION ON FRAGMENTATION. The v9 brief's '~11.5 EIoU fragments per GT identity' is the OLD-detector number (GSR_EIOU.md); on the stack we actually ship, GSR_V7_V4S1.md 3.2 had already measured 7.91 (DEV-20, 'touch' definition: any track id that touches a GT identity counts). The GSR train split measures 7.25 by that same definition, and row-weighted tracklet purity 0.9576 against DEV-20's 0.9395 - i.e. the training distribution matches the evaluation stack to within 0.7 fragments. Under the stricter dominant-label definition (a tracklet counts only for the identity it mostly is) fragmentation is 2.98 per identity: most 'touches' are a handful of rows in passing, not a fragment worth merging.
claims.unit: fragments per GT identity, touch definition, GSR train, v6 stack
evidence: results/GSR_V7_V4S1.md#3.2 Contamination -- the GT purity audit on the new detector
claims.method: Both definitions computed in tools.gsr_v9_factory.build_sequence; the touch definition and the row-weighted purity reuse generator.gta_link.tracklet_purity, the same instrument tools.gsr_eiou.partition_purity uses for the on-record numbers.
caveats: Train vs DEV-20 is a cross-split comparison on one code path, not a paired measurement.

claims.statement: THE INCUMBENT CONNECTOR'S HARD GATES FORBID 19.83% OF ALL TRUE MERGES. Measured on the 4,039 true same-identity tracklet pairs of the development portion (45 train sequences; the 12-sequence validation slice was not looked at): the GTA connector's same-team requirement alone forbids 16.59% of them, same-role 1.51%, team-or-role 17.63%, the jersey-disagreement veto a further 2.72%, and all three together 19.83%. Its recall ceiling on this distribution is therefore 0.802 at ANY tau, before appearance is consulted, while the physics-only candidate generator keeps 0.985. This is the measured case for carrying team/role/jersey as FEATURES rather than filters in the learned associator: one merge in five sits behind gates the incumbent cannot open.
claims.unit: share of true tracklet merges structurally unreachable by the GTA connector
evidence: results/GSR_V9_W1.md#4.4 The finding that changes the W2 case
claims.method: Pair table of tools.gsr_v9_factory over the 45 development sequences; the gate definitions read off generator.gta_link.connect (role equality, team equality, jersey-number disagreement veto).
caveats: Team and role labels are our own predictions, so part of the 16.59% is our team-assignment error rather than a genuinely cross-team merge - which is precisely why a model allowed to override a wrong team label has headroom here.
Pairwise, not the connector's agglomerative procedure: this is a ceiling on its recall, not a rerun of the connector, and it is not comparable to its on-record 0.5432 merge precision.
Raw pair table: outputs/gsr/v9_assoc/v1/pairs/*.parquet (57 files, cluster + laptop).

claims.statement: PREMISE CONTRADICTION, STATED PLAINLY: A PERFECT MERGER DOES NOT REACH 61.48. Our board entry is GS-HOTA 53.08 = sqrt(DetA 39.32 x AssA 71.67). Carrying V4S1's association oracles into that identity at fixed DetA: the merge-only oracle (+11.89 AssA -> 83.56) gives GS-HOTA 57.32, i.e. +4.24 and about 4.2 points SHORT of the 61.48 target; only the split+merge oracle (+24.79 AssA -> 96.46) reaches 61.59. A merge-only associator realising 100% of its oracle would still miss the campaign goal, so the associator has to be paired with a splitter for contaminated tracklets (13.3% of tracklets audit below 0.8 purity) and/or a GS-DetA lever.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA reachable at the merge-only oracle with DetA held at 39.32
evidence: results/GSR_V9_W1.md#1. Ceiling math -- what +11.9 is, and what it is not
claims.method: GS-HOTA = sqrt(GS-DetA x GS-AssA) applied to the on-record test-49 components, with the V4S1 oracle deltas added to AssA and DetA held fixed.
caveats: The oracle deltas were measured on DEV-20's loc_assoc proxy scale and are applied additively to test-49; cross-split additivity is an assumption (DEV-20 tracked valid-58 to within 0.008 on the ceiling), and the proxy carries about +-3 AssA.
The conclusion's direction survives V4S1's alternative linear mapping (+19.36 at split+merge), which is itself below the target's requirement at merge-only.
STATUS.md 2026-08-06: test-49 read 53.08 / DetA 39.32 / AssA 71.67

claims.statement: ARTIFACT HAZARD: outputs/gsr/positions_gate_v6det_eiou/ IS OVERWRITTEN IN PLACE BY EVERY EIoU ARM. tools.gsr_eiou.write_variant writes <positions_subdir>_eiou with no arm key, so the directory holds whichever arm ran last. The laptop's SNGS-021 copy audits at row purity 0.7098 with 35 tracklets against its own input's 47 ByteTrack tracks - FEWER tracklets than the input, which EIoU never produces (it fragments 1.89x) - against the on-record DEV-20 figures of 0.9395 purity and 7.91 frag/GT. It is therefore some later session's arm, not the frozen v6 partition. Any session reading those laptop files as 'the v6 tracker output' is reading the wrong artifact; rebuild with tools.gsr_eiou.build_arm_artifacts first. W1's train-split artifacts were built fresh server-side and are unaffected.
claims.unit: row purity of the laptop SNGS-021 _eiou artifact against the on-record 0.9395
evidence: results/GSR_V7_V4S1.md#3.2 Contamination -- the GT purity audit on the new detector
claims.method: tools.gsr_eiou.partition_purity on the laptop's positions_gate_v6det and positions_gate_v6det_eiou for SNGS-021, compared against the V4S1 on-record table.
caveats: Checked on one sequence; the directory's mtimes span 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-13, so the contents are probably a mixture of arms rather than one single wrong arm.

claims.statement: INCUMBENT BASELINE ON THE REGISTERED VALIDATION SLICE (measured before any training). The shipped GTA connector (generator.gta_link.connect, tau 0.450, jersey gate ON, team/role gates ON, splitter OFF) run on the W1 EIoU partition of the 12 registered train-split validation sequences: 1,095 tracklets (279 GT identities) -> 450 components, 645 merges, pair-level merge precision 0.7492, fragments per GT identity 3.315 -> 1.799, row-weighted purity 0.9490 -> 0.9313, and an implied pair ranking (-clip_cos_dist with its hard gates) of average precision 0.5586 over 20,733 labelled candidate pairs (7.34% positive). These are the a-priori bars for W2's gates G1-G3. NOT comparable to the on-record 0.5432 from GSR_V7_V4S1.md, which is DEV-20, post-splitter, on the shipped chain.
claims.unit: pair-level merge precision of the incumbent connector, validation slice
evidence: results/GSR_V9_W2.md#1.2 Incumbent baseline -- measured on the validation slice BEFORE training
claims.method: python -m tools.gsr_v9_train --stage baseline; merge precision via generator.track_relink.merge_precision over the connector's components, purity via generator.gta_link.tracklet_purity on the remapped rows, fragments per GT identity over tracklets carrying a trusted dominant GT id.
caveats: GT-proximity labels (nearest GT within 5 m), so absolute levels are optimistic; the model and the incumbent are scored against the same labels.
Connector-only: the splitter is costed separately (v9-w2-005) because it is inert on this chain.

claims.statement: REGISTERED VERDICT: THE METRIC-SPACE TWiX ASSOCIATOR FAILS ITS W2 GATE. A 72,385-parameter metric-space port of TWiX (MIT, Guepardow/TWiX; NormCoords dropped, (x, y, vx, vy) in m and m/s under constant normalisation, inter_pair attention kept, team/role/jersey/CLIP carried as side FEATURES not filters) trained on 40 GSR-train sequences, epoch chosen on a 5-sequence inner-val slice, measured on the 12 registered validation sequences, 3 seeds. G1 (pair-ranking AP > 0.5586): 0.6579 mean, seeds 0.676/0.622/0.676, noise floor (max-min) 0.0540 -> PASS by +0.0993. G2 (merge precision at the incumbent's matched 645 merges >= 0.7492 + 0.05 = 0.7992): 0.7260 mean (0.741/0.716/0.721), floor 0.0247 -> FAIL, and below the incumbent's own 0.7492. G3 (frag/GT <= 1.799 at purity >= 0.9313): frag 1.746 PASS, purity 0.9309 FAIL by 0.0004 (inside the 0.0068 floor). Pass required all three: FAIL. Cost 0.043 GPU-h.
claims.unit: merge precision at matched merge count, 3-seed mean (registered bar 0.7992)
claims.method: python -m tools.gsr_v9_train --stage train --seeds 0,1,2 on cluster a100server1 GPU 1; merges matched per sequence to the incumbent's count and accepted greedily by score under the temporal-chain feasibility test only (no team/role/jersey gate); AP over the labelled candidate pairs, unlabelled pairs excluded from the loss but kept as inter-pair context.
caveats: Inner-val (5 sequences) is a noisy epoch selector: seed 1 stopped at epoch 3 of 30 and is the worst seed on the validation slice.
merge_precision is transitive and pair-level, so one wrong link inside a large component is charged many times; applied identically to both arms.
No GS-HOTA was measured in W2; all numbers are W1 proxy instruments on train-split sequences.

claims.statement: A BETTER PAIR RANKING DOES NOT SURVIVE TRANSITIVE LINKAGE. On the same validation rows the trained associator ranks candidate pairs clearly better than the incumbent: raw precision of the top-645 pairs 0.883 mean (0.902/0.854/0.894) against 0.809, and AP 0.716 vs 0.667 even on the same-team subset where the incumbent's gates do not bind. That advantage is worth +0.03 merge precision at 324 merges, ~0.00 at 483 and ~0.00 at 645 -- it gets spent on links that glue large components together. Also measured: 0.011 of the incumbent's 0.7492 is its mean-recomputing agglomerative PROCEDURE, not its ranking (its own scores through our greedy single-linkage merger give 0.7381). Of the model's 645 merges, 8.6% cross a team boundary -- structurally impossible for the incumbent -- at 0.594 precision on the labelled ones.
claims.unit: raw precision of the model's top-645 candidate pairs (incumbent 0.809)
evidence: results/GSR_V9_W2.md#2.3 Why G1 passes and G2 fails
claims.method: Post-hoc diagnostics on the 6 pulled checkpoints, laptop CPU: precision@k over the pooled labelled validation pairs, merge precision at 0.5x/0.75x/1.0x/1.5x the incumbent's merge count, and the team/role/jersey composition of the accepted merges.
caveats: About 135 of the 645 accepted merges are unlabelled pairs, unauditable in either direction (the incumbent spends 138).
Component-level precision depends on linkage order; only the greedy path was measured for the model.

claims.statement: THE METRIC-COORDINATE NOVELTY IS NOT SUPPORTED STANDALONE. The registered kinematics-only ablation (identical model with the side features -- team, role, jersey, CLIP -- removed, so it sees only metric positions, velocities and time) scores val pair-AP 0.2707 (seed spread 0.0116) and merge precision 0.3276, against the incumbent's appearance-with-gates 0.5586/0.7492 and the full model's 0.6579/0.7260. Metric kinematics alone are roughly half as informative as appearance on this distribution. The supported claim is NOT 'metric coordinates beat image-space association' but 'learning the combination beats gating on one signal, at ranking' (+0.099 AP over the incumbent).
claims.unit: val pair-ranking AP, kinematics-only arm (full model 0.6579)
evidence: results/GSR_V9_W2.md#2.4 Ablation -- metric kinematics alone are NOT competitive
claims.method: python -m tools.gsr_v9_train --stage train --seeds 0,1,2 --no-side, identical data, schedule and evaluation to the main arm.
caveats: The kinematic tokens cover a 1.4 s window per side (8 observations at stride 5); a longer or denser trajectory encoding was not tried.
Candidate generation already applies a 9 m/s physical filter, so the easiest kinematic negatives are absent from the pool the ablation is scored on.

claims.statement: THE SHIPPED GTA SPLITTER IS INERT ON THE CLIP-EMBEDDING CHAIN, AND LOOSENING IT MAKES THINGS WORSE. Measured over all 57 GSR-train sequences (4,709 tracklets, 632,710 audited rows, 772 tracklets = 16.4% below 0.8 purity, row-weighted purity 0.9547): at its shipped eps 0.30 the DBSCAN splitter splits 2 tracklets in 57 sequences (purity 0.9547 -> 0.9548); at eps 0.40, none. Its eps was tuned for PRTreID embeddings while the chain now runs CLIP, whose cosine distances are far wider. At eps 0.20 it splits 597 tracklets but reaches only 77 of the 772 contaminated ones (10.0%), 280 cuts land on >= 0.99-pure tracklets, it manufactures 1,052 new fragments (+22.3%), the count of contaminated tracklets RISES 141 -> 183, and purity gains only +0.0046. A per-row GT ORACLE cut splitter splits 872 tracklets, reaches purity 0.9871 (71.5% of the impurity mass) at a cost of +2,642 fragments -- so 28.5% of contamination is interleaved rather than contiguous and NO cut-based splitter can repair it.
claims.unit: tracklets split by the shipped splitter (eps 0.30) across 57 sequences
claims.method: python -m tools.gsr_v9_train --stage split: generator.gta_link.split_tracklets over the mirrored per-detection CLIP caches at eps 0.20/0.30/0.40 (min_samples 5, min_run 5), plus a GT oracle that cuts at every audited identity change with runs under 5 rows absorbed; purity from generator.gta_link.tracklet_purity before and after.
caveats: The eps sweep is a measurement on train-split labels and selects nothing; no arm was carried forward.
min_samples/min_run were left at the shipped 5/5; a joint re-tune of the splitter for CLIP was not attempted.

claims.statement: PREMISE CONTRADICTION SHARPENED: THE SPLIT+MERGE BAND DOES NOT REACH 61.48 EITHER, SO DetA IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT. W1 registered that a perfect merger reaches GS-HOTA 57.32 and that only the split+merge oracle (61.59) clears the 61.48 target. W2 measured what a splitter can actually deliver: apportioning W1's +12.90 AssA split leg by the fraction of impurity mass removed (assumption stated, and optimistic -- it charges nothing for the fragments a split creates), the shipped splitter gives GS-HOTA 57.33, eps 0.20 gives 57.77, and a GROUND-TRUTH cut splitter paired with a PERFECT merger reaches only 60.40 -- still 1.08 short of 61.48. The 61.59 figure needs row-level correction of interleaved contamination, i.e. a tracker replacement, not a splitter. Conversely, hitting 61.48 needs DetA 45.23 with a perfect merger, 40.74 with perfect merge + oracle-cut split, or 52.74 at today's AssA 71.67 -- against today's DetA 39.32. W3 should be a detection/coverage session, not another association session.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA of an oracle-cut splitter + a perfect merger at DetA 39.32
evidence: results/GSR_V9_W1.md#1. Ceiling math -- what +11.9 is, and what it is not
claims.method: GS-HOTA = sqrt(DetA x AssA) on the board entry 53.08 = sqrt(39.32 x 71.67); W1's oracles (AssA 83.56 merge-only, 96.46 split+merge) with the split leg apportioned by the measured impurity-mass removal of each splitter arm (0.2% / 10.2% / 71.5%).
caveats: Linear apportionment of the AssA split leg to impurity mass is an assumption, not a measurement, and it is optimistic (no charge for the extra fragments a split creates).
Inherits W1's cross-split additivity assumption (DEV-20 proxy deltas applied to test-49 levels).
No end-to-end GS-HOTA was run in W2.

claims.statement: THE GS-DetA LOSS IS AN ATTRIBUTE PROBLEM, NOT A DETECTION PROBLEM. Census of the shipped v6 chain on DEV-20 (235,174 GT rows, 213,571 prediction rows, attribute-blind Hungarian match at the evaluator's own 5 m gaussian): we put a prediction within 5 m of 89.93% of GT rows, but only 56.47% of GT rows are also attribute-correct. Exclusive buckets: detection miss 10.07% (8.54 live + 1.53 on the 263 dead frames), role wrong 5.34%, team wrong 5.75%, jersey wrong 22.37% (coverage loss 15.37%, named-wrong 5.68%, over-naming 1.32%), false positives 0.88% of GT. On the fully-correct rows a further 3.76% of GT is lost in row-equivalents to the alpha sweep alone (mean alpha fraction 0.9333). Role confusion is dominated by player->referee (7,032 rows) and referee->player (3,377).
claims.unit: share of DEV-20 GT rows that are position-matched AND attribute-correct
evidence: results/GSR_V9_W3.md#2. The census -- 235,174 GT rows, 213,571 prediction rows, DEV-20
claims.method: Per-frame Hungarian match on the evaluator's gaussian pitch similarity (sigma = 2.0428 m, cut at 5 m) ignoring attributes, then exclusive bucketing in the order role -> team -> jersey using the evaluator's own attribute preprocessing (team only for player/GK rows, jersey only for player rows, None == None matches).
caveats: The census matcher is attribute-blind and unweighted; the evaluator's Hungarian runs on attribute-zeroed similarity weighted by the global alignment score. Point costs come from the official evaluator instead (v9-w3-002).
DEV-20 is the tuning split.

claims.statement: THE RANKED DetA LEVER TABLE (oracle counterfactuals scored with the official evaluator, DEV-20, baseline GS-DetA 39.3083 which reproduces GSR_V6.md to 4 decimals; the all-fixed arm returns exactly 100.00). Fixing ONE bucket: jersey +24.74 (coverage loss +16.36, named-wrong +5.06, over-naming +1.16), all detection misses +6.99 (with GT attributes on the inserted rows), role+team together +6.15, localization +3.74, team +3.47, role +1.42, dead-frame rows +1.12, false-positive removal +0.18. Isolated arms understate badly because a broken row is usually broken on two attributes; leave-one-out marginals are role +8.13, team +13.84, jersey +34.58. TWO PLANNING CONSEQUENCES: (1) FP suppression and dedup are DEAD levers (2,074 FP rows in 213,571 -> +0.18); (2) PERFECT ROLE+TEAM ALONE (+6.15) CLEARS the 45.23 DetA that W2's no-splitter path needs, so the attribute-labelling axis, not the detector, is the campaign's cheapest route.
claims.unit: GS-DetA points from perfect role+team alone on DEV-20 (need: +1.42 to +5.91)
evidence: results/GSR_V9_W3.md#3. The lever table -- oracle cost, DEV-20, official evaluator
claims.method: Counterfactual submissions that rewrite exactly one bucket (attributes copied from the position-matched GT row, or a prediction inserted on every missed GT row, or matched rows snapped onto GT positions, or unmatched predictions dropped), each scored with eval.gsr_score.gs_hota under the gs_hota_full config.
caveats: Isolated oracles are not additive; both brackets [isolated, marginal] are reported.
The nomiss arms grant perfect attributes AND perfect association on inserted rows, so their DetA is an upper bound and their GS-HOTA is meaningless.
DEV-20 is the tuning split; transfer to test-49 rests on DEV-20 DetA 39.31 vs test-49 39.32.

claims.statement: PREMISE CORRECTION: SMALL-BOX RECALL IS NOT THE DETECTION LEVER. Measured end to end on DEV-20, our recall on GT boxes under 40 px of image height is 0.538 -- which reproduces S4b's on-record 0.55 and validates the instrument -- but boxes under 40 px are only 1.57% of GT rows and 7.2% of all detection misses. Recall is 0.899 overall and still only 0.922 in the top height decile, so the miss mass is spread across every size bin. Perfect recall below 40 px recovers 1,708 of 23,677 missed rows. Crowding (best GT-GT image-box IoU > 0.3) costs ~0.10 recall (0.809 vs 0.906) on 7% of GT.
claims.unit: share of all DEV-20 detection misses that sit on GT boxes under 40 px
evidence: results/GSR_V9_W3.md#2. The census -- 235,174 GT rows, 213,571 prediction rows, DEV-20
claims.method: GT bbox_image height percentiles over all DEV-20 GT person rows, split by whether the attribute-blind matcher found a prediction within 5 m; occlusion proxied by the best image-box IoU with another GT box in the same frame.
caveats: Height is GT box height in pixels, a proxy for distance, not a measured range.
The IoU>0.3 crowding proxy is not the dataset's occlusion label (there is none).

claims.statement: REGISTERED PASS, ZERO GPU: a per-track majority vote on the submission's own attributes is worth +1.7999 GS-DetA and +2.9887 GS-HOTA on DEV-20 (39.3083 -> 41.1082, 51.8083 -> 54.7970), 20 sequences helped / 0 hurt, Wilcoxon p = 1.9e-06, against a registered bar of +0.50 DetA. The control is the same submission untouched (identical GPU artifacts, deterministic operation, noise floor exactly 0). Mechanism: our chain lets one track disagree with itself -- 4.60% of rows carry a minority role, 6.36% a minority team, 2.22% a minority jersey -- while a GT identity has one role and one team for the whole clip. TWO HONEST QUALIFIERS: role voting ALONE is NEGATIVE on DetA (-0.128, it destroys the rows where the minority was right, e.g. a GK correctly detected inside a mostly-player track), and the largest leg (+1.05 DetA) is a WRITER REPAIR -- gsr_deleak.write_arm writes the solver's number only onto rows whose per-row role is 'player', so goalkeeper/referee-labelled rows of a named track kept jersey null. Ships default OFF (eval.gsr_score.VOTE_TRACK_ATTRS = ()); no TEST-38, test-49 or challenge contact.
claims.unit: GS-DetA points on DEV-20 from the per-track attribute vote (bar: +0.50)
evidence: results/GSR_V9_W3.md#4. Stage 2 -- the per-track attribute vote
claims.method: eval.gsr_score.vote_track_attributes collapses each track's role/team/jersey onto its majority non-null value (ties keep the first-seen value); four arms registered a priori (role, team, role+team, role+team+jersey), each scored with the official evaluator against the untouched shipped DEV-20 arm.
caveats: DEV-20 is the tuning split; this is not a board number and no submission was built.
Transfer to test-49 inherits W1's cross-split assumption (DEV-20 DetA tracked test-49 to 0.01 before this change).
GS-AssA also rises (+4.76) because the metric already cuts an inconsistent track into pieces; this was a DetA session and the AssA gain is reported, not claimed.
The component stays default OFF pending a TEST-38 confirmation and a bundle decision.

claims.statement: THE JERSEY-COVERAGE LEVER IS NOT AN OPERATING-POINT PROBLEM. Jersey coverage loss (GT numbered, we emit null) is the single largest DetA bucket -- 15.37% of DEV-20 GT rows, oracle +16.36 GS-DetA -- but three separate bounds cut it down: (a) restricted to numbers our own GT-free chain actually emits somewhere in the sequence, the oracle falls to +8.15; (b) the frozen solver config already carries r_abstain = 0.0, i.e. the abstention dial is fully open and the solver leaves tracklets unnamed for lack of a slot, not for want of payoff; (c) on the 10 cached DEV bundles, 309 of 478 tracklets carry no confident crop read at all and hold 24,543 numbered GT rows (29% of the numbered mass). Under GS-DetA a WRONG number costs exactly what null costs on a numbered GT row, so trading coverage for precision is DetA-neutral at best -- the remaining lever is reader/roster quality, not policy.
claims.unit: GS-DetA points from oracle jersey coverage restricted to our own emitted roster
evidence: results/GSR_V9_W3.md#3.1 Ranked levers with an honest achievable fraction
claims.method: Oracle arm jersey_coverage_roster: fix jersey only on rows where the GT number appears in the (team side, number) set the submission itself emits for that sequence; scored with the official evaluator. Read availability from the cached identity bundles of the shipped arm.
caveats: The emitted-number set is a proxy for the solver's self-roster, not its slot set.
The read-availability figure covers 10 of the 20 DEV bundles cached on the laptop.

claims.statement: AFTER THE W3 VOTE, THE LARGEST REACHABLE ATTRIBUTE BUCKET IS THE GOALKEEPER'S TEAM. Per-track anatomy of the voted DEV-20 submission (885 prediction tracks, 213,571 rows, attribute-blind Hungarian match to GT, a track owned by the GT identity holding most of its matched rows): 586 tracks (83.41% of rows) carry the right role AND team; 111 tracks (9.32%) are CONTAMINATED (dominant GT identity owns < 70% of matched rows, so no relabelling can fix them); 92 tracks (3.97%) carry the wrong team and 70 (3.23%) the wrong role. Track-level relabel oracles, scored with the official evaluator on top of the voted control (GS-DetA 41.1082): the whole goalkeeper bucket is worth +3.0190 GS-DetA -- team-wrong keepers +2.2676 (29 tracks / 5,257 rows), keepers we call players +0.7597 (13 tracks) -- against referee<->player confusions +1.6341 combined, outfield team errors +0.4973 (63 tracks) and contaminated tracks +0.3365. TWO PLANNING CONSEQUENCES: track-level kit RE-CLUSTERING IS A DEAD LEVER (a perfect track-level team classifier for outfield players is worth +0.50, below the +0.75 bar), and CONTAMINATED TRACKS ARE AN ASSOCIATION PROBLEM WORTH ONLY +0.34, not an attribute one.
claims.unit: GS-DetA points from a perfect track-level relabel of the goalkeeper bucket, DEV-20
claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w4 --anatomy / --oracles. Anatomy: the W3 census matcher (gaussian at the evaluator's own sigma, cut at 5 m, attribute-blind) aggregated per prediction track. Oracles: for the tracks of one bucket, every row's role/team is forced onto the dominant GT identity's value and the submission is scored with eval.gsr_score.gs_hota under gs_hota_full. Control = the shipped v6 DEV-20 arm with vote_track_attributes applied, which reproduces the on-record 41.1082 / 54.7970 exactly.
caveats: The 70% purity floor that defines CONTAMINATED is fixed a priori, not tuned.
Isolated bucket oracles are not additive (a row can be wrong on both role and team).
DEV-20 is the tuning split.

claims.statement: REGISTERED PASS, ZERO GPU: A KEEPER'S TEAM IS THE GOAL HE STANDS IN, AND THAT RULE IS ORACLE-EQUIVALENT. Setting team = 'left' if a goalkeeper track's median pitch x < 0 else 'right' -- reading only our own predictions -- is worth +2.2676 GS-DetA and +1.4631 GS-HOTA on DEV-20 on top of the W3 vote (41.1082 -> 43.3757, 54.7970 -> 56.2601) against a registered bar of +0.75 DetA, with 18 sequences helped / 0 hurt on BOTH DetA and HOTA (Wilcoxon p = 1.96e-04; the other 2 sequences unchanged). It recovers the bucket's oracle value +2.2676 TO FOUR DECIMALS: the geometric rule is as good as knowing the answer. Row-level audit: 5,171 rows wrong -> right, 31 wrong -> wrong, ZERO right -> wrong. Adding the positional role step gives gk_side_role +2.2923 DetA / +1.4782 HOTA, also 18/0. Stacked on the shipped v6 chain the W3+W4 components take DEV-20 from 39.3083 / 51.8083 to 43.4004 / 56.2752 (+4.09 DetA, +4.47 HOTA) for 0.000 GPU-h. Mechanism: GSR's left/right is the half a team DEFENDS, and kit clustering is ANTI-informative for keepers (a GK kit contrasts with both outfield kits by regulation) -- our chain had the keeper's team wrong on 42 of 52 keeper-owned tracks. Ships default OFF (eval.gsr_score.GK_SIDE_REPAIR = ()), composable with VOTE_TRACK_ATTRS.
claims.unit: GS-DetA points on DEV-20 from the GT-free keeper side rule (bar: +0.75)
claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w4 --arms. Control = the same submission with the W3 vote only; both arms are deterministic pure functions of the submission JSON, so the GPU artifacts are byte-identical and the experimental noise floor is exactly 0. Arms and bars were written to results/gsr_v9_w4_registered.json before either was scored. The side rule was checked on GSR-TRAIN ground truth first: 79/79 keeper identities.
caveats: DEV-20 is the tuning split; this is not a board number and no submission was built.
The rule needs a keeper to be LABELLED a keeper: it does nothing for the 13 tracks that are keepers our role model calls players (+0.7597 DetA still on the table).
31 rows stay wrong: 3 tracks we call goalkeeper are GT players and the rule assigns them a side by geometry (2 of those rows go right -> wrong there). Net right -> wrong over the whole split is 0.
Ships default OFF pending a TEST-38 confirmation and a bundle decision.

claims.statement: THE GT-FREE POSITIONAL KEEPER-ROLE RULE IS PRECISE AND NEARLY INERT, BECAUSE OF FRAGMENTATION. Fitted on GSR-TRAIN ground truth ONLY (57 sequences, 79 keeper and 1,145 player identities), 'the most extreme candidate on a half of the pitch with median |x| >= 36 m and penalty-area share >= 0.90 is that half's keeper' scores 67 TP / 1 FP / 12 FN, while the same thresholds WITHOUT the most-extreme-per-side selector run at precision 0.74. Applied to DEV-20 under the structural guard 'only on a half that carries no goalkeeper track at all', it fires ONCE in 20 sequences (SNGS-081 track 58, a true keeper, 54 rows): precision 1/1, but recall 54 of the 1,773 keeper-as-player rows = 3%, worth +0.0247 GS-DetA of that bucket's +0.7597. The reason is fragmentation: our tracker splits a keeper into several tracks and usually labels at least one of them goalkeeper, so the guard blocks the rest. The remaining +0.73 DetA needs a rule that can add a SECOND keeper track to a half, which cannot be fit on train GT (GT roles are perfect there) and was therefore NOT built in this session.
claims.unit: GS-DetA points on DEV-20 from the positional keeper-role step (bucket oracle 0.76)
claims.method: Thresholds fit on GSR-TRAIN Labels-GameState.json only (per GT identity: median |x| and share of frames inside a FIFA penalty area), then applied unchanged to DEV-20 through eval.gsr_score.gk_side_repair with steps ('role','team'). No DEV score was consulted before the arm was registered.
caveats: One firing on 20 sequences is a sample of 1; its 1/1 precision carries no error bar.
The train fit is on GT positions while the arm runs on our projected positions -- a domain shift the fit cannot see.

claims.statement: THE REFEREE<->PLAYER AXIS HAS NO GT-FREE MECHANISM: REGISTERED REFUSAL OF THE LARGEST REMAINING BUCKET (+1.63 GS-DetA oracle). Three independent signals were measured on the W4 control and all three fail. (1) GEOMETRY: the referee-owned player-voted bucket is the MAIN referee, median |y| 7.94 m, not the touchline assistants -- our detector already labels 51 central referee tracks (7,831 rows correct) and 43 touchline ones, so no |y| rule separates the 3,355-row bucket from the 9,946 rows it would break. (2) ROLE FLICKER: per-row referee share on the unvoted submission is median 0.880 on GT-referee tracks vs 0.000 on GT-player tracks, but 24.4% of player tracks carry some referee row and 14.5% carry >= 0.10; the best threshold (0.30) wins 2,456 rows and loses 3,497. (3) KIT DISTINCTNESS IS TRUE BUT TOO WEAK, AND THE GK TRAP IS WORSE THAN ASSUMED: distance from a track's mean CLIP embedding to the nearer team centroid separates referees from players at AUC 0.8821, yet GOALKEEPERS SIT FARTHER OUT THAN REFEREES (median 0.949 vs 0.900 vs 0.678), and at the 90th player percentile the rule catches 12 of 26 referees while hitting 23 of 225 players (precision 0.34). No arm was built on this axis.

caveats: The kit measurement uses only the 9 DEV sequences whose embedding cache still joins the submission's track ids (267 tracks); the cache joins 790 of 896 tracks overall and is broken on 11 of 20 sequences -- a fresh instance of kb v9-w1-006, which is also why no embedding-based arm could be shipped without re-extraction.
The threshold sweeps are DEV-20 reads used to REFUSE a rule, never to select one.

claims.statement: REGISTERED FAIL: THE CONCURRENCY-GUARDED SECOND-KEEPER RULE IS PRECISE BUT TOO SMALL. Replacing W4's global guard ('this half carries no goalkeeper track at all') with a TEMPORAL one ('this candidate shares no frame with a goalkeeper-majority track on his half' -- two tracks that never coexist can be fragments of one person, two that do cannot) is worth +0.1718 GS-DetA / +0.0695 GS-HOTA on DEV-20 over the W4 control (43.3757 -> 43.5476), against a registered bar of +0.35. The dominance variant (also promote a concurrent candidate that is deeper than every keeper track it overlaps) is worth +0.2142 / +0.0915 (-> 43.5899). Both FAIL the bar; gk_second also fails the paired gate (4 of 20 sequences change, Wilcoxon p = 0.068) while gk_second_dom passes it (5 sequences, p = 0.043). Row-level audit is clean in both: 350 / 447 wrong->right against 4 right->wrong (0.8% / 0.7% of touched rows). No new threshold was introduced: the |x| >= 36 m and penalty-share >= 0.90 gates are W4's train-fitted ones and the concurrency test has no parameter. On GSR-TRAIN GT (57 sequences, 1,145 player identities) the strict rule fires 0 times and the dominance rule 2 times, and every train firing is a false positive by construction. NOTHING SHIPS: the stack stays at vote_all + gk_side(team).

caveats: The bar was moved from the brief's +0.60 to +0.35 BEFORE any arm was scored, because stage 1 showed +0.60 to be arithmetically unreachable on this bucket (see v9-w5-004); the arms fail even the reduced bar.
Only 4-5 of 20 sequences are touched at all, so the paired statistics are weak by construction.

claims.statement: THE KEEPER-AS-PLAYER BUCKET HAS A HARD POSITIONAL CEILING OF ABOUT +0.51 GS-DetA, AND ITS RESIDUAL IS AN ASSOCIATION PROBLEM. Of the 13 tracks / 1,773 rows worth +0.7597 on track-level relabel, TWO tracks (571 rows, 32%) are keepers who left their line entirely -- SNGS-096 t70 (405 rows, median pitch x -22.1 m, penalty share 0.00) and SNGS-093 t56 (166 rows, 26.0 m, 0.00) -- and carry no keeper positional signature at all, so no |x|/penalty rule can ever reach them. Of the remaining 10 tracks that sit on a half already carrying a goalkeeper-labelled track, 5 OVERLAP IT IN TIME (SNGS-042 t26 50 of 529 frames, SNGS-054 t110 9 of 101, SNGS-030 t71 7 of 14, SNGS-027 t114 3 of 68, SNGS-087 t47 2 of 115) -- i.e. the tracker emits two concurrent tracks on the SAME person, which defeats the physical non-coexistence guard and holds ~+0.30 DetA hostage. That is a duplicate-track / dedup problem, not an attribute one.

claims.method: Per-track geometry (median pitch x, penalty-area frame share) and frame-set intersection between each keeper-owned player-voted track and the goalkeeper-majority tracks on its half, on the W4 control submission.
caveats: The +0.51 figure is the bucket oracle scaled by the reachable row share, not a scored arm.

claims.statement: THE OVER-NAMING EXPOSURE OF ANY JERSEY-PROPAGATION SCHEME, MEASURED ON BOTH SPLITS. On GSR-TRAIN (57 sequences, the W1 EIoU partition) 2,609 player-majority tracklets carry no jersey read: 1,514 (159,963 rows) belong to GT identities that ARE numbered, 484 (79,144 rows) to identities GT leaves UNNUMBERED and 611 (3,315 rows) have no trusted GT identity -- so 24.2% of the GT-resolvable unnamed player tracklets, and 33.1% of their rows, are rows where writing ANY number destroys a null==null match. On DEV-20 the same census over the shipped control's own tracks is WORSE, not better: 228 unnamed player tracks, 143 GT-numbered (41,707 rows) vs 84 GT-unnumbered (27,809 rows) -- 37.0% of tracks and 40.0% of rows in the danger zone. The reason is structural: the shipped solver has already named most of the numbered players it can reach, so the residual unnamed pool is ENRICHED in identities that were never numbered. The shipped submission also already over-names 81 tracks / 12,888 rows (48 player-labelled, 21 referee-labelled, 12 keeper-labelled) whose GT identity is unnumbered, and those tracks are available as lenders.
claims.unit: percent of DEV-20 unnamed-player-track rows whose GT identity is unnumbered
claims.method: GSR-TRAIN: tools.gsr_v9_w6.calibrate census over the W1 tracklet summaries with per-identity GT jersey from Labels-GameState.json (verified constant per identity). DEV-20: tools.gsr_v9_w6.dev_census, tracks summarised from the control-state submission and owned via the W4/W5 attribute-blind Hungarian matcher (tools.gsr_v9_w5.owners).
caveats: The two censuses use different naming sources by necessity: GSR-TRAIN naming is the per-crop reader's dominant number at the 0.80 confidence floor, DEV-20 naming is the shipped identity solver's decision. That difference is itself the finding.
DEV-20 track ownership uses the 5 m position-only Hungarian match; 10 tracks (104 rows) get no GT owner and are reported separately as gt_unknown.

claims.statement: NAME-BORROWING FAILS ON DEV-20: THE LEARNED ARM LOSES 0.32 GS-DetA AND THE PHYSICS ARM BUYS NOISE. Registered before contact (results/gsr_v9_w6_registered.json): candidates are (named, unnamed) tracklet pairs of the shipped control inside the W1 physics window with both sides player-majority and same known team; the scorer is the frozen W2 TwixMetric seed-ensemble mean logit with the appearance channel forced missing; the threshold -2.5 was the GSR-TRAIN point maximising net rows subject to <= 15% over-naming (943 tracks / 28,347 rows / 15,179 correct / 3,047 over-named / 10.7% over-naming). On DEV-20 that arm fires on 6 tracks / 1,538 rows and scores GS-DetA 43.0518 (-0.3239) / GS-HOTA 56.0468 (-0.2133), 0 sequences helped and 2 hurt (Wilcoxon p = 0.180); its row audit is 1,262 OVER-NAMED (82.1% of touched rows, against the registered 20% ceiling), 270 newly-wrong-named, 6 unmatched and ZERO newly-correct. The registered model-free fallback (rank by required speed) had NO admissible train threshold at all -- its net rows are negative across the whole grid -- and at its least-bad point it scores 43.4001 (+0.0244) / 56.2657 (+0.0057), 3 helped / 0 hurt, p = 0.109, i.e. 2% of the +1.00 gate. Nothing ships; the stack stays at GS-DetA 43.3757 / GS-HOTA 56.2601 and no shipping module was modified.
claims.unit: GS-DetA delta on DEV-20 of the registered twix borrow arm vs the 43.3757 control
claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w6 --traincal then --arms; eval.gsr_score.gs_hota gs_hota_full over the 20 DEV sequences; paired per-sequence Wilcoxon; row audit against the GT jersey of the position-matched GT row.
caveats: Deterministic given the frozen checkpoints, so the noise floor is 0; the failure is not sampling error.

The arm changes only the jersey attribute -- no track was merged and no track_id changed, which the GS-AssA reads confirm (72.9681 twix / 72.9493 phys vs 72.9755 control, moved only by the attribute-conditioned matching, not by association).

claims.statement: WHY IT FAILS: THE CANDIDATE SET, NOT THE THRESHOLD, IS THE CEILING -- AND IT IS ABOUT +0.2 GS-DetA. Over all 20 DEV sequences the physics window yields only 165 (named, unnamed) candidate pairs touching 78 distinct borrowing tracks. Labelling every one of them against GT: 7 borrowers (618 rows) would get the RIGHT number, 47 (7,112 rows) would get a wrong number from a numbered identity (DetA-neutral), 23 (4,639 rows) would be over-named, 1 unknown. So of the 41,707 rows that are the actual prize -- unnamed player tracks whose GT identity IS numbered -- the candidate generator reaches 7,730 rows (18.5%) and only 618 of those (8.0% of the reached mass, 1.5% of the prize) have a lender carrying the correct number. At W3's coverage-oracle exchange rate (44,866 rows = +16.36 GS-DetA) a PERFECT oracle over this candidate set is worth about +0.23 GS-DetA, a quarter of the registered +1.00 gate and 3% of the +8.15 own-roster bound. Name-borrowing cannot reach the jersey-coverage prize because the GTA connector has already consumed the temporally-disjoint same-player links: what is still unnamed is unnamed because the reader never read it ANYWHERE in the clip, not because a fragment lost a number it once had.
claims.unit: GS-DetA of a perfect oracle over the whole DEV-20 name-borrow candidate set
claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w6 --devcensus: every candidate pair labelled with the GT jersey of its borrower's owning GT identity, deduplicated per borrowing track; the DetA conversion uses the W3 jersey_coverage oracle rate.
caveats: The +0.23 conversion is a linear extrapolation of the W3 coverage oracle and is an UPPER bound: borrowed rows still have to be position-matched and role/team-correct to score at all.
32 of the 38 over-naming candidate pairs have a lender that is ITSELF over-named, so a borrow would be multiplying the solver's existing over-naming onto more rows.

16 of the 38 over-naming candidates have a borrower whose GT role is REFEREE while our chain labels it player -- the W4/W5 referee bucket leaking onto the jersey axis, which no jersey-side filter can see.

claims.statement: THE W2 TWIX RANKING DOES NOT TRANSFER TO THE (NAMED, UNNAMED) SUBPOPULATION, AND ITS LOGIT SCALE IS NOT SEED-STABLE. On the 165 DEV-20 borrow candidates the frozen seed-ensemble scorer ranks same-identity pairs at average precision 0.0916 against a base rate of 0.0545 (per seed: 0.0824 / 0.0884 / 0.1133) -- essentially chance, against the val pair-AP 0.6579 that passed W2's G1 gate on merge candidates. It is marginally worse than chance in the direction that matters: AP for OVER-NAMING candidates is 0.2482 against a 0.2303 base rate, i.e. the model mildly PREFERS the pairs that cost points. Separately, the absolute logit scale differs by roughly 0.7 between seeds, so the registered ensemble threshold -2.5 fires on 25 tracks under seed 0, 7 under seed 1, 2 under seed 2 and 6 for the ensemble: any single-seed deployment of a threshold fitted on the ensemble is a different arm.
claims.unit: average precision of the ensemble ranking for same-identity DEV-20 borrow pairs
claims.method: all three twixm_side checkpoints scored on the DEV-20 candidate pool with the appearance channel forced missing; AP against the GT-derived candidate outcome labels of the --devcensus pass.
caveats: The checkpoints are applied out of their training distribution twice over: trained on the pre-connector EIoU partition of GSR-TRAIN, applied to post-connector post-solver DEV tracks, and with the appearance channel switched off because the DEV embedding cache is broken on 11 of 20 sequences (kb v9-w1-006).
This does not retract W2's G1 result, which was measured on the merge-candidate population it was trained for.

claims.statement: PREMISE REFUTED: THE GS-DetA DETECTION-MISS BUCKET IS NOT A DETECTOR PROBLEM. On the v9-W7 same-stack DEV-20 control the detector's OWN image-space recall is 0.9711 at the shipped DETECT_CONF 0.20 (0.9754 at 0.10, 0.9854 at 0.01) while the submission's position recall is 0.9152 -- the chain after the detector loses 5.6 recall points and the detector itself is 2.9 short of perfect. Splitting all 19,933 control misses by where the row dies: 13,167 (66.1%) have a confident (>=0.20) detector box that never reaches the submission (8,815 killed between the detector and positions, 4,352 after positions), 4,828 (24.2%) have only a sub-threshold box ([0.10,0.20) 1,401; [0.01,0.10) 3,427) and just 1,938 (9.7%) have no box at any confidence. Apportioning the control's own nomiss oracle (+5.8204 GS-DetA) linearly across those classes prices a PERFECT DETECTOR at +0.57 GS-DetA, the confidence floor at +1.41 and the post-detector chain at +3.85. W3's pricing of a detector retrain at +2..4.4 GS-DetA assumed the misses were detector misses; they are not, and no detector training was run.
claims.unit: GS-DetA ceiling of a perfect detector on DEV-20 (oracle, GT attributes)
claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w7 --stage anatomy: per-frame attribute-blind pitch Hungarian match of the submission to GT (the W3 census matcher, reproduced row for row) plus a scale-free image-space match (foot-point distance <= 0.5 GT box heights) of each GT row against (a) the arm's own positions parquet and (b) a conf=0.01 dump of the same weights (tools.gsr_v9_w7_infer, a100server1 GPU 1). Oracle from tools.gsr_v9_deta.run_oracles 'nomiss' on the same control.
caveats: The apportionment of the oracle across row classes is linear and therefore approximate; the oracle also grants GT attributes, so every figure is an upper bound.

The conf=0.01 dump is a raw ultralytics predict on file paths (BGR) while the pipeline feeds an RGB numpy array; measured on 3 sequences the two differ by ~2% of rows and move the class split by <= 2%, so channel order is not what produces this result.
DEV-20 only; TEST-38, test-49 and challenge were not read.

claims.statement: SAME-MACHINE STACK DRIFT IS REAL, LARGE AND SIGNED THE OTHER WAY: kb v8-w4-004 CONFIRMED ON THE CLUSTER. Re-extracting DEV-20 on a100server1 GPU 1 on 2026-08-15 with the same code, the same weights (gsr_v3_ft_b/weights/last.pt, md5 2074d8741f97a6892a1322d0f808244c) and the same conda env as the 2026-08-07 on-record artifacts gives a DIFFERENT extraction (SNGS-021 11,893 rows / 53 tracks vs 11,757 / 48) and scores +1.0182 GS-DetA / +1.0817 GS-HOTA higher flags-OFF (39.3083/51.8083 -> 40.3265/52.8900) and +1.2489 / +0.9495 with the shipped vote+gk_side stack (43.3757/56.2601 -> 44.6246/57.2095). Per sequence the shift is a wash (13 helped / 7 hurt, Wilcoxon p=0.165), i.e. a pooled level shift rather than a per-sequence effect. The drift is LARGER than the +1.0 GS-DetA bar this session registered for its arms, so an arm paired against the on-record numbers instead of a same-day control would have booked a full pass out of nothing.
claims.unit: GS-DetA of a same-machine re-extraction over the 8-day-old on-record arm
claims.method: tools.gsr_v6det --stages extract,gate,percrop,boxes,embed,arm --variant _w7ctl over the DEV-20 sequence list, then tools.gsr_v9_w7.score_pair of the on-record submission against the fresh one under the official evaluator, flags OFF and ON.
caveats: Which package changed since 2026-08-07 (ultralytics 8.4.115 / supervision 0.30.0 / torch 2.5.1+cu121 today) was NOT isolated; the session only needed to know that cross-date pairing is invalid.
The sign is opposite to the laptop measurement in v8-w4-004 (-1.1395 GS-HOTA), so drift cannot be assumed to be a fixed penalty in either direction.

claims.statement: REGISTERED FAIL: RECOVERING EVERY DETECTION THE TRACKER DISCARDS COSTS -7.11 GS-DetA. supervision.ByteTrack.update_with_detections re-matches its Kalman track boxes to the input at IoU >= 0.5 and returns only the input rows that match, discarding 8.0% of the detector's confident boxes (250,705 -> 230,753 on DEV-20). Arm A1 (generator.tracking.KEEP_UNTRACKED, default OFF) writes those rows through on fresh ids. It does exactly what it was built to do -- positions recall 0.9240 -> 0.9707, misses 19,933 -> 7,830, 12,103 GT rows recovered -- and against its same-stack control scores -7.1054 GS-DetA / -8.4451 GS-HOTA flags-OFF and -8.4305 / -9.6670 on the full vote+gk_side stack, 0 of 20 sequences helped, Wilcoxon p=1.91e-06. Cause, from the row census: the 27,282 extra prediction rows bring +14,088 duplicate false positives and triple the tracklet count (938 -> 2,163 submission tracks; SNGS-096's solver goes from 34 tracklets / 25 groups to 111 / 141), which collapses jersey coverage (+20,475 coverage-loss rows) and destroys 12,704 rows that were fully correct before.
claims.unit: paired DEV-20 GS-DetA vs the same-stack control, flags OFF
claims.method: Full DEV-20 chain re-run (extract/gate/percrop/boxes/embed/arm) under variant _w7a1 on the same machine and env as its control, scored with eval.gsr_score.gs_hota (gs_hota_full) in both flag states by tools.gsr_v9_w7.score_pair; buckets from tools.gsr_v9_deta.census_sequence.
caveats: Only 33% of the written-through boxes overlap a kept box at image IoU >= 0.5, so an IoU dedup would remove about a third of the extra rows; it was NOT run, because the dominant damage is the +20,475 jersey-coverage collapse from fragmentation rather than the duplicates themselves.
The identity solver and the EIoU association were left at their frozen settings; the arm changes the input distribution they were tuned on.

claims.statement: A RECOVERED DETECTION IS WORTH ZERO: THE CLEANEST READ OF THE SESSION. Arm A2 (ByteTrack minimum_consecutive_frames 3 -> 1, nothing else) recovers 3,113 DEV-20 misses (submission recall 0.9152 -> 0.9285) and the number of fully-correct rows moves by MINUS TEN (136,206 -> 136,196). Every recovered row lands in a wrong-attribute bucket -- jersey coverage loss +2,806 -- while 4,676 rows are added to the GS-DetA denominator, so the arm scores -0.5221 GS-DetA / -0.5833 GS-HOTA flags-OFF and -0.5299 / -0.7069 on the vote+gk_side stack (10 helped / 10 hurt, p = 0.65). Against a control whose matched rows are 63.28% attribute-perfect, the attribute yield of newly recovered rows is 0.0%. Corollary for the campaign: GS-DetA oracles that insert GT-attributed rows on missed detections (W3 lever #4 at +6.99; this session's control at +5.82) are NOT reachable by finding the detections, because the rows the chain loses are exactly the rows the identity machinery cannot name.
claims.unit: change in fully-correct DEV-20 rows after recovering 3,113 missed detections
claims.method: As v9-w7-003 with variant _w7a2 and generator.tracking.MIN_HITS = 1; correct-row counts from tools.gsr_v9_deta.census_sequence on both submissions.
caveats: 'Zero yield' is a net figure: recovered rows could in principle be correct while an equal number of previously correct rows turned wrong. The per-row provenance of the -10 was not traced.
Only two points on the recall axis were tested (+3,113 and +12,103 rows); both are negative and the larger is much more negative, but the curve between and beyond them is unmeasured.

claims.statement: A ZERO-GPU TRACKER REPLAY PREDICTS THE EXTRACTION'S RECALL TO WITHIN 0.0004. Replaying supervision.ByteTrack on a cached low-confidence detector dump (tools.gsr_v9_w7.replay_tracker) predicted DEV-20 positions recall 0.9242 for the shipped (conf 0.20, min_hits 3) configuration and 0.9374 for min_hits 1; the actual full re-extractions measured 0.9240 and 0.9353. The replay costs seconds of CPU per sequence against ~1.0 GPU-h per extraction, so any (DETECT_CONF, min_hits, activation) point can be priced on recall before a GPU slot is booked. It also priced, correctly, why no confidence arm was registered: lowering DETECT_CONF from 0.20 to 0.10 is worth only +0.15 recall points once min_hits is fixed.
claims.unit: absolute error of the replay's predicted DEV-20 positions recall
claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w7 --stage replay over an 8-point grid, feeding the cached conf=0.01 dump into supervision.ByteTrack frame by frame exactly as generator.extract does (empty frames skip the update), then matching the tracker's output to GT in image space; compared against the positions parquets of the _w7ctl and _w7a2 extractions.
caveats: Validated on two configurations only, both on the same detector and the same split.

The replay models the tracker stage alone: it says nothing about calibration, association, the identity solver or GS-DetA -- and this session's whole result is that recall does not transfer to GS-DetA.

claims.statement: ATTACH-INHERIT WORKS AS A MECHANISM AND IS STILL NOT WORTH BUILDING. Giving a ByteTrack-discarded detection to an EXISTING track (so it inherits that track's role/team/jersey) fixes the exact failure that killed v9-W7 A2: the attached rows are 65.0% (gap 10) to 67.6% (gap 30) fully attribute-correct, against a control whose own matched rows are 63.28% attribute-correct and against 0.0% attribute yield for the fresh short tracks A2 created. But the mechanism's GT-PERFECT ceiling on DEV-20 -- attach every discarded box that really is a miss, onto the track that really carries its GT identity, with that host's own attributes -- is +0.7800 GS-DetA / +1.0309 GS-HOTA flags OFF (+0.8538 / +1.0899 with the vote+gk_side stack) over the v9-W7 same-stack control, on 6,249 inserted rows of which 4,225 are correct. The registered build bar was +0.75 GS-DetA of REACHABLE value, and reachable value is far below the oracle, so no arm was built and 0 GPU-hours were spent.
claims.unit: GS-DetA of the GT-perfect attach oracle on DEV-20, flags OFF
claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w8 --stage score: supervision.ByteTrack replayed over the cached conf=0.01 detector dump at the shipped settings to recover the discard set, each discard classified against GT and against the control submission, then counterfactual submissions written with the HOST track's own attributes and a pitch point from a homography fitted to the control's own rows in that frame, scored with eval.gsr_score.gs_hota (gs_hota_full) in both post-processing flag states.
caveats: The oracle is an upper bound in three separate ways: it uses GT to choose which discard to attach and to which host; it inserts rows directly into the final submission, so it assumes the attach survives the EIoU re-association and the identity solver unchanged; and it grants the host's majority attributes rather than what the solver would produce after the input distribution changes.

2,466 further attachable rows (28% of the gap-30 pool) could not be written at all because their timestep has fewer than 4 surviving rows to fit a homography. Those frames are the calibration-gate bucket, not an attach lever.
DEV-20 only; TEST-38, test-49 and challenge were not read.

claims.statement: BYTETRACK'S DISCARD IS MOSTLY CORRECT: ONLY 41.6% OF WHAT IT THROWS AWAY IS RECOVERABLE. Replaying the shipped tracker over the DEV-20 detector dump, 24,418 of 250,705 confident (>=0.20) person boxes are discarded. Classified against GT and against the control submission: 10,150 (41.6%) are a GT row the submission misses -- the recoverable pool; 4,470 (18.3%) duplicate a GT row the submission already covers; and 9,798 (40.1%) match no GT person at any distance, i.e. they are detector false positives the tracker is correctly suppressing. The W7 framing of the discard as boxes the tracker loses under camera pan is therefore only 41.6% true, and no geometry-only gate separates the three classes: the best GT-free rule found anywhere in a 3-gap x 5-radius x 4-separation sweep reaches 47.7% correct picks, on 791 rows.
claims.unit: fraction of ByteTrack-discarded confident boxes that are recoverable GS-DetA misses
claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w8 --stage oracle. Discards from a supervision.ByteTrack replay (kept-set GT recall 0.9242 vs the extraction's measured 0.9240, kb v9-w7-005); GT identity by scale-free image match (foot point within 0.5 GT box heights) run over the FULL confident box set so a discard cannot claim a GT row a kept box already explains; submission coverage by the W3 census matcher (attribute-blind pitch Hungarian, 5 m floor).
caveats: A discard tagged no_gt could in principle be a real person the GSR annotation omits; the SoccerNet GSR annotation is dense, so this is treated as a detector false positive.
The classification is per box, not per person: a GT row with two discarded boxes contributes one gt_miss and one gt_covered once the first is notionally attached.

claims.statement: REGISTERED STOP: THE BEST GT-FREE ATTACH RULE REALISES 20% OF ITS OWN ORACLE AND 21% OF THE BUILD BAR. Nine counterfactual attach arms were scored on DEV-20 against the v9-W7 same-stack control. The best GT-free rule -- pan-compensated nearest gap track, gap 30 timesteps, acceptance radius 1.0 box heights, minimum separation 0.3 box heights from any kept box, only on frames whose global image shift is >= 8 px -- scores +0.1553 GS-DetA / +0.2010 GS-HOTA flags OFF and +0.1760 / +0.2152 with the vote+gk_side stack, on 1,780 attached rows (872 correct, 286 right-identity-wrong-attributes, 291 wrong identity, 90 onto an already-covered GT row, 241 onto no GT row). Its thresholds were chosen by looking at DEV itself, so even this number is optimistic, and it is a CPU simulation that inserts rows straight into the submission rather than letting the chain re-derive them. The pre-registered bar was +0.75 GS-DetA. Note for future registrations: this arm PASSES the a-priori row-audit bar (wrong identity 16.3% of attached rows, bar < 25%) while failing the score bar by 4.8x -- the row audit is not a proxy for value.
claims.unit: GS-DetA of the best GT-free attach rule on DEV-20, flags OFF, DEV-tuned
claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w8 --stage score over nine (mode, gap, radius, separation, pan) points, each written as a full counterfactual submission and scored with eval.gsr_score.gs_hota (gs_hota_full) against the same control in both flag states. The one-attach-per-host-per-timestep constraint is forced by the evaluator, which refuses a submission emitting one track id twice in a frame.
caveats: Thresholds were swept on DEV-20, which the campaign's own discipline forbids for a shipping arm; they are reported here only to bound the mechanism from above.

The candidate rule is geometry-only (position, size, pan compensation, separation). Kit colour from the raw crop was not tried: at 41.6% recoverable mass and a 47.7% purity ceiling, appearance would have to be near-perfect to move the arm past +0.75.
Nothing was re-extracted, so downstream re-derivation of an attached row by the EIoU association and the identity solver is assumed benign rather than measured.

claims.statement: CAMERA PAN IS THE RIGHT COVARIATE, AND IT SPLITS THE DISCARD BUCKET CLEANLY. Bucketing DEV-20 discards by the frame's global image shift (median displacement of tracks shared with the previous frame): frames panning >= 8 px/frame hold 42.8% of all discards (10,447) and 57.6% of those are recoverable misses, against 36.0% at < 1 px/frame; the GT-free attach rule is 41.6% correct there versus 7.1-15.6% in the low-pan bands. Restricting the rule to pan >= 8 is the single most valuable gate found (+0.1553 vs +0.1249 GS-DetA for the same rule unrestricted, on 43% fewer rows). The premise that the Kalman prediction drifts off the player under pan is therefore confirmed; it is simply not worth enough, because even in the best pan band a majority of discards are duplicates or phantoms.
claims.unit: fraction of discards that are recoverable misses on frames panning >= 8 px/frame
claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w8 --stage oracle, pan buckets (0-1, 1-3, 3-8, >=8) px/frame from the median frame-to-frame displacement of control submission tracks present in both frames; the pan-gated arm scored by --stage score.
caveats: The pan estimate is the median track displacement, so it conflates camera pan with a coordinated team shift; on a broadcast tactical camera the two are hard to separate and the estimate was not validated against the GT camera parameters, which the sequences do carry.
The bucket edges were not pre-registered.

claims.statement: THE V9 FREEZE IS DRIFT-PROOF BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE DRIFT WAS RE-MEASURED TO PROVE IT. The v9 bundle differs from the frozen v6 bundle by nothing but two post-processing flags (VOTE_TRACK_ATTRS = role,team,jersey and GK_SIDE_REPAIR = team), both pure functions of an already-written submission, so a flags-ON arm and its flags-OFF control are the same extraction bit for bit and the re-extraction drift of kb v9-w7-002 cannot enter the comparison. Measured on two DEV-20 lineages nine days apart (v6 laptop 2026-08-06, W7 server 2026-08-15): the BASELINES differ by 1.0817 GS-HOTA / 1.0182 GS-DetA (the drift) while the off->full flag delta differs by only 0.1323 GS-HOTA (4.4518 vs 4.3195) and 0.2307 GS-DetA (4.0674 vs 4.2981). The session therefore ran ZERO GPU against a ~12 GPU-h budget: re-extracting test-49 would have replaced a MEASURED 53.0846 lineage with a +/-1 point coin flip, and choosing between them afterwards would be selection on test.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA spread of the off->full flag delta across two DEV-20 lineages whose baselines are 1.0817 apart
claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w9.score_states over states off/vote/full on each lineage's own submission directory, official scorer EVAL_CONFIGS['gs_hota_full'], laptop sn-trackeval 0.4.0 @ 9c25232. Harness fidelity first: flags-off reproduces both lineages' on-record GS-HOTA/GS-DetA to 4 dp (51.8083/39.3083 and 52.8900/40.3265), vote reproduces W3's 54.7970/41.1082 and full reproduces W5's 56.2601/43.3757 to 4 dp.
caveats: Two lineages, one split. The delta's lineage stability is not measured on TEST-38 or test-49, where only one lineage exists.
This is an argument about post-processing flags only. Any future arm that changes the extraction still needs a same-window control.

Declared in results/gsr_v9_frozen.json at 2026-08-15T16:12:49Z, before any TEST-38 score of either flag state: paired mean GS-HOTA >= +2.0, >= 24/38 helped, Wilcoxon p < 0.01, paired mean GS-DetA >= +1.5. claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w9 on outputs/gsr_srv/deleak_v6t38_v6det_clip_e0.3r1w0.5a0.3 (digest fdb79d769487..., extracted 2026-08-06T12:52Z, a100server1 GPU 1), states off/vote/full, per-sequence Wilcoxon over n = 38.

The DEV-20 lineage used to size the arm is a laptop stack (supervision 0.28.x) while TEST-38 is the 2026-08-06 server stack, so the DEV->TEST transfer estimate crosses stacks. The TEST-38 -> test-49 step does not.

Same 467,425-row extraction as the v6 package, flags ON: GS-HOTA 55.4062 / GS-DetA 41.2793 / GS-AssA 74.3774 / GS-LocA 94.1272 / IDF1 58.5357 (flags-OFF reproduces the on-record 53.0846 / 39.3231 exactly). claims.method: tools.gsr_v9_w9 on outputs/gsr_srvtest/deleak_v6test_v6det_clip_e0.3r1w0.5a0.3 (digest 2b989ee76c2a..., the exact directory the v6 package was built from), states off/vote/full, run once after the TEST-38 gate passed. Row-change counts are the 'changed' counters returned by vote_track_attributes and gk_side_repair.
caveats: Local score, not a board score. The board has matched our local scorer once on record (39.0215 local vs 39.02 returned, 2026-08-02) and the v6 53.08 package was never uploaded, so the board prediction rests on a single confirmed agreement.
The decay is explained by one covariate (base attribute consistency) measured on three splits; no competing explanation was tested.

claims.statement: SUBMISSION #6 IS PACKAGED AND AUDITED: gsr_testphase_gtfree_v9_c5fcae6e.zip, sha256 a9ef0f002b078d2b5f2aa25dd1a731cc911a24382e535a1b7abdf844f46ce0c9, 35,466,405 bytes, 49 sequences, 467,425 predictions.
