The audit proves no label reached the team attribute; it is not a proof about the jersey or role attributes, which come from our own reader and role head.

claims.statement: REGISTERED BARS FAIL, and by one read: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (Apache-2.0, greedy, 12 stratified closest views per tracklet as 12 separate images) scores 8 correct of 9 emitted = 0.889 precision on Sid's 13 confident tier-A human numbers (bar 0.90, Wilson 95% CI [0.565, 0.980] -- the pool cannot resolve the bar) and 10 false positives on 274 human-confirmed-none tracklets = 3.65% (bar <= 5%, PASS). The other two registered regimes are worse on precision: contact sheet 6/7 = 0.857 at 1.46% FP, single 4x-upscaled best crop 4/5 = 0.800 at 2.92% FP. It comfortably beats the v7 Qwen2-VL-2B trial's 0.265 (ident-020), so that failure was a model-size failure -- but the bar is still not cleared.
claims.unit: precision on the 13 human-numbered tier-A tracklets
claims.method: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct bf16, transformers 5.14.1, A100-40GB GPU 1, greedy decode, one JSON line out; GT = Sid's 499-tracklet W3 annotation (GSR-train only, no training anywhere); registration written to results/GSR_V10_W1.md section 1 before any weight was downloaded.
caveats: n=9 emissions: the pool cannot distinguish 0.89 from 0.90.
7 of the 13 human numbers are '1' and 6 of those are goalkeepers; excluding all read==1 rows gives 4/5 for both the VLM and the incumbent chain.
A post-hoc mean-logprob threshold would clear both bars (>= -0.1: 8/8 = 1.000 precision, FP 3.65%), but it was chosen after seeing the labels and is not a PASS.

claims.statement: The VLM does NOT beat the shipped PARSeq + legibility chain on identical evidence, at either level. Tier A, same 12 views: the chain scores the identical 8 of 9 (0.889) with 14 of 274 false positives (5.11%) against the VLM's 10 (3.65%). Tier B (210 tracklets whose number SoccerNet annotates): the chain names 194 of 210 correctly -- 0.9848 precision at 0.9238 recall -- against the best VLM regime's 182 (0.9579 / 0.8667); paired, chain-only correct 14 vs VLM-only 2, union 196. Per crop over the same 2,520 cells the gap is decisive: chain-only correct 324 vs VLM-only 54, exact McNemar p = 4.8e-48.
claims.unit: tracklet recall of the shipped chain on tier B
claims.method: Incumbent parseq_v6_arm4t.ckpt (md5 39c0c15defafda072ca0cefd0a4b8e18, verified equal to the shipped reader), shipped legibility gate at 0.7 and pose torso RoI, run over the same 5,988 cells the VLM saw; tracklet read = confidence-weighted majority of the gated per-crop reads.
caveats: Tier-B tracklets are GT identities with GT boxes; a tracker's tracklets fragment and switch, so 0.9238 is an upper bound for the deployed pipeline.
Tier-B tracklets were selected by legibility-gate uncertainty (v8-w3-009), not at random.

claims.statement: CONFIRMED at machine scale by two independent readers that never saw the labels: the SoccerNet-GSR train unnamed-tracklet pool is genuinely unnumbered. On the 274 tracklets Sid marked 'none' the VLM emits a number on 10 (3.65%) and the shipped chain on 14 (5.11%); both emit on only 5 and AGREE on the number on 2 -- one a goalkeeper '1' (the prior both readers carry) and one, SNGS-100 track 18 read as 33 by three independent reads, strong evidence of a single human miss. Per crop the chain's gate passes and PARSeq emits on 68 of 3,468 tier-A cells (2.0%) against 990 of 2,520 (39.3%) tier-B cells from the same builder. v8-w3-007's 94.8% genuine-absence figure therefore needs a correction of at most ~0.4 pp, and v9-W3's judgement that the jersey over-naming bucket (+1.16 DetA oracle) is unreachable stands.
claims.unit: fraction of the 274 human-'none' tracklets with strong independent evidence of a missed number
claims.method: Re-read of the identical 12 stratified closest views per tracklet by Qwen3-VL-8B and by the shipped chain; agreement = both readers emit and emit the same integer.
caveats: Absence is established only for the 12 views shown, exactly as in v8-w3-007.
The goalkeeper-'1' agreement (A0026) is weak evidence: both readers carry a GK-1 prior.

claims.statement: The jersey-coverage loss is upstream of the reader, not in it. Given twelve stratified closest views (>= 89 px) of one clean GT identity, the shipped reader names 92.4% of numbered tracklets correctly at 0.985 precision -- while on the 10 cached DEV bundles 309 of 478 tracklets carry no confident read at all (GSR_V9_W3.md section 3.1). The binding constraint on the +16.36-DetA jersey-coverage oracle is therefore WHICH CROPS REACH THE READER (tracker fragmentation, box quality, view selection, and a per-crop gate whose admissions are 27% unreadable per v8-w3-010), not the reader's ability to read.
claims.unit: tracklet naming accuracy on GT identities given 12 stratified views
claims.method: Tier-B positive control, 210 GSR-train tracklets, shipped chain unchanged.
caveats: The comparison crosses splits (train GT tracklets vs DEV predicted tracklets) and crosses box provenance (GT boxes vs our detector's); it motivates a DEV-20 measurement, it does not substitute for one.

claims.statement: Reader agreement is a perfect-precision naming gate on this pool: requiring the shipped chain and Qwen3-VL-8B to emit the SAME number names 180 of 210 tier-B tracklets and gets 180 of 180 right (precision 1.0000 at 0.857 recall) against 0.9848 / 0.9238 for the chain alone; on tier A it is 6 of 6 correct with 2 false positives in 274 (0.73%). The two readers' errors are near-disjoint -- on the 13 human numbers each one's only error is the other's success.
claims.unit: precision at 0.857 recall (agreement gate, tier B)
claims.method: AND-ensemble of the two independent tracklet reads over the same 12 views.
caveats: Measured on GSR-train GT tracklets, never on DEV-20; no GS-DetA number exists for this rule.
The second reader costs 0.79 s per tracklet at the multi12 regime.

claims.statement: Two mechanism results that close the obvious follow-ups. (a) Sid's per-cell visibility labels are a LOWER bound on machine readability, not a ceiling: on the 1,749 cells he judged illegible the shipped chain returns the correct number on 250 (14.3%, precision 0.912) and the VLM on 82 (4.7%) -- both beat single-view human reading, the chain by 3x. (b) The VLM's deficit is NOT a localization artifact: handed the identical pose torso RoIs PARSeq reads, it gets WORSE (tier-B tracklet recall 0.748 from 0.867; per-crop recall 0.201 from 0.271). Whole-body context is load-bearing for a general VLM, and a jersey-fine-tuned STR specialist reads digits better than an 8B VLM at any crop geometry.
claims.unit: fraction of human-illegible cells the shipped chain reads correctly
claims.method: Per-crop reads of both readers over the 2,520 tier-B cells carrying Sid's visibility labels; the torso arm re-runs the VLM on the 5,319 pose torso RoIs the chain uses.
caveats: 'Correct' means matching the tracklet's GT number, which is identity-carried (v8-w3-001), so a correct read on a hidden cell cannot be told from a lucky one without per-cell number GT -- but at 0.912 precision over 274 emissions luck is not the explanation.

claims.statement: CALIBRATION AUDIT AGAINST THE LEADER'S SIX-DEFECT CHECKLIST: four of six are ABSENT from our PnLCalib integration and one more is present only by design. BGR/RGB is correct (generator/calibrate.py::_detect does cv2.cvtColor(BGR2RGB) and every caller supplies BGR); preprocessing is line-for-line PnLCalib's own inference.py (to_tensor [0,1], no ImageNet normalisation, T.Resize((540,960)), thresholds 0.3434/0.7867, denormalize+normalize paired); radial distortion is N-A because PnLCalib fixes CALIB_FIX_K1..K6 and emits radial_distortion=[0]*6, so there is no coefficient to invert or mis-apply; frame skipping is absent (calib_period=1 on every GSR path). Only the heatmap DECODE is defective -- and the measured residual field says the defect is not the one the checklist names.
claims.unit: of six checklist defects absent (1 by design, 1 genuinely present)
claims.method: Source audit of generator/calibrate.py, generator/extract.py, generator/postprocess.py and the ~/PnLCalib dependency (utils_heatmap.py, utils_calib.py, inference.py) with file:line evidence per item; the distortion item additionally measured as the radial component of the image-space GT residual field over 211,496 DEV-20 GT rows (median radial -0.58 px, non-monotonic across six radius bins, unchanged by the decode fix).
caveats: Nothing from Baishev's repositories was fetched, read or run; the six-item checklist was the only permitted transfer.

Item 6a (960x540 rather than native 1080p) is present but deliberate -- that is PnLCalib's training resolution and feeding native frames is out of distribution. Not attempted; its recoverable half is the decode quantisation, measured separately.

claims.statement: THE SUBPIXEL FIX IS THE WRONG FIX AND MAKES CALIBRATION WORSE. Replacing PnLCalib's integer arg-max heatmap decode with an exact sub-cell estimate (log-parabola through the peak and its two neighbours per axis; exact for a Gaussian to 1e-6) moves the GT-anchored homography error the WRONG WAY on DEV-20: pooled median 0.4773 -> 0.5085 m (+6.5%), mean 1.374 -> 1.915, GT-free keypoint reprojection 3.816 -> 3.855 px, 23,392 rows worse against 18,773 better over 42,165 paired rows. Un-rounding PnLCalib's line-intersection keypoints (complete_keypoints' round(x, 0), fixed by handing it an 8x canvas) is worth exactly nothing: median 0.4773 -> 0.4771 m, 624 of 42,165 rows changed at all.
claims.unit: m, pooled median GT-anchored homography error under sub-cell decoding (ctrl 0.4773)
claims.method: DEV-20, every 5th frame, six decode arms built from ONE forward pass per frame (same weights, same heatmaps, cv2.setRNGSeed(20260815) per frame) so the decode is the only variable. Error instrument: each annotation's own bbox_image bottom-middle pushed through that frame's gate-selected homography against its own bbox_pitch -- no detection, no matcher, no box-convention term.
caveats: The estimator is not the weak link: it recovers a synthetic off-cell Gaussian to under 0.005 cells (tests/test_calibrate.py), where a +-2 centroid leaves 0.29 cells of bias.

The mechanism is in PnLCalib's TRAINING code: utils_heatmap.resize_keypoints builds every target as int(x * 0.5), so the Gaussian's true centre IS an integer cell and sub-cell interpolation can only add noise.

claims.statement: THE REAL DECODE DEFECT IS A HALF-CELL BIAS, AND ONE LINE REMOVES IT. PnLCalib's label generator floors keypoints into heatmap cells (utils_heatmap.resize_keypoints: x_resized = int(x * 0.5)), so the decoder's cell*2 returns the cell's LOW EDGE and every keypoint and line endpoint is biased by U[0, 2) px of the 960-wide input toward the image origin -- 2 px of a 1080p frame, in both axes, on every frame. Measured in image space over 211,496 DEV-20 GT rows the stock chain's median residual is dx +1.497, dy +2.336 px, as predicted; adding half a cell (generator.calibrate.shift_half_cell) collapses it to dx -0.533, dy +0.335 px. GT-anchored homography error falls 0.4778 -> 0.4272 m median (-10.6%), p90 1.4611 -> 1.3965, mean 1.594 -> 1.316 (-17.4%), improving on 17 of 20 sequences.
claims.unit: m, pooled median GT-anchored homography error, DEV-20 every frame (ctrl 0.4778)
claims.method: Full-stride DEV-20 (15,000 frames), two decode arms from one forward pass per frame with a fixed RANSAC seed. Accuracy: the annotation's own image foot point through the gate-selected homography vs its own bbox_pitch. Mechanism: the same GT pitch point pushed BACK through H^-1 into the image, residual medians and their radial component binned by image radius. The offset is scale/2 = 1.0 px by derivation from the label code -- no sweep, no alternative value tried.
caveats: Derived AFTER the sub-pixel arm failed, from PnLCalib's training code rather than from a score, and registered in results/gsr_v10_w2_registered.json before any s4 coordinate was decoded, under the same 3% bar as every other arm.
s4's x residual slightly overshoots (-0.533 px), so the true x bias is nearer 1.5 px than 2.0 -- line-intersection keypoints partly cancel it.
DEV-20 only. TEST-38, test-49 and the challenge split are untouched.

claims.statement: THE HALF-CELL FIX FAILS ITS PRE-REGISTERED SHIP BAR WHILE MOVING EVERY COLUMN THE RIGHT WAY. End to end on DEV-20 with detections, ByteTrack ids, CLIP embeddings, per-crop OCR, EIoU association, the GTA connector and the MILP solver held identical and only the pitch coordinate varying, the flags-ON stack scores GS-DetA 42.4914 -> 42.8846 (+0.3932) against a pre-declared >= +1.00 bar: FAIL. Every supporting condition passes -- GS-HOTA 55.0660 -> 55.5557 (+0.4896), GS-AssA +0.6079, IDF1 +0.1537, paired per-sequence GS-HOTA +0.4240 with 17 helped / 3 hurt, Wilcoxon p = 0.00486 -- and GS-LocA RISES by +0.5831 (93.1805 -> 93.7636), the registered signature of a real geometry fix. Flags OFF the same picture: DetA +0.3434, HOTA +0.4358, LocA +0.5766, 16/4, p = 0.0073.
claims.unit: GS-DetA gain on DEV-20, flags ON (bar: +1.00)
claims.method: tools.gsr_eiou.run_point at the frozen v6 point (e=0.3, rounds=1, w_app=0.5, app_max=0.30, embedder clip_v6det, tau 0.450, reader _v6_v6det) per arm, then tools.gsr_v9_w7.score_pair flags ON (vote role/team/jersey + gk_side team) and OFF. The control is re-derived in the SAME window from the same forward pass, the same weights and the same RANSAC seed as the arm (kb v9-w7-004's drift rule).
caveats: The bar was set for a fix expected to reach into the +3.74 DetA localization oracle of the v9-W3 census; it delivered 10.5% of that oracle. The bar stands as registered -- nothing was re-run and no threshold was moved.
Worst sequence SNGS-024 -1.684 GS-HOTA, best SNGS-036 +1.772.

The re-derived control (flags-ON DetA 42.4914) is not the on-record shipped DEV-20 number: it is a fresh calibration of every frame, which GSR_CALIBGATE.md prices at a median 0.26 m coordinate difference. Only the paired within-window delta is claimed.

claims.statement: THE LEADER'S +12.6 CALIBRATION PATTERN DOES NOT APPLY TO US, AND THE v8-W2 0.475 m WAS ALL CALIBRATION. The whole overhaul -- six defects audited, both live ones fixed and measured -- is worth +0.49 GS-HOTA on DEV-20, 3.9% of the 12.6 the leader's private jump represents. Two supporting facts. (a) The v8-W2 detection-anchored 0.475 m was assumed to be an upper bound containing detection-box and matcher error; the homography-only instrument built here reads 0.4778 m on the same chain, so essentially ALL of it is calibration and there is no detection-side slack hiding in that number. (b) A latent crash was found and fixed on the way: PnLCalib's cv2.calibrateCamera raises on a degenerate correspondence set that the integer decode can produce (6 occurrences on SNGS-096 alone) and generator.calibrate.candidates had no guard, so one bad keypoint subset killed an entire extraction instead of 1 of its 18 hypotheses.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA the entire calibration overhaul is worth on DEV-20 (leader's jump: +12.6)
claims.method: Six-defect audit (v10-w2-001) plus two decode arms measured GT-anchored and end to end (v10-w2-002 to -004). The crash was surfaced by fixing the RANSAC seed, which makes the degenerate inlier set reproducible; the guard counts (PnLCalibCalibrator.n_solver_errors) instead of raising.
caveats: This does not say the leader's +12.6 is not calibration for HIM -- his public baseline is a different pipeline. It says OUR calibration had one recoverable defect worth half a HOTA point, consistent with v8-w2-002 (we were already more accurate than the previous leader's SFR module).
The crash guard changes shipped behaviour: a raising subset is skipped and counted instead of propagating. Frames that never raised are byte-identical.

The 0.475 vs 0.4778 comparison is indicative, not exact: v8-W2 measured 10 probe sequences on the on-record positions_gate_v6det coordinates, this session measured DEV-20 on a fresh re-calibration of every frame. The two instruments agree to 0.003 m across those differences, which is why the detection-side slack is called negligible.

claims.statement: A TEMPORALLY-CONSISTENT TRIPOD CAMERA TRACKER IS 2.5x LESS ACCURATE THAN OUR PER-FRAME SOLVER ON GSR. BroadTrack (WACV 2025, EVS proprietary, run privately as an instrument) was built from upstream and run on the 10-sequence v8-W2 probe in its intended two-pass configuration (prior-position pass, then a per-sequence tripod file at the tight radius 0.211 m). GT-anchored homography error on 106,748 paired annotation rows: BroadTrack median 1.0001 m / p90 3.2533 / 94.5% within 5 m, against our shipped chain's s4 arm at 0.4024 m / 1.2867 / 99.6% and ctrl at 0.4682 m on the identical rows. Excluding the one clip where the tracker diverges (SNGS-078), the mean of per-sequence medians is still 0.954 m vs our 0.431 m -- the gap is systematic, not a failure-mode artifact. Registered escalation bar was <= 0.85x our s4 median (0.342 m): FAIL by 2.9x.
claims.unit: GT-anchored median position error, metres (our s4 = 0.4024 m on the same rows)
claims.method: tools.gsr_v10_w3_camtrack --accuracy. Each GT annotation's own bbox_image bottom-middle pushed through that frame's camera against that annotation's own bbox_pitch; no detection, no matcher and no box convention enters. Our side is the v10-W2 candidate cache (outputs/gsr/v10_w2_full) replayed through the shipped select_calibration gate -- the ctrl/s4 per-sequence medians reproduce results/gsr_benchmark/gsr_v10_w2_full.json. The external camera-parameter reading convention was resolved once on SNGS-024 by a 16 x 3 discrete search (rotation composition x distortion mode) and cross-checked with cv2.solvePnP on GT: the chosen reading agrees with the PnP-fitted rotation to ~2 degrees per frame with per-frame sign changes, so the residual is the tracker's error, not a misreading.
caveats: BroadTrack's own tripod estimator (scripts/compute_tripod.py) succeeds on only 1 of the 10 clips; the other 9 tripods are the median of the pass-1 per-frame positions over the above-median-score frames. On SNGS-057, where their estimator succeeds, its centre and ours agree to 2.5 m and the run behaves the same, so the substitute is not the cause of the gap.

One arm gave the tracker our own detections as human bboxes to mask (its --b option, which our calibrator has no equivalent of): on 3 sequences it helped one (SNGS-024 1.310 -> 0.810 m) and hurt one (SNGS-042 1.250 -> 1.469 m). It does not close the gap.

INSTRUMENT ONLY: EVS proprietary licence, noncommercial internal research, no distribution of derivatives. Nothing was vendored into the repo; the binary and its weights live in ~/work/v10w3 on a100server1.

claims.statement: THE TRIPOD TRACKER IS 26x TEMPORALLY SMOOTHER THAN OUR CHAIN -- THE ONE REGISTERED BAR IT PASSES. On the frames both systems answer, the pitch position of a fixed 5x5 image grid moves with a frame-to-frame second difference (acceleration: the pure jitter signal, zero for any smooth pan) of 0.0146 m median / 0.2207 p90 for BroadTrack against 0.3795 m / 2.1871 for our s4 arm and 0.3811 m for ctrl. First differences: 0.129 m vs 0.283 m. Registered bar was <= 0.5x ours: PASS by 26x, which is what licensed stage 2.
claims.unit: ratio of our jitter to theirs (0.3795 m vs 0.0146 m median grid acceleration)
claims.method: tools.gsr_v10_w3_camtrack --jitter, evaluated only inside maximal runs of >= 3 consecutive frames that BOTH systems calibrate, so the number is smoothness and not coverage.
caveats: Smoothness is measured, not its value: stage 2 shows it buys nothing downstream when it costs accuracy (v10-w3-004).
Our jitter is the shipped gate's chosen hypothesis per frame; the gate re-selects among 18 PnLCalib hypotheses independently each frame, which is the mechanism.

claims.statement: OUR DEAD-FRAME PROBLEM IS NOW 2.3% OF FRAMES, AND AN EXTERNAL CAMERA ANSWERS ALL OF IT BUT AT TWICE OUR ERROR. Across the 10-sequence probe our gate plus fill_calibration_gaps(10) leaves 176 of 7,500 frames without a camera (2.35%); BroadTrack emits a usable camera on 176 of 176 (100%). Its error on exactly those frames is 0.858 m median / 1.880 p90 against our chain's 0.402 m on its own live frames, so the registered accuracy-conditioned coverage bar (<= 1.25x ours, i.e. 0.503 m) FAILS. The v8-W2 framing of coverage as the leader's real edge is largely obsolete on our side: the dead pool has shrunk to 176 frames and the whole prize for filling it is +0.35 GS-HOTA.
claims.unit: dead frames after fill across 7,500 probe frames (2.35%); external recovers 100%
claims.method: tools.gsr_v10_w3_camtrack --coverage. Dead = frames with no finite pitch coordinate for any player/GK row in the shipped positions_gate_v6det table after fill_calibration_gaps(max_gap=10).
caveats: Frame-level, not row-level: 2,288 GT-matched annotation rows sit on those 176 frames.
Measured on the v6det lineage over the DEV-20 probe subset, not the test split.

claims.statement: SWAPPING THE TRIPOD TRACKER INTO THE CHAIN COSTS 7.39 GS-HOTA -- SMOOTHNESS BUYS NOTHING WHEN IT COSTS ACCURACY. End to end on the probe with detections, ByteTrack ids, CLIP embeddings, per-crop OCR, EIoU association and the solver held identical and only the pitch coordinate varying: control 42.9370, t1 (external camera everywhere) 35.5461 (-7.39, hurt 10 of 10, Wilcoxon p = 0.00195, worst -23.26), t2 (external + fill) 35.3593. GS-LocA falls 93.6348 -> 87.7888 and GS-AssA falls 58.8777 -> 49.5836: a 26x smoother camera made association WORSE, because position accuracy dominates. Only t3 (ours where finite, external on our NaN rows) gains: 43.2901, +0.35, helped 6 hurt 3, p = 0.086 -- indistinguishable from the +0.33 the leader's per-frame calibrator bought in the same t3 slot in v8-W2. The camera-model-class hypothesis is closed: the leader's remaining edge is not a better camera model.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA delta vs same-lineage control, 10-sequence probe (t1 arm)
claims.method: tools.gsr_w2_calibswap --positions/--arms at suffix v10w3t, tag v10_w3, origin 0,0 on the exported per-frame homographies (homography-fit residual to the exact camera map 0.0000 m median: the pass-2 distortion coefficients are ~5e-4). The control re-derives v8-W2's control to 42.9370 vs 42.9371.
caveats: This is the frozen v6/v8-W2 lineage chain (the same one v8-W2's t-arms rode), not the v9 flags-ON stack; only the paired within-window delta is claimed.
A ceiling measurement, not a shippable component: the instrument's licence forbids shipping anything built from its code.

claims.statement: THE TRACKER LOSES LOCK ON 2 OF 10 CLIPS WITH NO SHOT CUT TO BLAME -- THE STRUCTURAL COST OF TEMPORAL STATE. SNGS-078 flags 328 of 749 frames as reinit (44%) with its horizontal FOV estimate running from 5.6 to 226.3 degrees; SNGS-027 collapses from frame 483 onward (222 reinits, FOV to 333.2 degrees). A frame-difference cut detector finds ZERO shot cuts in either clip (or in the well-behaved SNGS-051 control), so these are divergences on continuous single-shot footage, not cut-induced. The other 8 clips take 1-3 reinits. Our per-frame solver cannot fail this way by construction: on SNGS-078 it calibrates 719 of 750 frames at 0.398 m while the tracker sits at 2.393 m.
claims.unit: clips of 10 where the temporal tracker diverges (44% and 30% of frames reinit)
claims.method: tools.gsr_v10_w3_camtrack --failures on the tracker's own per-frame score/reinit trace, cross-tabbed against a downscaled-grayscale frame-difference cut detector (threshold = median + 8 IQR).
caveats: Reinit count does not predict accuracy monotonically: SNGS-027 takes 222 reinits yet scores 0.438 m, while SNGS-024 takes 1 and scores 1.310 m.
The tripod files for 9 of 10 clips are our median substitute (v10-w3-001); SNGS-057, the clip carrying the tracker's OWN tripod estimate, behaves like the substitute clips.

claims.statement: WE CAN BUY THE SMOOTHNESS OURSELVES FOR FREE -- AND IT IMPROVES ACCURACY TOO (EXPLORATORY, NOT REGISTERED). Temporally averaging OUR OWN per-frame homographies (four fixed image points pushed to the pitch, centred moving average inside runs of consecutive calibrated frames, homography re-fitted) cuts jitter 9.5x and cuts error at the same time: window 9 gives GT-anchored median 0.3635 m vs 0.4028 m raw (-9.8%, better on 10 of 10 sequences) with grid acceleration 0.0402 m vs 0.3800 m; window 5 gives 0.3718 m and 0.0704 m. End to end through the same chain the smoothed arm scores GS-HOTA 43.3621 vs control 42.9370 (+0.4251), GS-LocA 93.6348 -> 94.4502 (+0.82), GS-AssA +0.75, GS-DetA +0.22, helped 7 hurt 3, Wilcoxon p = 0.131 on n = 10. This lever needs no external code and no licence.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA gain vs same-lineage control, 10-sequence probe, window 9 (exploratory)
claims.method: tools.gsr_v10_w3_camtrack --smooth 1,5,9 for the geometry, then tools.gsr_w2_calibswap --positions/--arms at suffix v10w3s, tag v10_w3s, arms control,t2 (smoothed + fill_calibration_gaps(10)).
caveats: EXPLORATORY AND POST-HOC: conceived after the registered BroadTrack measurements, two windows were tried, and p = 0.131 on 10 sequences is not significant. It needs its own pre-registration and a DEV-20 read before any of it counts.
The moving average is unbiased only for a linear pan; a fast zoom or an accelerating pan is lagged, a candidate explanation for the 3 sequences it hurt.
Nothing here derives from BroadTrack's code -- only from the measurement that our own camera jitters 26x more than a temporally-consistent one.

claims.statement: THE GEOMETRY AXIS HOLDS +6.82 GS-HOTA, AND THE '5 m TOLERANCE' PREMISE IS WRONG. GS-HOTA's position match is not a 5 m gate: TrackEval's SoccerNetGS class scores every pair with a GAUSSIAN, sim = exp(-d^2 / (2 * 2.0427^2)), where 5 m is merely the distance at which the similarity has decayed to 0.05 (0.43 m -> 0.978, 1 m -> 0.886, 2 m -> 0.62). Every centimetre of pitch error is charged. On DEV-20, flags ON, holding detections / track ids / association / attributes byte-identical and rewriting only bbox_pitch: re-projecting every submission row through a GT-fitted per-frame homography (perfect camera, our own detections) moves 55.0660 -> 61.3198 (+6.2537 GS-HOTA, DetA +4.745, AssA +8.239, LocA 93.18 -> 98.35); adding the 2,893 rows the calibration chain loses takes it to 61.8867 (+6.8207). The registered a-priori kill threshold for the whole axis was '< +1.00 -> Rungs 2-3 are not worth 3-5 weeks': exceeded 6.8x.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA headroom vs same-lineage control, DEV-20 flags ON (perfect camera + perfect completeness oracle)
claims.method: tools.gsr_v10_w4 --curve, arms O_acc / O_comp / O_all on the v10-W2 ctrl lineage (deleak_v10w2_ctrl predictions, positions_v10w2ctrl_v6det, v10_w2_full/ctrl candidate cache); flags applied after the rewrite via tools.gsr_v9_w7 FLAGS_ON; scored with eval.gsr_score.gs_hota EVAL_CONFIGS['gs_hota_full'].
caveats: UPPER BOUND, twice over: the oracle homography is FITTED per frame to that frame's own GT annotations, so it absorbs lens distortion and any GT foot-point convention locally -- no physical camera model is guaranteed to reach it; and the GT fit's own residual (0.09 m median) is the instrument's floor.

LOWER BOUND in one respect: the rewrite is downstream of association, so the oracle gets no credit for better geometry feeding EIoU / the GTA connector / the solver. The end-to-end value of perfect geometry is therefore >= this number.
Null arm verified: re-projecting every row through its OWN frame's solved homography reproduces the control to 4 dp (55.0660) and to 1e-14 m per row.
305 of the 3,198 lost rows are skipped by the completeness oracle (no GT camera on that frame, or a duplicate (track, timestep) the evaluator rejects), so O_comp is itself conservative.

claims.statement: THE CALIBRATION-ERROR -> GS-HOTA SENSITIVITY CURVE (unpublished elsewhere). DEV-20, flags ON, association frozen; mean induced pitch displacement -> GS-HOTA loss. Camera pan/tilt jitter: 0.049 m -> 0.034, 0.098 -> 0.121, 0.244 -> 0.647, 0.487 -> 2.225, 0.973 -> 6.739, 2.616 -> 19.642. Focal jitter: 0.012 -> 0.003, 0.029 -> 0.015, 0.058 -> 0.055, 0.117 -> 0.195, 0.233 -> 0.718. iid per-row Gaussian: 0.125 -> 0.133, 0.313 -> 0.849, 0.627 -> 3.485, 1.253 -> 12.309, 2.507 -> 30.690, 3.760 -> 41.405, 6.267 -> 49.481. The loss is QUADRATIC in mean error near zero (loss / err^2 runs 11-16 over 0-0.25 m and falls as saturation sets in). DIRECT ANSWER TO 'when does calibration stop mattering under the 5 m kernel': only below ~0.20 m MEAN pitch displacement (~0.13 m median), where the cost falls under 0.5 GS-HOTA. Our shipped camera sits at 0.76 m mean / 0.48 m median -- an order of magnitude inside the regime where geometry pays.
claims.unit: metres of mean pitch-position error below which the GS-HOTA cost is < 0.5 (DEV-20, flags ON)
claims.method: tools.gsr_v10_w4 --curve families F1 (iid row Gaussian), F2 (per-frame Gaussian), F3 (per-frame pan/tilt jitter through generator.camera_track), F4 (per-frame log-focal jitter), F5 (dead-run simulation), seed 20260816; the threshold is a log-log interpolation between the bracketing measured levels of F3 (0.214 m) and F4 (0.188 m).
caveats: Association is held fixed, so this is the METRIC's response: a lower bound on the end-to-end cost of the same error injected upstream.
Perturbed rows are not re-gated; the shipped chain would NaN a coordinate that lands off the pitch, so the large-sigma end is slightly pessimistic.

F1 vs F2 agree to < 0.05 GS-HOTA at every level: GS-HOTA charges ABSOLUTE position and has no notion of the relative geometry a frame-correlated (camera) error preserves. Camera error and detection error cost the same per metre.
Bit-reproducible: the F1 ladder is identical to 4 dp across two independent runs.

claims.statement: OUR DEAD-FRAME TAIL IS SMALL AND NOW PRICED: 474 of 14,919 DEV-20 frames (3.18%) get no camera from the per-frame solver + gate, 216 (1.45%) survive fill_calibration_gaps(10) with no position at all, and 3,198 person-rows carry an image point but no pitch coordinate (1,512 on dead frames, 1,686 on live frames). Projecting all of them through a GT camera is worth +0.4913 GS-HOTA; repairing the geometry of the 7,672 rows the fill wrote is worth +0.4816. The whole tail is ~1.0 of the +6.82 the axis holds -- 85% of the headroom is the median accuracy of ordinary SOLVED frames. Of the 216 post-fill dead frames, 95 already carry a PnLCalib hypothesis with >= 4 ground correspondences (killed by the metre gate / on-pitch plausibility, not by missing evidence), and only 24 are central-view frames (centre circle in view, no penalty box) -- the population arXiv:2504.20052's circle->line conversion targets, i.e. 0.16% of frames.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA from perfect completeness alone, DEV-20 flags ON (2,893 rows added)
claims.method: tools.gsr_v10_w4 --anatomy (census + per-dead-frame landmark visibility from that frame's GT-fitted camera) and --curve arms O_comp / O_fill.
caveats: The 121 dead frames with NO cached hypothesis have < 4 correspondences by construction (PnLCalib emits nothing below that) and the cache does not record how many keypoints they had; the exact '2 or 3 correspondences, solvable under a tripod prior' count needs a GPU re-detect that was NOT run, because O_comp already caps the entire prize at +0.49.
The completeness oracle inherits each lost row's identity from its own ByteTrack track's surviving submission rows; rows whose track never survives anywhere are skipped, not invented.

claims.statement: REGISTERED RUNG-1 RESULT: RTS SMOOTHING IN CAMERA-PARAMETER SPACE FAILS, AND FAILS HARD. Both registered arms lose on DEV-20 flags ON against the same-lineage control (55.0660): arm A (smooth all frames) 49.2941, paired -5.6834, helped 2 / hurt 18, p = 3.6e-05; arm B (smoother prediction on dead frames only) 54.6543, paired -0.4322, 6/9, p = 0.078. The mechanism is measured, not guessed: our per-frame solves ARE exactly decomposable into [pan, tilt, roll, log f, log aspect, C] (round trip < 5 cm on 93% of solved frames, once the non-square pixel aspect fy/fx ~ 0.94-0.97 that PnLCalib's calibrateCamera leaves free is modelled), but the decomposition is DEGENERATE: the estimated camera position carries 1.2-2.6 m of frame-to-frame measurement noise that trades off against focal length, so smoothing the parameters independently destroys the image->pitch map -- GT-anchored median error 0.4779 -> 0.6801 m (+42%), 115,503 rows worse vs 63,077 better. Extrapolating those parameters into dead runs is worse still: median 3.83 m, mean 78.8 m, 55% within 5 m, against the shipped linear fill's 2.06 m / 73%.
claims.unit: paired GS-HOTA vs same-lineage control, DEV-20 flags ON (registered arm A)
claims.method: generator.camera_track (decompose / RTS / compose; measurement and process noise estimated from each series' second differences, per-frame measurement weight from the solver's metre residual, 2 m grid clamp) via tools.gsr_v10_w4 --smooth --accuracy --score; the frozen v6 chain per arm, tools.gsr_v9_w7.score_pair flags ON and OFF.
caveats: The 2 m clamp fired on 2,330 of 13,538 parameterised frames -- the smoothed camera disagreed with its own frame's solve by more than the 2024-winner guard on 17% of frames; without the clamp the arms would be worse still.
This is a negative about the PARAMETERISATION, not about temporal modelling as such: see v10-w4-005.

claims.statement: TEMPORAL SMOOTHING WORKS ONLY IN MAPPING SPACE, AND IS WORTH ABOUT +0.53 -- 8% OF THE GEOMETRY HEADROOM. Running the identical RTS smoother over the pitch coordinates of a fixed 3x3 image grid (homography re-fitted by DLT) instead of over camera parameters improves GT-anchored accuracy (median 0.4779 -> 0.4543 m, -4.9%; p90 1.463 -> 1.395; 105,353 rows better vs 91,895 worse) and scores, on DEV-20 flags ON: arm E (solved frames smoothed, fill untouched) 55.6036 = +0.5375 combined, paired +0.5273, helped 15 / hurt 5, Wilcoxon p = 0.0296, GS-DetA +0.3312, GS-LocA 93.1805 -> 93.5044; arm D (also replacing the fill) +0.4935, 14/6, p = 0.083. This is the DEV-20 confirmation that v10-w3-006's exploratory probe-10 +0.4251 (p = 0.131) asked for, at the same sign and magnitude.
claims.unit: paired GS-HOTA vs same-lineage control, DEV-20 flags ON (arm E, mapping-space RTS)
claims.method: generator.camera_track.smooth_homographies(mode='mapping') via tools.gsr_v10_w4 --smooth --score, arms D and E; same chain, same control, same window as arms A/B.
caveats: POST-REGISTRATION ARM. The registered probe was camera-parameter space (arms A/B). The mapping parameterisation was added after the camera series was found degenerate and was selected on the GT-ANCHORED ACCURACY instrument -- which it passes at v10-W2's own escalation bar (-4.9% median vs a 3% bar, p ~ 0, more rows better than worse) -- BEFORE any end-to-end score was read. It is still not pre-registered, and it clears the +0.50 bar by 0.03. CANDIDATE, not a ship: it needs its own registration and a same-window TEST-38 confirmation.
Two arms (D, E) were scored, so +0.5375 is the better of two.
8% of the +6.82 the geometry axis holds: temporal consistency is real but small, and it does not change where the money is.

claims.statement: LADDER DECISION: THE CAMERA-INNOVATION MAP'S PREMISE IS INVERTED. The map argued that the 5 m kernel puts our 0.43-0.48 m median past the bottleneck and that the remaining edge is completeness + tail behaviour. Measured on one lineage, one window, one control: the kernel is Gaussian; the median IS the bottleneck (+6.25 of the +6.82 total headroom is per-frame accuracy on frames we already solve); completeness is worth +0.49; the fill is worth +0.48; and the registered temporal probe returns -5.68 in its registered form and +0.53 in its best post-hoc form. The Rung-1 decision rule ('< +0.5 -> temporal camera modelling is non-bottleneck') therefore FIRES: temporal modelling is not the lever. Rung 2 (tripod clip solver) is justified only insofar as a tripod prior makes the per-frame solve MORE ACCURATE -- its advertised prize, 100% completeness, is capped at +0.49 -- and Rung 3 (offline bundle adjustment) is justified because a batch solve attacks the +6.25 accuracy term, the only large number on this axis.
claims.unit: GS-HOTA in the per-frame-accuracy term vs 0.49 completeness + 0.53 temporal (DEV-20, flags ON)
claims.method: Synthesis of v10-w4-001..005 on one lineage, one window, one control.
caveats: The +6.25 is an oracle ceiling, not a reachable target: it is what a camera fitted to the frame's own ground truth achieves. What a tripod-constrained or bundle-adjusted solve can actually recover of it is UNMEASURED -- that is the next probe, and it is now the only geometry question worth GPU time.

v10-W3's independent result constrains the space and is consistent: a full camera-model replacement (BroadTrack) reads 1.00 m against our 0.40 m and loses 7.39 GS-HOTA inside our chain, so the accuracy term has to be attacked from OUR per-frame solver, not by swapping the model class.
